articles.headline: Cacoal é o primeiro município de Rondônia a receber tecnologia com drones para combater a dengue
articles.headlineTranslated: Cacoal is the first municipality in Rondônia to receive drone technology to combat dengue.
articles.summary: Cacoal in Rondônia, Brazil becomes the first municipality in the state to receive drone-based technology to fight dengue. The Techdengue program uses drones with high-resolution cameras to map urban areas, identifying standing-water hotspots—the main breeding grounds for Aedes aegypti and the arboviruses dengue, Zika, and chikungunya. Images are processed by AI and converted into risk maps that guide field teams, enabling targeted interventions where problems are most likely to arise. The approach allows precise larviciding at identified sites with 100% organic, biodegradable larvicide, reducing broad, inefficient actions. Techdengue already supports over 630 Brazilian municipalities, reaching around 13 million people. Preventive, data-driven action lowers costs: for each R$1 invested, up to R$28.60 can be saved in public health costs by avoiding hospitalizations and illnesses.

articles.headline: Bactéria resistente a antibióticos sai de hospitais e circula em São Paulo
articles.headlineTranslated: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria leave hospitals and circulate in São Paulo.
articles.summary: MRSA (Staphylococcus aureus resistant to methicillin) is circulating beyond hospitals into the São Paulo metropolitan area, Brazil. A study by Associação Fundo de Incentivo à Pesquisa in partnership with Escola Paulista de Medicina at UNIFESP analyzed 51,532 S. aureus cases from 2011–2021 and found a shift from hospital-linked infections to community-origin cases, with results published February 19, 2026 in an Oxford University Press journal. Hospital MRSA cases declined on average 2.48% per year, while community-associated infections rose by 3.61% annually. MRSA accounted for 42.6% of active infections and 37.4% of colonized individuals. Highest burden occurred in children under 3 and adults 65+. A community-associated MRSA subtype sensitive to clindamycin increased at 8.77% per year. Data from over 600 health units mapped regions with community MRSA rates above 20%, signaling a need for broader public-health strategies and antibiotic stewardship.

articles.headline: Fortaleza antecipa campanha de vacinação contra a Influenza
articles.headlineTranslated: Fortaleza advances influenza vaccination campaign.
articles.summary: Influenza vaccination campaign pushes forward in Fortaleza, Ceará, Brazil, starting Friday, March 20, 2026. The initiative follows a period when back-to-school, post-carnival, and rainy-season conditions have boosted influenza-like illness (ILI) and severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARI). Ceará’s Central Public Health Laboratory reports that from February 2025 to 2026, nearly half of tested samples were positive, with over 11,000 ILI cases recorded and related activity from respiratory viruses including influenza. In Fortaleza, 134 health posts will vaccinate priority groups (children 6 months to under 6 years, elderly, pregnant women, health workers, teachers, and those with comorbidities); on the 21st–22nd, 16 additional vaccination points will operate. The city had received more than 220,000 vaccine doses, with an expectation to vaccinate about 1 million people this year. Nationally, Butantan delivered about 7 million doses to the Health Ministry, and 63 million more are to be delivered by May. Regions: Northeast, Central-West, South, and Southeast run March 28–May 30; the North region vaccinates later due to Amazon winter. Common respiratory viruses typically cause mild symptoms (fever, cough, sneezing), but dyspnea, rapid breathing, chest tightness, persistent fever, drowsiness, and dehydration warrant medical care and can progress to pneumonia.

articles.headline: Prefeitura de Três Lagoas reforça ações de combate à dengue em reunião do Comitê - Perfil News
articles.headlineTranslated: Três Lagoas City Hall reinforces dengue control actions in a committee meeting - Perfil News.
articles.summary: March 19, 2026 — Três Lagoas City Hall, through the Municipal Health Secretariat, convened another meeting of the Municipal Committee for Mobilization and Combat of Aedes aegypti to align strategies and strengthen dengue and arbovirus prevention in the municipality. Updated epidemiological data were presented and are continuously monitored by Health Surveillance teams. Actions across Endemias, Epidemiological Surveillance, Immunization, Entomology, and Health Promotion were detailed, including home visits, chemical barriers, monitoring of strategic points, application of biolarvicides, removal of unusable materials, and mass cleaning drives across regions. Educational activities such as lectures, blitz campaigns, and school programs aim to raise awareness. The administration emphasizes that combatting the Aedes aegypti is a shared responsibility; residents are urged to eliminate water-filled containers to reduce breeding sites and interrupt transmission of dengue and other arboviruses.

articles.headline: Novo drone de combate ao mosquito da dengue alcança locais de difícil acesso
articles.headlineTranslated: New drone to combat the dengue mosquito reaches hard-to-access locations.
articles.summary: New drone deployed in Santos, Brazil, to combat Aedes aegypti dengue vectors, enabling access to hard-to-reach locations and depositing larvicide and insecticide. The drone, operated by the city’s Health Department, supports the Municipal Health Secretariat teams with a 10–15 minute battery life and a 10-liter reservoir for larvicide/insecticide. In 2026, Santos recorded 144 dengue cases and eight chikungunya cases. Across seven community outreach campaigns, 582 mosquito larval habitats were eliminated, while agents were refused entry to 644 properties. The device aims to target hidden breeding sites and supplement traditional vector-control efforts. No information on laboratory confirmation or infection sources is provided in the article. This initiative reflects ongoing dengue activity in Santos and highlights rapid, field-deployable vector-control technology to curb transmission.

articles.headline: Saúde de Guarulhos reforça a importância da segunda dose contra a dengue entre adolescentes - Click Guarulhos
articles.headlineTranslated: Guarulhos Health Department Reinforces the Importance of the Second Dengue Vaccine Dose Among Adolescents - Click Guarulhos
articles.summary: Guarulhos, Brazil, reports progress in dengue vaccination, emphasizing a second dose for adolescents 11–14 years old. Data presented by the Health Secretariat at the monthly Arboviruses Commission show 10-year-olds surpassing the first-dose target at 140% coverage, with 51.8% having already received the second dose. Among 11-year-olds, 72.6% have had the first dose and 54.1% completed the schedule. For 12–14-year-olds, first-dose coverage ranges from 49.7% to 51.7%, while second-dose coverage is 30.1%–34.6%. Guarulhos reports 74 confirmed dengue cases. The goal is at least 90% vaccination coverage across all target ages. Parents are advised to verify vaccination cards and bring 10–14-year-olds to a Basic Health Unit to start or complete the schedule. The dengue vaccine is described as safe and effective, reducing severe disease and hospitalizations and helping safeguard the public health system.

articles.headline: Campinas confirma mais duas mortes por febre maculosa registradas em 2025
articles.headlineTranslated: Campinas Confirms Two More Deaths from Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever Recorded in 2025.
articles.summary: Campinas, Brazil – The Health Secretariat confirms two additional Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever (febre maculosa) deaths from 2025, bringing that year’s total to six with 100% fatality; no 2026 cases have been recorded as of 19 March 2026. The latest fatalities: a 63-year-old woman in the Santa Bárbara health-center area (symptoms began Oct 3, 2025; death Oct 11) with probable home-based infection in a transmission area; and a 46-year-old man in the Nova América area (symptoms Oct 29; death Nov 3) with undetermined infection source. Previously confirmed cases include residents around Campinas’ Aeroporto and Jardim Guanabara centers and a Curitiba visitor, with infections linked to fishing areas, private rural land in Sousas near Rio Atibaia, and a lagoon area after horse riding. Symptoms include fever, severe headache, nausea/vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, myalgia, edema with redness on palms/soles, possible gangrene or paralysis. Incubation is 2–14 days. Prevention emphasizes tick avoidance, protective clothing, repellents, and careful tick removal.

articles.headline: Novo drone é capaz de lançar larvicida em focos de dengue em Santos; entenda
articles.headlineTranslated: New drone capable of releasing larvicide at dengue hotspots in Santos; find out how.
articles.summary: New drone to fight Aedes aegypti in Santos, São Paulo, Brazil, reaches hard-to-access sites, releasing larvicide and insecticide to eliminate dengue and chikungunya foci. Acquired by the City Health Department for R$150,000, the device has a 10-liter reservoir and 10–15 minute battery life. It enhances site visualization and allows immediate deposition of larvicide or insecticide, reducing the mosquitoes' life cycle and preventing adult mosquitoes from transmitting viruses. First operations occurred at Paquetá Cemetery and on the roof of an abandoned building with standing water, signaling the end of training and the permanent deployment of the technology; weekly inspections continue. In 2026, Santos logged 144 dengue and eight chikungunya cases. Across seven mutirões, 582 larval breeding sites were eliminated, and agents faced 644 entry refusals.

articles.headline: São Carlos realiza 2º Encontro Interprofissional para o Enfrentamento da Tuberculose
articles.headlineTranslated: São Carlos Holds the 2nd Interprofessional Meeting to Address Tuberculosis.
articles.summary: São Carlos, Brazil — On 19 March 2026, the 2nd Interprofessional Meeting to Address Tuberculosis was held at the Museu da Ciência, organized by the Municipal Health Secretariat via the Center for Chronic Infections (Caic). The event gathered health professionals, researchers and managers to discuss TB diagnosis, treatment and prevention. Caic director Cíntia Martins Ruggiero reported 45 patients under care and 16 new TB cases this year. Ricardo Arcêncio, professor at USP Ribeirão Preto and president of the Rede Brasileira de Pesquisa em Tuberculose, noted TB is neglected, with Brazil 19th worldwide in cases; São Paulo state concentrates many, with interior cities like São Carlos prioritized. He stressed treatments have changed little in 40 years and called for stronger professional training, active case finding, and clear information. Any SUS unit can diagnose and provide free TB treatment. Symptoms include persistent cough >2 weeks, weight loss, and loss of appetite.

articles.headline: Existe diferença entre gripe comum e H1N1? Entenda
articles.headlineTranslated: Is there a difference between seasonal influenza and H1N1? Find out.
articles.summary: On 19 March 2026, western São Paulo school suspended a class after a rise in H1N1 cases to curb transmission. H1N1 is a subtype of influenza A; seasonal flu is caused by influenza A and B. Since 2009, vaccines and antivirals reduce severe outcomes, though disease remains possible. Symptoms include fever, cough, body aches, headache, sore throat, and runny nose; in children, nausea and vomiting. High-risk groups include pregnant individuals, older adults, immunocompromised, and those with chronic diseases such as obesity, heart disease, diabetes, or asthma. Complications can include pneumonia, sinusitis, otitis, or worsening of conditions. Vaccination is the most effective prevention; vaccines are updated annually. SUS offers free vaccination for priority groups; others are available in pharmacies from around R$80. Preventive measures: avoid crowds, ventilate spaces, hand hygiene, avoid touching mucous membranes, do not share utensils, wear a mask if symptomatic, seek care within 48 hours if at risk.

articles.headline: MS tem escalada de casos de Chikungunya anos após epidemia no Paraguai
articles.headlineTranslated: Ministry of Health reports a surge in chikungunya cases years after the outbreak in Paraguay.
articles.summary: Chikungunya outbreaks intensify in Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, linked to border with Paraguay where PAHO records about 138,700 infections in 2023. In MS, 2022 had 237 confirmed cases, rising to a peak in 2023 with about 7,600 infections and 17 deaths. 2024 saw 919 cases, with 11 municipalities at high incidence and 23 at moderate levels. By week 9 of 2026, 1,100 cases had been confirmed, with four deaths, all Indigenous residents of Jaguapiru and Bororó in Dourados. The disease spread from Indigenous villages to urban areas; emergency declarations are being considered. No vaccine exists; control hinges on reducing Aedes aegypti breeding sites, requiring community participation, especially where water storage in tanks is common due to lacking infrastructure. The FN-SUS is aiding via tripartite ambulatory support for Indigenous communities.

articles.headline: Novo vírus? Surto gastrointestinal fecha escolas no RS e situação com crianças preocupa
articles.headlineTranslated: New virus? Gastrointestinal outbreak closes schools in Rio Grande do Sul, and the situation with children is worrying.
articles.summary: Norovirus suspected in a gastrointestinal outbreak prompting the temporary suspension of classes across Pelotas' municipal schools in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. About 60 students from eight schools have reported symptoms, including vomiting, diarrhea and abdominal pain, with rapid spread among younger children. Classes will remain suspended for several days, with reopening anticipated on Monday, March 23, 2026. During this period, all campuses undergo comprehensive cleaning using virus-elimination products, requiring the absence of students and staff. Health authorities have collected samples to confirm the causative agent, and parents are advised to keep children with symptoms at home. The incident highlights the high transmissibility of norovirus in school settings and the need for basic infection-control measures while awaiting laboratory confirmation.

articles.headline: Existe diferença entre gripe comum e H1N1? Entenda
articles.headlineTranslated: Is there a difference between seasonal flu and H1N1? Find out.
articles.summary: In São Paulo's western zone, an elementary school suspended a class on Thursday, March 19, after detecting H1N1 cases among students to curb spread. H1N1 is influenza A subtype and tends to be more severe in children, pregnant people, elderly, and immunocompromised individuals. Symptoms align with seasonal flu and include fever, cough, body aches, headache, sore throat, nasal congestion, malaise, and chills; in children, nausea and vomiting can occur. Illness generally lasts three to seven days. At-risk groups face higher risks of hospitalization from viral or bacterial pneumonia, sinusitis, otitis, or worsening of underlying conditions such as obesity, heart disease, diabetes, or asthma. Most recover at home, but at-risk individuals should seek care within 48 hours of onset. Vaccination is the most effective prevention; the SUS provides free vaccine for priority groups and, when doses remain, to all; private clinics offer shots from about R$80. Additional preventive measures exist.

articles.headline: Vereadores pedem doações para indígenas atingidos por epidemia de chikungunya em Dourados
articles.headlineTranslated: Councilors request donations for indigenous people affected by Chikungunya epidemic in Dourados
articles.summary: Chikungunya epidemic in Dourados Municipality prompts emergency aid for the Dourados Indigenous Reserve (Jaguapiru and Bororó). A total of 407 chikungunya cases have been notified in the reserve: 202 confirmed, 181 under investigation, and 24 discarded. The Committee to Support the Dourados Indigenous Reserve launched an emergency drive to collect water, isotonic drinks, repellents, and ready-to-eat foods (fruits and crackers) for affected families. The initiative was approved in a Dourados City Council meeting on Thursday, with participation from councilors, the Rotary Club, professional associations, and civil society to mount a rapid sanitary response. Donations can be delivered at the City Council headquarters at Shopping Avenida Center (07:00–13:00) and at OAB Dourados/Itaporã. The Indigenous Reserve comprises Jaguapiru and Bororó and shelters more than 15,000 people, the country’s largest urban indigenous reserve.

articles.headline: Mpox: Manhuaçu tem o primeiro caso confirmado
articles.headlineTranslated: Mpox: Manhuaçu has the first confirmed case.
articles.summary: Mpox (monkeypox) in Minas Gerais, Brazil: Manhuaçu confirms its first case on March 19, 2026. The SES-MG reports 17 confirmed mpox cases statewide in 2026, all among men aged 25–56, with full recovery in every patient. Belo Horizonte accounts for 11 cases, Contagem 3, Formiga 1, and Ribeirão das Neves 1; Manhuaçu’s case is the sole municipality record this year. A second suspected case in Governador Valadares was ruled out. Transmission is via direct contact with skin lesions, body fluids, or contaminated objects; symptoms include fever, headache, muscle pain, lymphadenopathy, and skin lesions. Treatment is supportive; no specific antiviral exists. Vaccination targets high-risk groups, including immunosuppressed individuals (especially those with HIV/AIDS), laboratory workers, and close contacts. Suspected cases should seek a basic health unit and isolate during transmissible periods, with emphasis on hand hygiene.

articles.headline: Diante de avanço da chikungunya, Câmara articula ajuda emergencial à Reserva Indígena - O PROGRESSO
articles.headlineTranslated: In light of the chikungunya outbreak, the Chamber of Deputies coordinates emergency aid to the Indigenous Reserve - O PROGRESSO.
articles.summary: Chikungunya outbreak prompts emergency aid in Dourados, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, with the City Council forming the RID Support Committee and launching a fundraising drive to assist families affected in the Indigenous Reserve of Dourados (Jaguapiru and Bororó). Four deaths are reported; 407 cases notified in the reserve, including 202 confirmed, 181 under investigation, and 24 discarded, per Health Surveillance using Ministry of Health data. The reserve houses over 15,000 people and is the country’s largest urban Indigenous reserve, with many lacking access to water, hydration, repellents, and ready-to-eat foods, worsening clinical outcomes. Donations are accepted at City Hall (Shopping Avenida Center) from 7:00 to 13:00, and at OAB Dourados/Itaporã. The effort stresses community participation and a rapid, coordinated response to mitigate the outbreak’s impact on vulnerable indigenous communities.

articles.headline: Prefeitura coleta carrapatos para análise após morte por febre maculosa no ES - ES HOJE
articles.headlineTranslated: City Hall collects ticks for analysis after death from Brazilian spotted fever in ES - ES Hoje
articles.summary: Boa Esperança, a city in northern Espírito Santo, Brazil, collected ticks for analysis after confirming the death of a child from Brazilian spotted fever (febre maculosa) in January 2026; laboratory confirmation was issued only recently by LACEN/ES. The infection source remains uncertain as the child had been in another municipality before symptoms. Preventively, health teams collected ticks at multiple city sites; samples were sent for testing, but no conclusive result yet. Brazilian spotted fever is transmitted mainly by the star tick, with capybaras as a key host; the disease can progress rapidly and requires early diagnosis and treatment. The city is coordinating with the Espírito Santo State Health Secretariat to strengthen surveillance, monitoring, and public guidance. Residents are advised to seek medical care if fever, body pains, and skin rashes appear.

articles.headline: Secretaria de Boa Esperança coleta carrapatos após morte de criança por febre maculosa
articles.headlineTranslated: Boa Esperança Health Department collects ticks after the death of a child from Rocky Mountain spotted fever.
articles.summary: Two-year-old Kyara Silva Rubia died from Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever in Boa Esperança, northern Espírito Santo, after about a week of symptoms and three hospital transfers; death confirmed by LACEN/ES. The case is under epidemiological investigation because the child had been in another municipality before symptom onset, leaving the infection site unidentified. Tick samples collected in Boa Esperança have been sent for laboratory analysis, with results not yet available. The rural home about 6 km from the municipal center, where capybaras were observed, may indicate exposure to the star tick (carrapato-estrela), the disease vector. The girl was treated in Boa Esperança, Nova Venécia, São Mateus, and Vitória before dying in January. SESA is supporting surveillance; residents are advised to seek care promptly if fever, body aches and skin rashes appear.

articles.headline: Em meio a alerta na Zona da Mata, BH concentra maioria dos casos de leptospirose e tem 3 mortes
articles.headlineTranslated: Amid an alert in Zona da Mata, Belo Horizonte accounts for the majority of leptospirosis cases and has three deaths.
articles.summary: Leptospirosis outbreak alerts in Minas Gerais, Brazil, driven by floods in Zona da Mata. Belo Horizonte accounts for the majority of notifications, with 7 confirmed cases and 3 deaths as of March 17. Statewide totals reach 38 confirmed cases and 6 deaths. In the Zona da Mata, Ubá reports 2 confirmed cases and 1 death (a 33-year-old woman on March 10); Juiz de Fora has 4 confirmed cases; Matias Barbosa 1 case. Leptospirosis is transmitted via water or mud contaminated with urine from infected rats (Leptospira), typically affecting people with skin abrasions. Symptoms include fever, body aches, headache, nausea, malaise; severe cases may involve high fever, vomiting, breathing difficulty. Authorities urge caution during cleanup after floods; PPE recommended. The Minas Gerais government, declaring a disaster in Zona da Mata, advanced ~R$48.2 million to boost health services in Juiz de Fora, Ubá and Matias Barbosa, following a Feb 24 epidemiological alert.

articles.headline: Prefeitura de Londrina realiza mutirão contra a dengue no Jardim Eldorado neste fim de semana
articles.headlineTranslated: Londrina City Hall conducts a dengue-control blitz in Jardim Eldorado this weekend.
articles.summary: Londrina's Municipal Health Secretariat will conduct a dengue-control blitz in Jardim Eldorado on March 20-21, mobilizing about 50 agents for door-to-door visits from 8:00 to 16:00 to identify Aedes aegypti breeding sites and educate residents on proper disposal of water-holding materials. A drone will survey rooftops and gutters to locate hard-to-reach larval habitats. Green disposal bags will be distributed for safe disposal of containers and other unused objects. Trucks from CMTU and the Agriculture Secretariat will collect only items that could serve as mosquito breeding sites, excluding construction debris, furniture, pruning waste, or regular household waste. The operation depends on weather and will be canceled if it rains to preserve insecticide efficacy and agent safety. Community participation is essential; residents should place disposal items on the sidewalk according to the truck schedule.

articles.headline: Infectologista explica sintomas e transmissão da Mpox após primeiro caso confirmado na fronteira do Acre - O Alto Acre
articles.headlineTranslated: Infectious disease specialist explains symptoms and transmission of Mpox after first confirmed case at the Acre border - O Alto Acre
articles.summary: Monkeypox (Mpox) case confirmed at the Acre border in Brazil, near Alto Acre. Infectious disease specialist Thor Dantas explains Mpox is a viral infection caused by a smallpox-like virus, producing skin lesions such as blisters and vesicles, similar to chickenpox. Transmission is mainly by contact, with sexual contact being highly efficient; it can also spread through direct contact with skin lesions, contaminated objects, and, less commonly, respiratory routes. The disease is generally benign and rarely life-threatening, though genital or anal involvement can cause pain during defecation and substantial discomfort. Public health messaging emphasizes clear communication to avoid unnecessary anxiety. Large-scale outbreaks are unlikely because Mpox does not sustain efficient airborne transmission; unlike respiratory viruses, it requires person-to-person contact for spread. This article underscores the need for awareness around symptoms and transmission.

articles.headline: Worldwide Approaches to Safeguard Seals and Sea Lions from Avian Influenza
articles.summary: H5N1 avian influenza has devastated pinnipeds worldwide. Since its 1996 emergence on an Asian poultry farm, the virus has reached every continent except Oceania, affecting hundreds of millions of poultry and spilling into wild mammals. In South America, outbreaks in Peru, Chile, Brazil, Uruguay, and Argentina have killed more than 36,000 South American sea lions, 17,400 southern elephant seals, and about 1,000 South American fur seals. A severe 2023 event in Argentina highlighted pinniped risks. In February 2026, northern elephant seals along the California coast marked the first marine-mammal case in the state, detected through proactive UC Davis–led surveillance with the Año Nuevo Reserve and UC Santa Cruz collaborators. The study calls for sustained wildlife health surveillance, interagency coordination, and integrating public health and social science, plus non-invasive monitoring (auditory/thermal imaging, satellite data). It urges international cooperation to address habitat loss, agricultural intensification, global trade, and climate-related stressors.

articles.headline: Paraná reforça vigilância contra gripe aviária com operação no Litoral
articles.headlineTranslated: Paraná strengthens avian influenza surveillance with operation along the coast.
articles.summary: Avian influenza of high pathogenicity (IAAP) surveillance expanded along Paraná's coast in seven municipalities: Pontal do Paraná, Paranaguá, Guaratuba, Matinhos, Morretes, Antonina and Guaraqueçaba. Initiated March 17, 2026, through March 27, 2026. Led by Adapar's Avian Health Division with 16 staff and veterinarians from the Santos Basin Beach Monitoring Project (PMP-BS) under Petrobras licensing conditions with Ibama; executed by UFPR's Ecology and Conservation Laboratory. Preventive, risk-based action complements routine health inspections, guidance on IAAP and Newcastle Disease, and sanitation education for backyard poultry. On day one, PMP-BS assisted with simulations and necropsies to detect signs of disease. Paraná had 13 wild-bird IAAP foci in 2023; currently no suspected cases. Officials emphasize One Health and safeguarding Paraná’s status as Brazil’s largest animal-protein producer and a leading chicken-meat producer, protecting public health, economy, and food security.

articles.headline: Força Nacional reforça monitoramento para frear epidemia de chikungunya em Dourados
articles.headlineTranslated: National Force Strengthens Monitoring to Curb Chikungunya Epidemic in Dourados
articles.summary: Chikungunya outbreak in Dourados, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil intensifies with four deaths and hundreds of cases, primarily in Jaguapiru and Bororó Indigenous villages. On March 18, the National Force of the SUS (FN-SUS) deployed 20 health professionals, logistics, active case finding, home spraying, and expanded care to assist indigenous health services. A field hospital was opened March 17 at the Tengatui Marangatu Indigenous School in Jaguapiru, treating about 80 patients on day one. Epidemiological bulletin: Indigenous Reserve of Dourados presents 407 cases notified, 202 confirmed, 181 under investigation, 24 discarded, 4 deaths (all Jaguapiru). Urban area reports 912 notifications, 379 confirmed, no deaths. Actions include 4,319 properties inspected, 2,173 treated, 1,004 mosquito breeding sites identified (90% in water tanks, trash, tires), 43 properties sprayed; 86 endemic agents and 29 Indigenous health agents deployed. Some Jaguapiru schools suspended classes, though authorities say no official closure; emphasis on eliminating standing water. Dengue vaccine coverage reported at 100%.

articles.headline: Tres fallecidos y 841 casos de contagios a nivel nacional por leptospirosis: "Una enfermedad cíclica"
articles.headlineTranslated: Three deaths and 841 nationwide cases of leptospirosis: "A cyclical disease"
articles.summary: Leptospirosis (Leptospira) in Peru has caused three deaths in Piura, San Martín, and Tumbes and 841 cases through week 9 of 2026 (Mar 1–7), with 505 probable and 336 confirmed. Regions with the highest incidence include Loreto, Madre de Dios, Tumbes, Ucayali, San Martín, Amazonas, Ayacucho, Huánuco, and Cusco. Transmission remains zoonotic, mainly from water, soil, or food contaminated with urine from infected animals, particularly rats, which drive about 60% of cases. Early symptoms resemble flu; severe disease can cause liver damage, massive hemorrhages, and later jaundice. El Niño-related rains heighten contamination risk; in severe zoonotic zones like Iquitos, Madre de Dios, and Loreto, mortality may reach 50%. Minsa, with Diresa/Geresa, is strengthening laboratory diagnostics, surveillance, case analysis, and preventive education; experts say sanitation and health-service improvements are essential to halt this cyclical outbreak.

articles.headline: Dengue grave: entenda sintomas de alerta e tratamento do quadro do apresentador Felipeh Campos
articles.headlineTranslated: Severe dengue: understand warning signs and treatment for presenter Felipeh Campos's condition.
articles.summary: Felipeh Campos, a journalist and presenter, was admitted to Hospital Samaritano Higienópolis in São Paulo after a severe dengue episode; discharge date not yet announced and his condition is under medical monitoring. Severe dengue arises when the body's immune response leads to vascular leakage, hypotension, bleeding, and possible liver involvement. Common symptoms include high fever, headache, body aches, and malaise; warning signs include eye pain, skin rashes, severe abdominal pain, vomiting, bleeding, and low blood pressure, which can worsen as fever declines. The term dengue hemorrhagic is outdated (abandoned in 2009) to avoid the misconception that bleeding alone defines severity. Vulnerable groups include the elderly, infants and young children, pregnant women, and those with chronic diseases, though dengue can be dangerous in healthy individuals as well. Management is supportive: emphasis on hydration, rest, and safe fever control, with early recognition of warning signs being lifesaving.

articles.headline: Bactéria resistente a antibióticos deixa hospitais e passa a circular entre a população - Jornal Americanense
articles.headlineTranslated: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria leave hospitals and begin to circulate among the population - Jornal Americanense
articles.summary: MRSA (methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus) has left hospitals and is circulating in the community in São Paulo state, Brazil, per a study by AFIP and the Federal University of São Paulo (Unifesp). Hospital infections fell, while community infections rose, indicating a shift in transmission. Among active infections, MRSA prevalence reached 42.6%; among colonized individuals, 37.4%. The highest incidence is in children under 3 and seniors 65+, groups more vulnerable to complications. Public health implications include challenging control of community spread; emphasize hygiene, prudent antibiotic use, and prompt recognition of infection signs—non-healing wounds, pain, redness, and fever. The study underlines an expanded infection-control challenge as of 2026-03-19.

articles.headline: Boehringer Ingelheim reúne especialistas da suinocultura para debater sobre salmonelose | Agrimidia
articles.headlineTranslated: Boehringer Ingelheim gathers swine production specialists to discuss salmonellosis | Agrimidia
articles.summary: On 19 March 2026, Boehringer Ingelheim hosted the third edition of 'Salmonella Experts', convening swine-production specialists in Indaiatuba, São Paulo, to discuss control of salmonellosis in Brazilian pig farming. Embrapa Aves e Suínos researcher Jalusa Kich stressed systemic prevention across the production chain—from feed mill to slaughterhouse—to ensure food safety and reduce consumer risk. UFMG professor Roberto Guedes highlighted salmonellosis as a significant public health issue, advocating improved husbandry and biosafety to lower incidence and calling for ongoing training for technicians and producers. Indaiatuba was chosen for logistic convenience and São Paulo's importance in national pig production. Executives presented control solutions, including the Enterisol Salmonella T/C vaccine. Previous editions were in Toledo and Ouro Preto; Chapecó is planned next.

articles.headline: Do Nipah vírus à gripe aviária: há uma nova pandemia à vista? | Com a Palavra
articles.headlineTranslated: From Nipah virus to avian flu: is there a new pandemic on the horizon? | Com a Palavra
articles.summary: Nipah virus triggers a 2026 global alert: first identified in Malaysia in 1998, it spilled from fruit bats to pigs and then to humans, with outbreaks especially in India. It now shows potential direct bat-to-human transmission, with mortality reaching 75%, but limited human-to-human spread probably prevents a pandemic. The episode underscores wildlife–human interfaces as a source of dangerous pathogens. Avian influenza A(H5N1) looms as a pandemic threat if the virus gains sustained human transmission, particularly amid perceived gaps after recent declines in U.S. surveillance. Measles resurges as vaccination coverage falls: the United States faces its largest outbreak in decades; Bolivia is a neighboring hotspot, and measles has been the leading cause of death among children in Brazil. A highly globalized world enables rapid cross-border spread; without robust surveillance and vaccination, the next pandemic threat could arrive sooner than expected.

articles.headline: Fumacê percorre 6 bairros da Capital nesta quinta para conter avanço da dengue
articles.headlineTranslated: Fogging covers six neighborhoods in the capital on Thursday to curb the spread of dengue.
articles.summary: ULV fogging covers six neighborhoods in Campo Grande, Brazil, on Thursday, March 19, 2026, to curb dengue, Zika, and chikungunya. Santo Antônio, Sobrinho, Taveirópolis, Parati, Piratininga, and Guanandi are targeted, with fumacê operations from 16:00 to 22:00 by the Municipal Vector-Borne Endemics Control Management (GCEV) under the Municipal Health Secretariat (Sesau). The approach targets adult Aedes aegypti, especially females, the primary vectors of arboviruses. Fogging does not kill eggs or larvae, so home-based actions remain essential. Residents are advised to open doors and windows during the vehicle’s pass to help the insecticide reach resting spots, such as behind curtains and in shaded areas. Weather—rain, strong wind, or mist—can delay dispersal. While important, fogging is an emergency, complementary measure; effective control still starts with eliminating standing water inside homes, amid rising respiratory cases and health-system strain.

articles.headlineTranslated: Severe dengue: understand warning signs and treatment for the presenter Felipeh Campos's condition - Portal Nosso Dia
articles.summary: Felipeh Campos, a presenter, was hospitalized in São Paulo, Brazil (Hospital Samaritano Higienópolis) after developing a severe dengue episode. As of 2026-03-19, there is no discharge date. Severe dengue arises from a more intense immune reaction, potentially causing plasma leakage with hypotension, bleeding, and organ involvement (including the liver). Typical dengue symptoms include high fever, headache, body aches, and malaise; warning signs in severe cases include eye pain, skin rashes, severe abdominal pain, intense vomiting, bleeding, and low blood pressure, often worsening as fever subsides. Suspected dengue requires hospital evaluation and diagnostic testing. There is no specific antiviral treatment; management is supportive, emphasizing hydration (oral or intravenous), rest, and safe fever control since some antipyretics can increase bleeding risk. High-risk groups include the elderly, infants, pregnant women, and individuals with chronic diseases. Early recognition of warning signs and good hydration save lives; the term dengue hemorrhagic is outdated since 2009.

articles.headline: Raíssa Meritein morre após comer pizza contaminada
articles.headlineTranslated: Raíssa Meritein Dies After Eating Contaminated Pizza.
articles.summary: One death and over 100 suspected food-poisoning cases traced to a Pombal pizzeria in the Sertão of Paraíba, Brazil. A 44-year-old woman, Raíssa Meritein Bezerra e Silva, died after consuming a Sunday pizza reportedly topped with carne de sol in nata (sun-dried beef in cream). Investigations by the Civil Police and the Sanitary Surveillance agency include analyses of seized foods, pizza remnants, and toxicology tests on the deceased and the foods. Preliminary investigations indicate the meat was bought on Saturday and the nata prepared the same afternoon; staff who ate the pizza also developed symptoms within 10 minutes, arguing against intentional poisoning. The victim was treated at Regional Hospital of Pombal, rapidly progressed to ICU with signs of severe infection, and died on Tuesday. Forensic results will confirm whether ingredients were spoiled or contaminated, guiding outbreak assessment.

articles.headline: Deputada associa casos de chicungunya em aldeias de Dourados com demora na obra de abastecimento de água
articles.headlineTranslated: Deputy links chikungunya cases in the villages of Dourados to delays in the water supply project.
articles.summary: Chikungunya and dengue cases are rising in the Indigenous villages around Dourados, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, linked to delays in a long-planned water-supply project. State deputy Gleice Jane (PT) said that despite about R$54 million secured and funds in the state treasury, the works have not begun; earlier project missteps and pumps delivered were noted. She filed a formal request to Governor Eduardo Riedel, infrastructure secretary Guilherme Alcântara, and Sanesul's director-president for start dates and reasons for postponement, highlighting the impact on transmission. Absence of reliable taps or reservoirs forces residents to store water in containers; water-truck refills these containers, creating stagnant water that fosters Aedes aegypti breeding and sustains dengue and chikungunya in the Indigenous Reserve of Dourados.

articles.headline: Strategies to Shield Seals, Sea Lions From Bird Flu
articles.summary: H5N1 highly pathogenic avian influenza has severely affected pinnipeds, with outbreaks across Peru, Chile, Brazil, Uruguay and Argentina killing at least 36,000 South American sea lions, 17,400 southern elephant seals and 1,000 South American fur seals. A UC Davis study reviews global pinniped impacts and recommends monitoring, risk characterization, and resilience-building to curb spread and protect vulnerable species such as the Hawaiian monk seal and Galapagos sea lion. The paper, published in Philosophical Transactions B, highlights the 2023 southern elephant seal outbreak in Argentina as a warning, and notes the first HPAI H5N1 cases in northern elephant seals in California in late February, detected via year-long Bay Area surveillance at Año Nuevo. Key recommendations include sustained wildlife monitoring, cross‑sector coordination, routine surveillance in conservation work, and development of non-invasive tools (auditory and thermal imagery, satellites). Calls for policy changes and addressing other stressors like habitat loss and climate change.

articles.headlineTranslated: Caracol intensifies fight against dengue fever with preventive measures.
articles.summary: Caracol municipality's Health Department continues a continuous schedule of dengue prevention actions, focusing on controlling the Aedes aegypti mosquito. Preventive interventions include community guidance on protective measures, home visits, neighborhood inspections, and targeting areas with potential water accumulation. Health teams deploy nebulizers to apply mosquito-control products in high-risk zones. Beyond eliminating breeding sites, educational outreach to residents remains a priority to ensure awareness of dengue risks and prevention methods. Municipal authorities emphasize that population participation is essential, urging daily precautions such as sealing reservoirs and eliminating containers or sites where water can collect. The coordinated effort aims to reduce dengue transmission by combining vector control with public education and community cooperation.

articles.summary: Dengue in São José dos Campos, Brazil, marks the first death of 2026 in the city. The municipal panel shows 371 confirmed dengue cases and 1,604 under investigation as of March 19, 2026. The victim’s age or neighborhood were not disclosed due to Brazil's LGPD privacy law. In the wider Vale do Paraíba region, Jacareí reported the first dengue death of 2026 (a 63-year-old man with preexisting conditions; death Jan 27, confirmed Feb 4). São José dos Campos continues control efforts, including Operation Casa Limpa, ovitraps, drones, a dengue-control vehicle, and tablet use by Endemic Combat Agents. Residents can view the municipality’s dengue activity schedule online; suspected mosquito foci should be reported via Central 156 (phone, website, or app).

articles.headline: Peste 1.000 de cazuri de infecții gastrointestinale în Europa, legate de turiști reveniți din Cabo Verde - Money.ro
articles.headlineTranslated: Over 1,000 cases of gastrointestinal infections in Europe linked to travelers returning from Cabo Verde.
articles.summary: Over 1,000 confirmed or probable gastrointestinal infections linked to travelers returning from Cabo Verde to Europe, the United Kingdom, and the United States, as of March 2026. From September 2022 through March 2026, 766 shigellosis cases have been reported in 13 EU/EEA countries plus the UK and US, with over 300 additional GI infections (salmonellosis, campylobacteriosis, giardiasis, cryptosporidiosis, and pathogenic Escherichia coli). Geographically, cases involve Germany, France, Sweden, the Netherlands, Belgium, and others, indicating a cross-border outbreak. Most illnesses concern tourists who stayed in the same hotel chain in the Santa Maria region on Sal Island, Cabo Verde. No source has been identified; evidence points to contaminated food or water, though direct person-to-person spread cannot be excluded. Lab data show predominance of Shigella and Salmonella, with recurring similar strains implying a persistent exposure source since 2022. European authorities monitor with the WHO and Cabo Verde; recommendations emphasize strict hygiene, safe food and water, and travelers’ precautions.

articles.headline: Leptospirose na Zona da Mata: mais casos são confirmados, e governo agenda nova visita à região
articles.headlineTranslated: Leptospirosis in Zona da Mata: More cases confirmed, and the government schedules a new visit to the region.
articles.summary: Leptospirosis outbreak reported in Zona da Mata, Minas Gerais, Brazil, with two additional confirmed cases and one death (a 33-year-old woman) following exposure to floodwaters contaminated with rat urine. About 200 suspected cases are under investigation; Ubá alone accounts for 181 probable cases since the February 24 floods, a 132% rise from 78 reported on March 12. Laboratory confirmation is ongoing at Fundação Ezequiel Dias (FUNED) in Belo Horizonte. The regional health response includes actions to restore services and bolster surveillance. The Minas Gerais government has allocated about R$8.3 million to Ubá to strengthen health assistance, including new cold-storage for medicines and vaccines, and support for health facilities in Ubá, Matias Barbosa, and Juiz de Fora. Key symptoms to watch: fever, body pains, headache, nausea, malaise; seek care promptly and use protective gear when cleaning flood-affected areas. Severe cases require immediate hospital care. A new regional visit is scheduled for early April.

articles.summary: Sun-dried beef pizza with cream served at La Favoritta in Pombal, Paraíba, Brazil, is under investigation for a suspected foodborne outbreak. The Polícia Civil da Paraíba reports the majority of those ill—and the lone death—consumed this pizza flavor. The restaurant has been closed for 90 days; the Ministério Público opened a procedure to review sanitary conditions, with Agevisa involved. A total of 114 hospital attendances occurred from Sunday to Monday morning, with symptoms including diarrhea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. The deceased is Rayssa Maritein Bezerra, 44, a municipal civil servant who rapidly deteriorated and was admitted to the ICU after eating at the establishment. Investigators consider cross-contamination the leading hypothesis; deliberate poisoning is deemed unlikely since staff also fell ill. Lab results and site inspections are pending.

articles.headline: Sesau passa orientações sobre medidas para evitar a leptospirose
articles.headlineTranslated: Sesau issues guidance on measures to prevent leptospirosis.
articles.summary: Leptospirosis prevention guidance issued for Alagoas, Brazil, ahead of the rainy season. Leptospirosis is an acute febrile, waterborne infection caused by Leptospira, with rodents as primary reservoirs. Transmission occurs via direct or indirect contact with urine-contaminated water or objects; bacteria enter through skin wounds or mucous membranes. Preventive measures include avoiding contact with floodwater, sewage, and overflowing rivers; when exposure is unavoidable, wear gloves and boots; use treated water for drinking and cleaning foods. Foods should be washed with potable water; if needed, sodium hypochlorite is available at health posts. After mud or floodwater exposure, bathe and monitor for symptoms. Common signs: muscle pain (calves), fever, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, headache, conjunctival hemorrhage, photophobia, eye pain, cough; rash and hepatosplenomegaly are less common. Incubation 1–30 days (typically 7–14). In 2025, Alagoas recorded 30 cases and 8 deaths; 2026 shows one case with no deaths reported by February.

articles.headlineTranslated: Felipeh Campos is hospitalized in serious condition with dengue.
articles.summary: Felipeh Campos, Brazilian journalist and TV presenter, is hospitalized at Hospital Beneficência Portuguesa de São Paulo with a severe dengue infection. articles.headline: Caso Cardoso Fontes: investigação da SMS atesta que menina de 3 anos morreu por meningite
articles.headlineTranslated: Cardoso Fontes Case: Investigation by the SMS confirms that a 3-year-old girl died of meningitis.
articles.summary: A 3-year-old girl, Myrella Ramos de Souza, died in Rio de Janeiro from meningococcal meningitis. After presenting with fever, abdominal pain and nausea at Cardoso Fontes Hospital in Jacarepaguá (Zona Sudoeste) on Sunday 15, she was later intubated and died from cardiorespiratory arrest in the early hours of Monday 16. The Municipal Health Secretariat (SMS) confirms death due to meningococcal meningitis after autopsy at the Instituto Médico-Legal (IML) and subsequent analysis by Lacen-RJ. The disease is described as aggressive with high fatality risk and may lack clear early signs. The SMS is conducting epidemiological follow-up and contact tracing per protocol; family claims inadequate care, though SMS says two pediatricians attended with initial diarrheal syndrome and appropriate care given. The case is under investigation by the 41st Police Precinct (Tanque). Burial occurred on Wednesday 18 at Pechincha Cemetery.

articles.headline: 9ª Campanha Regional "Juntos Contra a Dengue" traz saldo positivo a Araraquara
articles.headlineTranslated: 9th Regional Campaign "Together Against Dengue" Brings Positive Results to Araraquara
articles.summary: Araraquara, Brazil, hosted the 9th Regional Campaign 'Juntos Contra a Dengue' to curb Aedes aegypti, the dengue, Zika, and chikungunya vector. Vector-control teams visited Jardim São Rafael II and other neighborhoods, removing breeding sites and educating residents. Outcomes: 1,380 properties worked; 402 potential breeding sites eliminated; 97 larval foci removed; 8,250 kg of unusable materials removed. The IEC team (Instruir, Educar e Comunicar) operated in the city center with an information stand, distributing folders, posters, and prevention guidance. Nebulization occurred in Jardim Adalberto Roxo following a confirmed dengue case to reinforce protection. Campaign underscores daily prevention, including eliminating standing water, keeping yards tidy, covering water tanks, clearing gutters, proper waste disposal, avoiding open scrap, maintaining drains, and allowing vector-control inspections.

articles.headlineTranslated: Ministry of Health reinforces the fight against chikungunya with the reorganization of health care services in Dourados - Ponta Porã Informa - News from Ponta Porã - MS and Pedro Juan Caballero - PY.
articles.summary: Chikungunya control efforts intensified in Dourados, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, as the National Force of the SUS arrived on March 18 to expand outbreak response in the Indigenous Health District. The tripartite operation—Federal, state and municipal—integrates Sesai and the SVSA with the DSEI-MS surveillance center after an arboviruses alert due to rising chikungunya activity in the base area around Dourados. The response strengthens vector control and reorganizes health care, deploying about 20 additional SUS personnel, expanded Ebserh-backed services, improved logistics, active case finding, and regulatory support. Measures include home visits, elimination of breeding sites, and insecticide applications, plus training for early recognition of chikungunya symptoms. Since early March, roughly 100 health and endemic agents have visited over 2,200 Indigenous residences; a mobile Ebserh care unit operates on site, and dengue vaccine availability is reported at 100%.

articles.headline: Pelotas inicia higienização de escolas após mais de 60 casos de doença gastrointestinal | Zona Sul
articles.headlineTranslated: Pelotas begins school sanitization after more than 60 cases of gastrointestinal illness | South Zone
articles.summary: Pelotas’ municipal schools began intensified cleaning on March 19, 2026, after more than 60 confirmed gastrointestinal illness cases among students in the city’s South Zone. Health authorities suspect norovirus, a highly transmissible pathogen that can cause vomiting, diarrhea, and nausea. Cleaning uses concentrated chlorine-based products focusing on high-contact surfaces—doorknobs, taps, tables, floors, and toilet handles—to curb transmission. To maximize effectiveness and minimize chlorine exposure, the municipal network suspended classes for two days to allow thorough sanitization before in‑person return. Norovirus mainly spreads via the fecal‑oral route through contaminated surfaces and hands, especially in schools with young children. The intermission aims to interrupt transmission and reduce virus circulation. Parents are advised not to send symptomatic children to school; however, state and private schools have not halted operations.

articles.headlineTranslated: Measles alert draws attention in Brazil and places Goiás under surveillance
articles.summary: Measles alert prompts heightened vigilance in Brazil as cases rise across the Americas; Goiás is under constant surveillance though no recent outbreak has been recorded. The Ministry of Health cites importation risk from travelers entering Brazil, with a six-month-old infant diagnosed after international travel illustrating ongoing vulnerability in the unvaccinated age group. Brazil has resumed measles-free status, but falling vaccination coverage raises concerns among health authorities. Goiás is prioritized due to proximity to states with cases and interregional movement. Measles is highly contagious and can cause fever, rash and serious complications. Vaccination remains the main preventive measure, provided free through Brazil's Unified Health System (SUS), to close immunity gaps and prevent reestablishment of transmission.

articles.headline: BH promove vacinação emergencial contra raiva após caso no Barreiro
articles.headlineTranslated: Belo Horizonte promotes emergency vaccination against rabies after a case in Barreiro.
articles.summary: As of 19 March 2026, Belo Horizonte initiated emergency rabies vaccination after confirming a rabies case in the Barreiro region. The vaccination ring targets dogs and cats within a 300-meter radius of the case site. Health teams also advise residents on reducing bat presence in homes. For any contact or exposure to potentially rabid animals—bats, dogs, or cats—individuals should seek evaluation at a health center, where prophylaxis may include rabies vaccine or rabies immunoglobulin when indicated. In cases of aggression by domiciled dogs or cats, the animal should be observed at home for 10 days; if signs of illness appear, the animal disappears, or dies, contact Zoonoses or a health unit. Rabies vaccination for dogs and cats is offered year-round at the Centers for Sterilization and the Center for Zoonoses Control.

articles.headlineTranslated: "Speed of transmission draws attention," says the Health Secretary about an outbreak of a gastrointestinal illness in Pelotas' schools | South Zone
articles.summary: Norovirus is suspected as the cause of a gastrointestinal illness outbreak in Pelotas, Brazil, in the South Zone, with cases in municipal schools rising rapidly to 61 confirmed in a few days as of 2026-03-19. Symptoms include vomiting, diarrhea, and nausea, with transmission mainly via fecal-oral routes and contact with contaminated surfaces, spread especially among children aged 1–5 years in school settings. In response, authorities suspended in-person classes across the municipal network to break transmission and allow thorough cleaning with chlorine on high-contact surfaces, and to reinforce hand hygiene, surface disinfection, and avoiding sharing personal items. Most cases are mild and manageable at home with hydration; watch for dehydration signs, lethargy, or unwillingness to drink, which would warrant medical attention. Health authorities emphasized rapid containment to normalize the situation in coming days; ongoing case evaluations at other schools.

articles.headline: Inglaterra vive surto de meningite; veja cuidados antes de viajar
articles.headlineTranslated: England Experiences a Meningitis Outbreak; See Precautions Before Traveling.
articles.summary: 20 cases of bacterial meningococcal meningitis have been reported in Southwest England as of March 18, 2026, per UKHSA, described as an unprecedented outbreak with two deaths. The disease is caused by Neisseria meningitidis and spreads via respiratory droplets. Travelers between Brazil and the United Kingdom are urged to take precautions. Vaccination is ideally completed at least two weeks before travel, though schedules may require two to three doses depending on age, with each dose costing about 600 Brazilian reais. For those in the UK, avoid sharing personal items, maintain hand hygiene, and minimize time in crowded indoor venues such as pubs and tourist sites. Be vigilant for symptoms: sudden high fever, severe headache, and neck stiffness; the bacterial form can progress rapidly, so seek medical care immediately if suspected. Experts note vaccination as a key preventive measure.

articles.headline: Entenda o que é meningite meningocócica bacteriana; Inglaterra registra surto da doença
articles.headlineTranslated: Understand what bacterial meningococcal meningitis is; England records an outbreak of the disease.
articles.summary: Unprecedented outbreak of bacterial meningococcal meningitis due to Neisseria meningitidis is unfolding in southwest England, with at least 20 cases reported as of March 18, 2026, per the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA). The infection spreads through respiratory droplets generated by coughing, talking, or kissing; vaccination and good hygiene are essential prevention. Symptoms include fever and a severe headache, often accompanied by vomiting, extreme weakness, and in severe cases seizures. Hospital admission and intravenous antibiotics are mandatory. While meningitis can be caused by various pathogens, the bacterial form is typically more severe. The report contrasts with Brazil’s epidemiology, where meningitis is endemic and bacterial cases peak in autumn–winter, with 2025 São Paulo state reporting 3,333 cases and 407 deaths. Public health messaging highlights droplet transmission, not aerosols, distinguishing it from COVID-19.

articles.headline: Surto bacteriano atinge centenas de turistas na Ilha do Sal
articles.headlineTranslated: Bacterial outbreak hits hundreds of tourists on Sal Island
articles.summary: Shigellosis outbreak linked to hotels on Sal Island, Cabo Verde, with over 1,000 cases of shigellosis and other intestinal infections reported among tourists since Sept 2022. Since 2022, 766 laboratory-confirmed shigellosis cases identified, plus hundreds of salmonellosis and giardiasis cases in European and North American visitors; Portugal has 12 affected. Transmission is primarily fecal-oral, likely from contaminated water or food. The cluster centers on a hotel chain in the Santa Maria area; source has not been isolated. The ECDC issued urgent traveler recommendations; risk is moderate while origin remains uncontrolled. Cabo Verde authorities are conducting investigations of suppliers and hotel facilities to enforce sanitation protocols. Travelers should practice strict hand hygiene, drink only bottled water, and eat well-cooked foods; avoid raw vegetables, unpeeled fruits, salads, and ice. Seek medical care if diarrhea, fever, or abdominal pain occurs.

articles.summary: First Mpox (Monkeypox) case in Cachoeiro de Itapemirim, Espírito Santo, Brazil, was confirmed by the State Health Secretariat on March 17. The patient is male. Since confirmation, all Ministry of Health-recommended measures have been adopted, including isolation, monitoring of contacts, and appropriate case management by health teams. Sentinels of Health continue continuous surveillance with tracing and control actions aimed at preventing disease spread. Mpox is a viral illness that can cause fever, headache, body aches, lymphadenopathy, and skin lesions that may appear as spots, blisters, or sores, often on the face, hands, feet, and genital region. People with these symptoms should promptly seek a health facility. Municipal teams are trained to identify, advise, and safely manage cases, with active vigilance and adherence to sanitary protocols to protect the population. Information from the Cachoeiro de Itapemirim City Hall.

articles.headline: Brasil entra em alerta máximo por surtos de sarampo na América
articles.headlineTranslated: Brazil on high alert over measles outbreaks in the Americas.
articles.summary: Measles remains a priority for Brazil to preserve its measles-free status since November 2024, says Eder Gatti, director of the National Immunization Program. Internationally, the Americas reported 14,891 measles cases and 29 deaths in 2025; by March 5, 2026, another 7,145 infections were confirmed. Brazil’s first case of the year appeared in a six-month-old infant in São Paulo who contracted the virus during travel to Bolivia, a country experiencing an outbreak, but authorities say there is no sustained transmission at home. To sustain elimination, Brazil emphasizes active surveillance and expanded vaccination; the SUS schedule provides two doses at 12 and 15 months. Last year, first-dose coverage reached 92.5%, but only 77.9% completed on time. Campaigns focus on border regions; vaccination is advised for people up to 59 without two-dose proof. ANVISA warns at airports/ports ahead of the 2026 World Cup in the US, Mexico and Canada.

articles.headline: Detectan la cepa más peligrosa de viruela del mono en la Argentina y un hombre está internado
articles.headlineTranslated: The most dangerous strain of monkeypox detected in Argentina and a man is hospitalized.
articles.summary: Argentina detects monkeypox clade Ib, originating in DR Congo in 2023, a shift from earlier clade II cases in the country. Clade Ib is linked to greater severity and contagiousness. The outbreak has spread to the United States, Canada, Brazil and Mexico, with community transmission in Spain, France and Portugal. Symptoms include skin lesions (pink spots, ulcers, vesicles, or crusts) often near the genitals or face; fever, malaise, severe headache; painful lymphadenopathy; proctitis and sore throat. Incubation is 6–13 days, up to 21; more severe in immunosuppressed individuals or those with uncontrolled HIV. Health authorities recommend intensified surveillance and high suspicion for sudden rash; immediate medical evaluation; isolation until crusts fall and new skin forms; contact tracing within 24 hours. WHO vaccines exist for select groups, but Argentina prioritizes early detection and symptom management to prevent complications like bacterial infections or sepsis; Mendoza had earlier cases.

articles.headline: Felipeh Campos é internado em estado crítico após diagnóstico de dengue
articles.headlineTranslated: Felipeh Campos is hospitalized in critical condition after being diagnosed with dengue.
articles.summary: Felipeh Campos, a Band journalist and host in São Paulo, is hospitalized in critical condition after a dengue diagnosis. On March 18, 2026, his platelet count dropped to 25,000, prompting admission to Beneficência Portuguesa hospital, where doctors were evaluating next steps and the possibility of transfer to a higher-complexity unit. Dengue can cause drastic platelet declines; counts below 150,000 are abnormal, and under 50,000 increase the risk of bleeding and complications. Campos’ illness also disrupted his duties on the Band program Melhor da Noite, with the March 18 edition canceled while the care team determines the appropriate course of treatment. The report attributes the information to journalist Fábia Oliveira of Metrópoles.

articles.headline: Cabo Verde em alerta devido a infeção intestinal que afetou centenas de turistas
articles.headlineTranslated: Cabo Verde on alert due to an intestinal infection that affected hundreds of tourists.
articles.summary: Shigellosis outbreak linked to Sal Island, Cabo Verde, affects nearly 1,000 tourists since 2022, per the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC). Confirmed cases involve travelers from the United Kingdom, Sweden, Germany, France, the Netherlands, Belgium, Denmark, Luxembourg, the Czech Republic, Portugal, Finland, Norway, Ireland, Poland, and the United States. Shigellosis is a bacterial intestinal infection caused by Shigella, transmitted fecal-oral, with acute diarrhea (sometimes blood or mucus), fever, abdominal cramps, and nausea. Other tourists reported gastroenteritis due to salmonellosis, campylobacteriosis, giardiasis, or amebiasis. The outbreak appears centered in a chain of hotels in Santa Maria; the exact source is not yet confirmed. ECDC advises travelers to Cabo Verde to practice hand hygiene, eat hot prepared foods, avoid unwashed produce, drink bottled water, and seek medical care for compatible symptoms.

articles.headline: Força Nacional do SUS define ações contra chikungunya em Dourados após aumento de casos
articles.headlineTranslated: SUS's National Force defines actions against chikungunya in Dourados after an increase in cases.
articles.summary: Chikungunya outbreak in Dourados, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil triggers intensified action by the National Force of SUS. With exponential growth in confirmed chikungunya cases, especially in Indigenous reserves, the task force—joining Sesai and SVSA after a DSEI-MS epidemiological alert—focuses on vector control and health-service reorganization in Indigenous hubs. Aedes aegypti, the vector for dengue, Zika and chikungunya, drives the response. Measures include expanding health staff via Ebserh, reinforced logistics with vehicles to reach communities, active case finding and regulatory support, and intensified vector control with home visits, breeding-site elimination, and insecticide application; training for early recognition of chikungunya symptoms. Residents are urged to strengthen prevention. The Indigenous Escola Tengatui Marangatu in Jaguapiru is operating as a field hospital since March 17, with multisector teams and hours 7:00–19:00, possibly extending, as needed.

articles.headline: Gripe K: infectologista explica sintomas e como se prevenir
articles.headlineTranslated: Flu K: Infectious disease specialist explains symptoms and how to prevent it.
articles.summary: Flu K is a genetic subclade of Influenza A (H3N2), not a new disease. It presents with standard influenza symptoms: fever, cough, body aches, and fatigue. Infectious disease specialist Raphael Zanotti, from Hospital Santa Rita, explains that Influenza A frequently undergoes rearrangements and minor mutations, periodically generating variants. These changes can allow Flu K and other strains to evade immune responses built from past infections or prior vaccines, enabling new infections. The virus tends to circulate year after year across different populations and hemispheres, providing opportunities for new variants to emerge and spread. The article provides no case counts, laboratory confirmation details, or specific information on infection sources or imported/exported cases. It emphasizes the ongoing role of antigenic drift in influenza and notes the absence of detailed prevention guidance within the text.

articles.headline: Sesau faz alerta após casos de doenças respiratórias aumentarem em Campo Grande
articles.headlineTranslated: Sesau issues an alert after cases of respiratory diseases rise in Campo Grande.
articles.summary: Campo Grande, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil – As of epidemiological week 10 of 2026, 291 SRAG (Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome) cases have been recorded with 25 deaths (8.2% fatality). Simultaneous circulation of rhinovirus, influenza A, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and COVID-19 is identified among severe cases, with the surge starting earlier than the usual April–July peak. Most severe cases affect children, especially under 1 year, followed by ages 1–4 and 5–9. Prevention emphasizes hand hygiene, covering the mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing, avoiding closed spaces and crowds, and maintaining up-to-date vaccination. Influenza vaccination is the primary strategy to reduce severe illness; Campo Grande’s National Flu Vaccination Day (Dia D) is planned to begin on 28 March.

articles.headline: BH entra em alerta após caso de morcego com raiva
articles.headlineTranslated: Belo Horizonte goes on alert after a bat with rabies.
articles.summary: As of 19 March 2026, Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais, heightens alert after confirming a rabies-infected dead bat in the Diamante neighborhood of the Barreiro region. A rapid response vaccinates dogs and cats within 300 meters of the discovery, with zoonosis workers visiting homes to educate residents and curb transmission to humans. Authorities emphasize pet vaccination as the main preventive measure, not relying on annual campaigns, and advocate daily care for pets in wildlife-prone areas. People should avoid handling bats; if a bat is found or there is contact with bats, dogs, or cats, cover the animal and contact zoonoses for removal and evaluation. Immediate medical care is essential after bites or scratches. Minas Gerais reports rabies cases in cattle, horses, and bats this year, sustaining surveillance and urging notification to epidemiological services.

articles.headline: Other event - Brazil - 1 dead, over 100 sickened in Brazil food poisoning
articles.headlineTranslated: Other event - Brazil - 1 death, over 100 sickened in Brazil food poisoning
articles.summary: Food poisoning outbreak in Pombal, Paraiba state, Brazil, after dining at a local pizzeria on Sunday night. One death: a 44-year-old woman admitted to Pombal Regional Hospital on Monday; she died subsequently. Over 100 people were hospitalized or sought medical care with similar symptoms, including nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain and general malaise; eight-year-old child remains hospitalized as of 19 March 2026. The pizzeria was temporarily shuttered by the health inspection service, which collected food samples for analysis. Authorities have not confirmed a pathogen publicly; laboratory analysis is ongoing to determine cause. All reported cases linked to the same restaurant, suggesting a common source. There is no information on imported or exported cases. The incident prompted public health investigation and ongoing monitoring of hospitalizations.

articles.headline: Felipeh Campos é internado com dengue em estado grave em SP
articles.headlineTranslated: Felipeh Campos is admitted to hospital with dengue fever in serious condition in São Paulo.
articles.summary: Brazilian Band presenter Felipeh Campos is hospitalized in São Paulo with dengue fever in critical condition. He was admitted on March 18, 2026, to Beneficência Portuguesa after a sharp drop in platelets to 25,000/µL, a severe thrombocytopenia signaling high bleeding risk. He remains under medical observation with no discharge date and will not participate in the later broadcast of Melhor da Noite. Doctors report the severe thrombocytopenia as the main warning sign; platelets below 150,000 indicate alteration, and below 50,000 are concerning. There is no confirmed need for transfer to a higher-dependency unit (e.g., semi-intensive) yet; he is under continuous evaluation for clinical evolution. No prognosis on return to activities as of the report.

articles.headline: Bactéria transmitida por via fecal-oral está a atingir centenas de pessoas e há 12 portugueses afetados: maior foco da doença estará neste local
articles.headlineTranslated: A bacterium transmitted via the fecal-oral route is affecting hundreds of people, with 12 Portuguese affected: the disease's main hotspot will be in this location.
articles.summary: Shigellosis, a highly contagious bacterial infection transmitted via the fecal-oral route, is affecting tourists in Cabo Verde, with hundreds of cases on Sal Island and 12 Portuguese among the infected. The European CDC (ECDC) identifies a hotspot in a hotel chain in the Santa Maria area, though the precise source remains unclear and links between episodes are not definitive. From September 2022 to recent weeks, 766 shigellosis cases have been confirmed in travelers from the United Kingdom, Sweden, Germany, France, the Netherlands, and Portugal. More than 300 additional gastrointestinal illness cases, including salmonellosis, campylobacteriosis, giardiasis, and amebiasis, have also been reported. Symptoms typically appear 1–4 days after exposure and include diarrhea, fever, and abdominal pain. Preventive measures include frequent handwashing, eating well-cooked foods, avoiding raw or ready-to-eat items (salads, unwashed fruit, ice), and drinking only bottled water. Seek medical care for persistent diarrhea, fever, or intense abdominal pain.

articles.summary: Oropouche virus advances in Brazil, accounting for 90% of Americas cases in 2025 across 20 states, with five deaths (Rio de Janeiro four, Espírito Santo one). Mosquito-borne, it causes flu-like symptoms; Europe reports traveler-linked cases; vertical transmission documented. No vaccine or specific treatment exists; WHO on 5 January 2026 proposed accelerating prevention tools. H5N1 avian influenza jumped to cattle in the United States in 2024, with several state outbreaks and cow-to-human transmissions. Brazil reported a farm outbreak in 2025. US CDC records 71 human cases and two deaths; no sustained community transmission. Vaccines exist but may offer limited protection; Butantan Institute conducts preclinical vaccine safety studies. Mpox has spread since 2022, with clade IIb and rising clade I infections in Central Africa since 2024, more severe. In the US, cases occur in people without Africa travel history. Vaccines exist but no widely available treatment; 2026 could bring challenges.

articles.headline: 'A tuberculose não acabou, é um problema global', diz John Green, que lança livro sobre a 'infecção mais mortal'
articles.headlineTranslated: Tuberculosis isn't over, it's a global problem, says John Green, who releases a book about the "most deadly infection".
articles.summary: TB remains a global threat, killing about 1.2 million people annually despite available tests and treatments. American author John Green discusses his book 'Tudo é tuberculose' (Everything Is Tuberculosis), which argues TB disproportionately affects vulnerable populations lacking drug access and has shaped culture, while remaining stigmatized. Completed in 2024 and published by Editora Intrínseca, the book frames TB as a solvable crisis if cases are actively found, patients treated, and close contacts receive preventive care. Green warns the global situation will worsen amid wars and funding cuts in health, including a 2025 U.S. policy shift that halted treatment for hundreds of thousands; though funding later largely restored, drug resistance rose during the gap. Stigma drives abandonment of patients; activists urge more funding and advocacy, including protests. References include the United States and Brazil.

articles.headline: Agência da ONU relata transmissão de febre amarela em partes da América do Sul
articles.headlineTranslated: The UN agency reports yellow fever transmission in parts of South America.
articles.summary: Yellow fever transmission continues in South America, with 34 human cases and 15 deaths reported in the first seven weeks of 2026 across Bolivia, Colombia, Peru and Venezuela, extending beyond traditional Amazon basin foci. OPAS warns of sustained sylvatic transmission cycles involving mosquitoes and non-human primates, with reactivation in areas without recent transmission, including São Paulo state (Brazil) and Tolima (Colombia). For 2025, seven Latin American countries reported 346 confirmed cases and 143 deaths: Bolivia 8/2, Brazil 120/48, Colombia 125/46, Ecuador 11/8, Guyana 1 death, Peru 49/19, Venezuela 32/19. Urban transmission risk rises via Aedes aegypti, increasing city outbreak potential. OPAS urges vaccination coverage of at least 95% among exposed populations, strengthened epidemiological and epizootic surveillance, and maintenance of vaccine stocks; travelers should be vaccinated at least 10 days before travel; no specific treatment exists.

articles.headline: One Outbreak, Two Countries
articles.summary: Measles outbreaks in southern Alberta and northern Mexico (Chihuahua) are epidemiologically linked via a single measles genotype circulating among Mennonite communities across Canada, the United States, Mexico, Belize, Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, and Paraguay, indicating a transnational outbreak. Alberta’s epicenter is Taber, Lethbridge County, with two-dose coverage at 29% in Taber and 40% in Lethbridge County as of 2024; the province ended 2025 with over 2,000 confirmed cases, including a premature baby death and permanent harm to children. In Chihuahua, vaccination coverage is estimated at 40–50%, and by August nearly 4,000 confirmed cases accounted for most of Mexico’s measles deaths. The outbreak is described as a diaspora-spread event, not two separate national crises, and is complicated by Low German-speaking Mennonite community memory of vaccination experiences, shaping hesitancy beyond theology or politics.

articles.headline: Mulher morre e 118 ficam doentes depois de comer em pizzaria
articles.headlineTranslated: Woman dies and 118 fall ill after eating at a pizzeria
articles.summary: 118 people sickened and one woman died after dining at La Favoritta pizzeria in Pombal, inland Paraíba, Brazil, on March 14. The 44-year-old Raíssa Maritein Bezerra e Silva died after a rapid progression to a severe infectious illness; the hospital reported she arrived in grave condition with acute septic-like features. An eight-year-old child remains hospitalized; 40 patients treated at the UPA have been discharged. Civil Police consider intentional poisoning unlikely since staff also became ill within minutes. Infection source suspected to be carne de sol (sun-dried beef) used in the nata pizza; the meat was bought Saturday morning, nata prepared that afternoon. The pizzeria was interdicted; inspections revealed improper food storage and presence of insects, and a lack of SOPs, hygiene protocols, and pest-control measures. Municipal surveillance and Agevisa are investigating; the owner cooperates.

articles.headline: Felipeh Campos é internado em SP em estado grave com diagnóstico de dengue
articles.headlineTranslated: Felipeh Campos hospitalized in São Paulo in serious condition, diagnosed with dengue.
articles.summary: Felipeh Campos, 52, was hospitalized on March 18, 2026, at Hospital Beneficência Portuguesa in São Paulo after dengue progressed to a critical state. Doctors report a platelet count around 25,000 per microliter, requiring intensive monitoring and strict hydration to avert serious complications. As of March 19, 2026, no discharge date has been announced, and he remains under continuous surveillance led by Dr. Marcelo Sampaio. He will not participate in this week's Melhor da Noite on Band due to medical advice. The report confirms dengue diagnosis and hospitalization in São Paulo, Brazil; no information on infection source or further laboratory confirmation beyond the dengue diagnosis is provided.

articles.headline: Surto de sarampo em países das Américas deixa Brasil em alerta máximo
articles.headlineTranslated: Measles outbreak in the Americas puts Brazil on high alert.
articles.summary: Measles outbreak in the Americas puts Brazil on high alert. Last year region reported 14,891 cases, 38 in Brazil, nearly 32 times 2023’s 446. Through March 5, 2026, over 7,145 cases have been confirmed in the Americas; Brazil’s first case this year is a 6-month-old in São Paulo infected after a trip to Bolivia, a country with an outbreak. Most cases are imported—unvaccinated Brazilians returning with measles or foreigners infected on visits. The Health Ministry is boosting vaccination campaigns in border areas and surveillance at states and municipalities, including home and lab investigations. Director Eder Gatti cites heavy tourism and shared borders; Brazil coordinates with Anvisa to issue alerts on aircraft, airports, and cruise ships. Vaccination remains the main defense: SUS provides two doses (12 months via triple viral vaccine and 15 months via tetraviral), plus a dose zero during outbreaks. Brazil regained measles-free status in 2024, but the alert persists.
