articles.headline: Entrevista: Brasil entra em alerta máximo por surtos de sarampo na América
articles.headlineTranslated: Interview: Brazil goes into maximum alert amid measles outbreaks in the Americas.
articles.summary: As of 19 March 2026, Brazil is on maximum alert due to measles outbreaks across the Americas. The continent has confirmed 7,145 measles cases, about 50% of all 2025 records. Brazilian infectious disease expert Dr. Adelino Melo Freire Jr., president of the Minas Gerais Society of Infectology, discusses measures to prevent a further rise in Brazil and outlines guidance on what to do if measles is suspected. The interview underscores the regional outbreak in the Americas and the need for heightened vigilance and preventive action. It focuses on strategies to curb transmission and on steps for suspected cases, as explained by the expert.

articles.headline: Ação integrada entre as três esferas de governo intensifica vigilância de vírus respiratórios em RO
articles.headlineTranslated: Integrated action among the three levels of government intensifies surveillance of respiratory viruses in Rondônia.
articles.summary: From March 16–20 in Porto Velho, Rondônia, a technical visit brings together state, municipal, and national/international teams to strengthen respiratory virus surveillance, focusing on indicators, care pathways, vaccination coverage, and laboratory capacity. The effort enhances integration between sentinel influenza-like illness (ILI) surveillance and universal severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS) surveillance, immunization, and diagnostic testing. Governor Marcos Rocha emphasizes investment in surveillance to enable rapid, effective responses to respiratory diseases. Agevisa/RO director Gilvander Gregorio de Lima notes evaluation of health units, identification of best practices, and improvements under the Mosaic Strategy Action Plan for respiratory virus surveillance. Luma Kubota highlights exchange of experiences for border regions and indigenous populations. Sesau Secretary Edilton Oliveira dos Santos frames it as aligning protocols and boosting efficiency. The program includes technical meetings, visits to sentinel units, hospitals, the cold chain network, Lacen, and facilities such as Policlínica Ana Adelaide, Cemetron, and Hospital Infantil Cosme e Damião, with PAHO and the Ministry of Health.

articles.headline: Menina morre vítima de febre maculosa no Norte do ES - SiteBarra
articles.headlineTranslated: Girl dies of Brazilian spotted fever in northern Espírito Santo.
articles.summary: Two-year-four-month-old Kyara Silva Rúbia died of Brazilian spotted fever in Boa Esperança, Northwest Espírito Santo, Brazil. The death occurred January 28 and was confirmed March 18 by the Municipal Health Secretariat. The rural resident lived about 6 km from the town center, where capybaras were seen, animals that can host the star tick, the vector of the disease. The child presented fever and body rash; dengue and varicella were initially suspected. She was hospitalized successively at Hospital Cristo Rei in the city center, Hospital São Marcos in Nova Venécia, Hospital Estadual Dr. Roberto Silvares in São Mateus, and finally the Children’s Hospital in Vitória, dying about a week after symptom onset. The report emphasizes the tick-borne transmission and potential rural exposure.

articles.headline: Measles exposure warning issued for Calgary airport, Alberta travel hubs
articles.summary: Measles exposure warning issued for Calgary International Airport and several Alberta travel hubs after potential exposures at various locations during listed times. Anyone born in 1970 or later who has fewer than two documented measles vaccine doses and has never had measles could be at risk; review immunization records and monitor for symptoms, seeking care if needed. Alberta reports a measles resurgence with nearly 200 confirmed cases in 2026, following more than 2,000 cases in 2025. Calgary has two confirmed cases this year, with roughly half of 2026 cases in the South Zone. The advisory emphasizes vaccination status and early symptom awareness to curb spread amid ongoing outbreak activity.

articles.headline: Ministério da Saúde reforça ação de combate à chikungunya com reforço e reorganização da assistência à saúde em Dourados
articles.headlineTranslated: Ministry of Health strengthens its fight against chikungunya with reinforcement and reorganization of health care services in Dourados.
articles.summary: Chikungunya control efforts in Dourados, Brazil are being intensified through an integrated approach prioritizing vector control and reorganization of health services, with emphasis on Indigenous villages. Measures include expanding health staff via Ebserh, improved logistics with vehicle access, active case finding, and regulatory support; and stronger vector-control actions such as home visits, elimination of breeding sites, and insecticide application. Health workers will receive training for early recognition of chikungunya. National SUS Force director Rodrigo Stabeli said the population is not underserved, with about 20 professionals deployed to the territory alongside health agents for active searches, cleaning campaigns, and care of the ill. Sesai is hiring more endemic agents and continuing sanitation and living-condition improvements in Indigenous communities. Since early March, ~100 health/endemic agents have visited over 2,200 residences in aldeias; mutirões de limpeza and insecticide use are underway. Ebserh has a mobile care unit; the tripartite response (federal, state, municipality) includes vaccination outreach and prevention efforts, including 100% dengue vaccine coverage in the municipality.

articles.headline: Minsa refuerza acciones de prevención, diagnóstico y manejo clínico de la leptospirosis a nivel nacional
articles.headlineTranslated: Ministry of Health strengthens nationwide actions for prevention, diagnosis, and clinical management of leptospirosis.
articles.summary: Leptospirosis remains a national priority in Peru's health ministry, with 841 cases reported through epidemiological week 9 of 2026; 60% probable (505) and 40% confirmed (336). Regions with highest incidence: Loreto, Madre de Dios, Tumbes, Ucayali, San Martín, Amazonas, Ayacucho, Huánuco, and Cusco. Three deaths in Piura, San Martín, and Tumbes. The Ministry of Health intensifies surveillance, training, lab capacity, case analysis, health promotion, and risk communication through health offices. Training exceeded 300 health professionals from Cajamarca, Ayacucho, Cusco, Piura, Ucayali, Tumbes, and San Martín, improving surveillance and clinical management. INS is conducting quality control of diagnostic tests and distributing 500 ELISA kits; PCR tests are being rolled out regionally. Community interventions include household counseling, education sessions, and formation of community surveillance committees. Citizens are advised to avoid stagnant or contaminated water, use protection in flood zones, maintain hygiene, and seek care for fever, muscle pain, or malaise.

articles.headline: Sarampión en Bebés: Riesgos, Vacunación y Viajes
articles.headlineTranslated: Measles in Babies: Risks, Vaccination, and Travel.
articles.summary: On March 11, 2026, São Paulo state confirmed the first measles case of 2026: a six-month-old who contracted measles during a January trip to Bolivia. The infant was unvaccinated because the MMR vaccine is given at 12 months; maternal antibodies can blunt early responses. For babies six to eleven months traveling to areas with active transmission, a 'zero-dose' measles vaccination before the first birthday is sometimes recommended, but it provides partial protection and does not replace the two-dose schedule at 12 and 15 months, nor is it in the national calendar. Bolivia has ongoing transmission with 597 cases; the Americas saw a 32-fold rise in measles from 2024 to 2025, totaling 14,891 cases in 2025 across 13 countries, including 2,242 cases and three deaths in the United States, and 38 cases in Brazil (10 imported). Health authorities urge pre-travel pediatric consultation and destination risk assessment; vaccination remains the best protection.

articles.headline: Carrapato-estrela: criança morre de febre maculosa em cidade do ES - Folha Vitória
articles.headlineTranslated: Lone star tick: child dies of Rocky Mountain spotted fever in a city in Espírito Santo - Folha Vitória
articles.summary: Rocky Mountain spotted fever (RMSF) caused by Rickettsia rickettsii led to the death of a child in a city in Espírito Santo, Brazil, linked to the Lone star tick. The vector is the tick Amblyomma cajennense, which feeds on large animals such as horses and cattle. Transmission requires the tick to remain attached to the skin for about four hours; younger nymphs are harder to detect and thus more dangerous. RMSF is not transmitted between people. Primary symptoms include fever, body rash, and headaches and can be fatal. The Secretaria de Estado da Saúde (Sesa) advises people in tick-endemic areas to regularly inspect their bodies for ticks and to remove them carefully with protective gloves. If symptoms appear, seek medical care promptly and inform clinicians about tick exposure.

articles.headline: Aulas são suspensas em aldeia de MS após aumento de casos de chikungunya e quatro mortes
articles.headlineTranslated: Classes are suspended in a village in Mato Grosso do Sul after a rise in chikungunya cases and four deaths.
articles.summary: Chikungunya outbreak in Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, centered in Dourados' Jaguapiru Indigenous Reservation. As of March 16, 2026, the Jaguapiru Reserve reported 407 total chikungunya cases: 202 confirmed, 181 under investigation, 24 discarded, and 4 deaths. The deaths include a 69-year-old woman (Jaguapiru, 26/02), a 73-year-old man (Jaguapiru, 09/03), a 3-month-old infant (Bororó, 10/03), and a 60-year-old woman (Jaguapiru, 12/03). Urban area notes 912 notifications in 2026, with 379 confirmed, 383 pending, and 150 discarded; no deaths outside the reserve yet. In Jaguapiru, 30% of students and 9 teachers at the largest school Tengatui Marangatu are infected; Escola Estadual Guateka has about 20 staff out. Water shortages are linked to mosquito breeding; Aedes aegypti transmits the virus. Mutirão by municipal health teams and state support underway; SUS forces arriving March 19 to reinforce actions.

articles.headline: Felipeh Campos é internado com dengue em estado crítico e se afasta da TV
articles.headlineTranslated: Felipeh Campos is hospitalized with dengue fever in critical condition and is taking a break from TV.
articles.summary: Felipeh Campos, host of Melhor da Noite on Band, is hospitalized in São Paulo with a critical dengue fever diagnosis on March 18, 2026. He will not participate in the edition scheduled for today, and Band’s statement says he remains under medical observation with no discharge or return date yet. Dengue is a viral disease transmitted by the Aedes aegypti mosquito and can progress to severe forms with intense symptoms and risk of complications if not treated promptly; hospitalization is used for monitoring and clinical support in such cases. The report notes Campos is a journalist and television presenter, and attempts to contact him were unsuccessful by publication time. No laboratory confirmation or specific infection source details are provided in the article. The story highlights ongoing health impact on a public figure and his temporary withdrawal from filming obligations.

articles.headline: InfoGripe: número de casos de SRAG volta a aumentar em quase todo o país | Agência Fiocruz de Notícias
articles.headlineTranslated: InfoGripe: number of SRAG cases rises again in almost the entire country | Fiocruz News Agency.
articles.summary: InfoGripe Fiocruz reports SRAG (Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome) cases rising across Brazil in Epidemiological Week 8 (Feb 22–28). The rise is driven mainly by rhinovirus infections in children and adolescents aged 2–14, RSV in under-2s, and influenza A in youths, adults and seniors. With the exception of Roraima, Tocantins, Espírito Santo and Rio Grande do Sul, all states show long-term SRAG growth, and ten states are at alert or higher risk. Twelve capitals show rising SRAG activity: Aracaju, Belém, Belo Horizonte, Brasília, Cuiabá, Fortaleza, João Pessoa, Macapá, Manaus, Porto Velho, Rio Branco and São Luís. Nationally, 14,370 SRAG cases in 2026; 5,029 (35%) lab-positive, 6,193 (43.1%) negative, 2,073 (14.4%) pending. Positives: influenza A 20%, influenza B 1.7%, RSV 13.6%, rhinovirus 40%, SARS-CoV-2 17%; last four weeks: rhinovirus 45.4%, influenza A 20.8%, RSV 15.4%, SARS-CoV-2 14.3%. Incidence higher in young children; mortality concentrated in the elderly; COVID-19 most frequent among deaths, followed by influenza A (positives: SARS-CoV-2 39.1%, influenza A 27.5%).

articles.headline: Criança de 2 anos morre vítima de febre maculosa no Norte do Espírito Santo
articles.headlineTranslated: Two-year-old child dies of Rocky Mountain spotted fever in northern Espírito Santo.
articles.summary: Rocky Mountain spotted fever (tick-borne illness) in Boa Esperança, northern Espírito Santo, Brazil, has been confirmed as the cause of death of a 2-year-4-month-old girl, Kyara Silva Rubia. She died on January 28, with laboratory confirmation announced on March 18 after epidemiological investigation. The rural child lived about six kilometers from the town center in an area where capybaras, potential hosts for the star tick (Amblyomma spp.), are present; the exact exposure date is unknown. Initial symptoms included fever, followed by a maculopapular rash; dengue and varicella were initially suspected. She required multiple hospital transfers—from Boa Esperança to Nova Venécia, then Hospital Roberto Silvares in São Mateus, and finally a hospital in Vitória—dying about a week after symptom onset. Public health authorities confirmed the diagnosis through laboratory testing.

articles.headline: Aumento de casos de mpox preocupa autoridades de saúde no Brasil
articles.headlineTranslated: Increase in mpox cases concerns health authorities in Brazil.
articles.summary: Mpox cases rise in Brazil in early 2026, with confirmed infections concentrated in urban centers, especially São Paulo, and transmission extending to Rio de Janeiro, Roraima, and states across the South, Northeast, and Central-West. Official panels show most confirmed cases remain in São Paulo; dozens of cases are under investigation, while no substantial rise in mpox-related deaths is observed in 2026. The disease is transmitted mainly by close contact with infected individuals, including skin lesions, bodily fluids, respiratory droplets in prolonged exposure, and shared contaminated items. Symptoms occur in two stages: initial non-specific symptoms (fever, headache, fatigue, myalgia, lymphadenopathy), followed by an eruptive phase with lesions on face, hands, feet, trunk, genitalia or mucous membranes that evolve from macules to vesicles to crusts. Diagnosis relies on clinical assessment and laboratory testing; public health measures emphasize prevention, hygiene, rapid care seeking, and contact tracing, especially in high-risk settings.

articles.headline: Aos 86 anos, Fulvio Stefanini recebe alta e faz anúncio importante após infecção - Contigo!
articles.headlineTranslated: At 86 years old, Fulvio Stefanini is discharged and makes an important announcement after an infection.
articles.summary: Fulvio Stefanini, 86, was discharged from hospital after a bacterial infection and will return to the play 'The Father' at Teatro TotalEnergies in Rio de Janeiro's Glória neighborhood. He had canceled last weekend's performances but released a video assuring fans of full recovery and readiness to perform on Friday. The Brazilian staging of Florian Zeller's drama runs at Sala Adolpho Bloch through March 22, with shows on Friday and Saturday at 20:00 and Sunday at 17:00. Cast includes Lara Cordula, Fulvio Stefanini Filho, Deo Patricio, Carol Mariottini, and Leo Stefanini (also director). A post-performance talk with psychoanalyst Luiza Scarpa on March 20 will discuss aging and Alzheimer's disease, central to the plot. The play, based on Zeller's text, references the 2021 film adaptation starring Anthony Hopkins.

articles.headline: Aos 86 anos, Fulvio Stefanini vence infecção e recebe alta hospitalar
articles.headlineTranslated: At 86 years old, Fulvio Stefanini defeats infection and is discharged from hospital.
articles.summary: Fulvio Stefanini, 86, was discharged from a Rio de Janeiro hospital after a bacterial infection. He spent a few days under observation and paused the play O Pai at Teatro TotalEnergies, Sala Adolpho Bloch, in Glória. In a video released on 18 March 2026, the actor said he is completely recovered and will perform as scheduled on Friday, 20 March, with shows on 21 and 22 March at the venue. He previously faced a similar infection in 2020 that required ICU care after a bacterium normally living on the skin entered the bloodstream; he spent four days in the ICU and a total of 16 days in hospital, followed by a month of home care. The current update confirms recovery and readiness to resume performances.

articles.headline: Escola passa a funcionar como hospital após aumento de casos confirmados de chikungunya em Dourados
articles.headlineTranslated: School to operate as a hospital after a surge in confirmed chikungunya cases in Dourados.
articles.summary: Field hospital established inside Escola Municipal Indígena Tengatui Marangatu in Jaguapiru Indigenous Reserve, Dourados, Mato Grosso do Sul, to treat confirmed chikungunya. The unit operates in the school gym, opened March 17, with SESAI coordinating and in partnership with HU-UFGD; teams from Campo Grande and Caarapó reinforced care. On day one, about 80 people were attended. On March 18, demand fell due to rain, while active household surveillance intensified. The latest bulletin shows Jaguapiru with 407 notified, 202 confirmed, 181 under investigation, 24 discarded, and 4 deaths (69F, 73M, 3-month-old, 60F). In urban Dourados, 912 notifications and 379 confirmed, with no deaths. Preventive actions include 4,319 homes inspected, 2,173 sites treated, 1,004 mosquito breeding sites identified (90% in water tanks, trash, tires), and 43 properties sprayed. Staffing: 86 endemic agents and 29 indigenous health agents. Clinic hours 07:00–19:00, extendable.

articles.headline: Governo envia 2 especialistas para controlar chikungunya em aldeias
articles.headlineTranslated: Government sends two specialists to control Chikungunya in villages.
articles.summary: Chikungunya outbreak in the Dourados Indigenous Reserve (Jaguapiru) in Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, as of 18 March 2026. The Health Ministry has dispatched two specialists from the National Force of SUS to coordinate containment for the reserve, the country’s most populous Indigenous area with about 20,000 residents. Of 692 suspected cases, 217 are confirmed; 401 are under investigation and 44 have been discarded. Four residents have died in the last 22 days. A field hospital was opened at Tengatuí Marangatu School; day one saw about 80 patients, and over 30 school staff reported symptoms, with some classes suspended by local leadership. The response includes field teams, clinical-management training, and plans to add four more Força Nacional teams for active case finding. Surveys identified 1,004 Aedes aegypti breeding sites, roughly 90% in water tanks, discarded containers, and tires. Severe cases are referred to HU-UFGD or Caiuá hospital.

articles.headline: Surto de virose faz prefeitura de Pelotas suspender aulas da rede municipal
articles.headlineTranslated: Viral outbreak prompts Pelotas city hall to suspend classes in the municipal school network.
articles.summary: Norovirus-suspected gastrointestinal illness triggers a two-day suspension of Pelotas’ municipal school network in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. As of 18 March 2026, 61 cases have been confirmed, mainly among children under five years old. Health authorities suspect norovirus; samples were sent to the Central Laboratory (Lacen) in Porto Alegre for confirmation. The two-day pause will allow disinfection of 93 schools, with confirmed cases reported in five municipal schools and three additional schools notifying similar symptoms. The preventive measure aims to interrupt transmission; make-up days will be scheduled to recover lost learning time. If a student shows symptoms (vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal cramps) next Monday, they should remain at home and seek care at a Basic Health Unit, with hydration and hand hygiene emphasized. No deaths reported in the article.

articles.headline: Saúde de Brasiléia esclarece situação de Mpox na fronteira com a Bolívia
articles.headlineTranslated: Health Department of Brasiléia clarifies the Mpox situation at the border with Bolivia.
articles.summary: Mpox (monkeypox) remains unconfirmed in Brasiléia, Brazil, on the Brazil-Bolivia border, as of March 18, 2026. The Municipal Health Secretariat reports no confirmed Mpox cases in the municipality. A Brazilian resident of Cobija, Bolivia, diagnosed at the Hospital Regional do Alto Acre, is described as an imported infection originating in another state, not Brasiléia. Several other suspected cases are in Brasiléia awaiting laboratory results. The Vigilância em Saúde and the Border Health Surveillance Center (CIEVS) maintain active monitoring and adherence to established protocols. All health units are prepared to treat suspected cases. If confirmed, the city will inform the public through official channels. Symptoms prompting investigation include fever, body aches, fatigue, and skin lesions.

articles.headline: Criança de dois anos tem morte confirmada por febre maculosa no ES
articles.headlineTranslated: Two-year-old child's death confirmed due to Rocky Mountain spotted fever in Espírito Santo.
articles.summary: Rocky Mountain spotted fever (RMSF) has been confirmed as the cause of death of a two-year-old child in Espírito Santo, Brazil. The family said the child lived in a rural area about 6 km from the municipal seat, where capybaras were observed; capybaras are animals that can host the tick transmitting RMSF. The initial symptoms were fever, followed by a body rash. Dengue and chickenpox were initially suspected. The patient remained hospitalized for two days at a local hospital, then was transferred to Nova Venécia, to Hospital Roberto Silvares in São Mateus, and later to a hospital in Vitória as the condition deteriorated. About a week after the first symptoms, the child died. The case highlights potential tick exposure in rural settings and the role of wildlife as tick hosts.

articles.headline: Leishmaniose em Rio Branco: Saúde alerta sobre doença e orienta moradores
articles.headlineTranslated: Leishmaniasis in Rio Branco: Health alerts about the disease and guides residents.
articles.summary: Leishmaniasis in Rio Branco, Acre, Brazil, manifests in two main forms: cutaneous and mucosal. The disease is caused by Leishmania parasites and is transmitted by the sandfly Birigui, which becomes infected after biting wildlife and then transmits to humans. In Rio Branco it is predominantly rural, forested, and riverside, where vectors and wildlife reservoirs are abundant. Symptoms include painless skin lesions that can appear anywhere on the body, including the nose; some lesions may itch and are slow to heal. After a positive diagnosis, a treatment protocol is initiated and the full course is provided free by the SUS. Semsa advises that suspicion should prompt immediate medical care at the nearest URAP, emphasizing early diagnosis and free treatment in the public system.

articles.headline: Surto gastrointestinal faz 8 escolas do RS suspenderem aulas; mais de 60 crianças têm sintomas
articles.headlineTranslated: Gastrointestinal outbreak prompts 8 schools in Rio Grande do Sul to suspend classes; more than 60 children have symptoms.
articles.summary: Gastrointestinal outbreak in Pelotas, southern Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, prompts eight municipal schools to suspend in-person classes as of March 18, 2026. At least 61 children have reported symptoms in recent weeks, with cases initially concentrated in five schools and later across eight institutions. The municipal Health Secretariat halted classes until March 23 to enable reinforced hygiene measures. Cleaning across affected units will use chlorine-based products, effective against viruses but requiring the absence of students and staff due to toxicity risk. The state public health laboratory Lacen is analyzing samples collected from the affected units, with results expected in the coming days. No specific pathogen description is provided; authorities are monitoring the situation and conducting laboratory confirmation to identify the viral agent and potential infection source.

articles.headline: Paraná reforça combate à gripe aviária no litoral
articles.headlineTranslated: Paraná strengthens the fight against avian influenza along the coast.
articles.summary: Paraná launches new operation against Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza along the state's coast from March 17 to March 27, 2026, centered in Pontal do Paraná at UFPR's Marine Studies Center. Led by Adapar and veterinarians from Petrobras-linked Santos Basin Beach Monitoring Project, in partnership with UFPR's Ecology and Conservation Lab under IBAMA requirements, this preventive action targets coastal municipalities. Paraná reported 13 wild-bird foci of the disease in 2023; no new occurrences since. The effort aims to maintain sanitary status essential for the regional economy and public health, given Paraná accounts for the majority of Brazil's chicken meat production (over one-third of national output). Activities include farm inspections, guidance on Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza and Newcastle Disease prevention, and subsistence breeder education, with simulations and necropsies on day one. Officials emphasize routine field surveillance to mitigate risk.

articles.headline: Estância Velha prevê mais de 100 casos de dengue até final de 2026
articles.headlineTranslated: Estância Velha forecasts more than 100 dengue cases by the end of 2026.
articles.summary: Estância Velha, in Vale do Sinos, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, recorded four confirmed dengue cases in March 2026 and projects surpassing 100 by year-end, more than double 2025’s 42. Health Secretary Yuri Campos attributes the rise to the virus life cycle and circulation of multiple serotypes. The city uses ovitramp traps—made with beer barley—to attract Aedes aegypti for egg-laying, enabling monitoring and biological control. Lago Azul and Rincão dos Ilhéus are the areas with the most foci. Residential settings account for about 70% of sites, with transmission linked to water-stagnant spots such as plant pot saucers and undiscarded tires in backyards. After a surge, immunity to the circulating serotype increases temporarily; over 2–3 years cases rebound as susceptible individuals accumulate and herd immunity wanes. The 2026 forecast aligns with 2024’s total of 173 dengue cases.

Lago Azul and Rincão dos Ilhéus are the areas with the most foci. Residential settings account for about 70% of sites, with transmission linked to water-stagnant spots such as plant pot saucers and undiscarded tires in backyards. After a surge, immunity to the circulating serotype increases temporarily; over 2–3 years cases rebound as susceptible individuals accumulate and herd immunity wanes. The 2026 forecast aligns with 2024’s total of 173 dengue cases.

articles.headline: Infecção resistente cresce fora de hospitais e acende alerta em SP
articles.headlineTranslated: Drug-resistant infection grows outside hospitals and sparks alarm in São Paulo
articles.summary: MRSA (methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus), once confined to hospitals, is increasingly spreading in the São Paulo community, signaling a shift in the infection landscape. A decade-long analysis of over 51,000 laboratory exams from hundreds of health facilities, published in Research Connections (Oxford University Press) in 2026, confirms MRSA transmission outside hospital settings as an emerging public health challenge. Staphylococcus aureus is common on skin and in the upper airways; some variants resist antibiotics such as methicillin, making standard treatments more difficult. Infections range from mild skin conditions to bloodstream infections in severe cases. Community circulation elevates overall exposure, including among people without evident risk factors. Antimicrobial resistance remains a global crisis; the report calls for enhanced community surveillance, better monitoring, and targeted control measures, alongside policy and individual behavior adaptations to curb spread.

articles.headline: Escola vira hospital na 'guerra' contra chikungunya em aldeias
articles.headlineTranslated: A school becomes a hospital in the 'war' against Chikungunya in villages.
articles.summary: Chikungunya outbreak escalates in Jaguapiru and Bororó, Dourados, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil. A field hospital was opened at Indigenous Tengatui Marangatu School in Jaguapiru on Mar 17, operating 7:00–19:00 with SESAI and HU-UFGD staff; teams from Campo Grande and Caarapó joined. Day one saw about 80 patients; Mar 18 visits declined due to rain as health workers intensified household searches for fever, muscle and joint pain, and nausea. Four deaths occurred, all in Jaguapiru. Jaguapiru has 407 notified, 202 confirmed, 181 under investigation, 24 discarded; Dourados urban area 912 notified, 379 confirmed, no deaths. Campaigns include 4,319 properties inspected, 2,173 treated, 1,004 breeding sites identified (mainly in water tanks, trash, tires), 43 properties sprayed; 86 endemic agents and 29 indigenous health agents mobilized; LECO insecticide used. Força Nacional do SUS to reinforce starting Mar 19 for Jaguapiru and Bororó. School closures in Jaguapiru; Tengatui staff symptomatic; calendar later normal.

articles.headline: Vigilância explica motivos para suspensão de aulas em Pelotas: "Cortar a cadeia de transmissão" | Zona Sul
articles.headlineTranslated: Surveillance explains reasons for suspension of classes in Pelotas: "To cut the chain of transmission" | South Zone
articles.summary: Pelotas, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, suspends municipal classes through Monday the 23rd due to a gastrointestinal illness outbreak primarily affecting children under five. The Epidemiological Surveillance reports at least 61 symptomatic children across five schools, with eight institutions having cases. Norovirus is suspected, but confirmation from the State Central Laboratory (Lacen) is pending; identifying the exact pathogen is not the priority, as the aim is to interrupt transmission. Symptoms include vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal discomfort; fever has not been reported. School closure allows disinfection with chlorine-based products and reduces student contact, though family cooperation is crucial to prevent recontamination. The suspension applies only to municipal schools; state and private schools remain open, but cases should still be reported to health authorities.

articles.headlineTranslated: Confirmed Measles Case Raises Alarm Over Vaccination Coverage
articles.summary: Measles outbreak in Brazil raises vaccination concerns. A confirmed infant case in São Paulo marks the first measles case in the country this year; last year Brazil reported 38 infections, mostly imported. Brazil retains the PAHO measles-free area certificate (2024), a status previously earned in 2016 and lost in 2019 after imported outbreaks. In the Americas, last year saw 14,891 cases across 14 countries with 29 deaths; by March 5 this year, 7,145 infections had been confirmed, nearly half of 2024’s total in just two months, with Mexico, the United States, and Guatemala hardest hit. Most cases occur in unvaccinated individuals, especially children under 1 year. Vaccination guidance: ages 5–29 require two doses (one month apart); ages 30–59 require one dose; pregnancy and immunocompromised individuals should not be vaccinated. Symptoms include fever and red rash, plus cough, runny nose, and conjunctivitis; measles can suppress the immune system for 3–6 months.

articles.headline: Porto Nacional inicia vacinação contra dengue em adolescentes de 10 a 14 anos
articles.headlineTranslated: Porto Nacional begins dengue vaccination for adolescents aged 10 to 14 years.
articles.summary: Porto Nacional, Brazil, launched a dengue vaccination campaign for adolescents aged 10–14 on 2026-03-18, using Takeda's dengue vaccine. In this first phase, 300 doses are available across all Basic Health Units in Porto Nacional and the districts of Luzimangues, Escola Brasil, and Nova Pinheirópolis. The two-dose regimen is administered 90 days apart. Health Secretary Cristiane Nunes urged parents to vaccinate their children, noting the vaccine is a powerful tool but does not replace basic prevention. Thayane Karla, Director of Health Surveillance, emphasized that eliminating standing water and reducing mosquito breeding sites remain essential, highlighting collective responsibility to combat dengue. Doses are accessible at local UBS clinics for youths aged 10–14.

articles.headline: Felipeh Campos é internado com dengue grave e Band perde titular do "Melhor da Noite" , nesta semana
articles.headlineTranslated: Felipeh Campos is hospitalized with severe dengue, and Band loses the host of 'Melhor da Noite' this week.
articles.summary: On March 18, 2026, Brazilian television host Felipeh Campos was hospitalized at Beneficência Portuguesa in São Paulo after a severe dengue episode. Platelet count dropped to 25,000, signaling a critical condition requiring close clinical monitoring. He is under medical evaluation and off-air from Band's Melhor da Noite. The report emphasizes the seriousness of the dengue case and the immediate production impact, with Campos as a central figure unable to participate on the program. No infection source, lab confirmation details beyond the platelet count are provided. The incident highlights how severe dengue can disrupt public-facing media programs in Brazil, with ongoing treatment and uncertainty about when he will return to duty.

articles.headline: Cresce o número de focos do mosquito aedes aegypti em Rio Grande
articles.headlineTranslated: The number of Aedes aegypti mosquito foci is rising in Rio Grande.
articles.summary: Rio Grande, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, faces a rising number of Aedes aegypti foci, fueling dengue risk. The municipal epidemiological bulletin reports 26 new foci this week, bringing 2026 total to 154. Most are in the Industrial District (36) and Downtown (Centro) with 35 in the latter; access restrictions hamper control efforts as many residences are closed or unoccupied and residents refuse entry to vector-control teams. Health authorities note that even with ovitraps and larvicidal disseminating stations (EDLs), in-home inspections are essential to identify hidden breeding sites. Property owners are responsible for closed properties, and outdoor areas such as yards, water tanks, drains, and pools must be checked. No dengue cases have been confirmed in Rio Grande, though 28 suspected cases exist (26 ruled out, 2 under analysis). In Rio Grande do Sul, confirmed cases reach 257 this week. WhatsApp tip/visit line: (53) 32337289.

articles.headlineTranslated: Outbreak of swine fever in Piauí leads to the slaughter of 17 animals as the Northeast discusses eradication of the disease | Agrimidia
articles.summary: Classical swine fever outbreak in Pedro II, northern Piauí, Brazil, prompted the culling of 17 pigs after confirmation on February 26. The eradication effort by the State Agricultural Defense Agency (Adapi) included slaughtering exposed animals, complete area disinfection, and proper carcass disposal under sanitary norms. Following the focus, technical teams intensified surveillance in nearby properties to rapidly detect new cases, recognizing that spread hinges on animal movements and biosafety lapses. The outbreak poses no risk to human health but has direct economic impacts on pig production and triggers sanitary restrictions in affected zones. Representatives of Northeast state veterinary services met in Recife to advance the Brazil Plan for the Eradication of Classical Swine Fever (Plano Brasil Livre de Peste Suína Clássica), aiming to standardize protocols, bolster surveillance, and coordinate actions across northeastern states to reduce regional spread and market barriers.

articles.headline: São Leopoldo é destaque em estudo sobre a tuberculose | abc+
articles.headlineTranslated: São Leopoldo is featured in a tuberculosis study | abc+
articles.summary: São Leopoldo, Brazil, leads the national Estudo GXT on pediatric tuberculosis, with 121 participants and sole top position in February. The city joined in 2022 via a technical cooperation between Hospital Moinhos de Vento and the Ministry of Health through PROADI-SUS. The study targets children under 10, validating GeneXpert rapid molecular testing and AI-assisted chest X-ray analysis for TB detection. Nationally, Estudo GXT has enrolled 535 of 681 participants (78.6%). São Leopoldo also reports data quality: 94.4% of records monitored, 94% of participants closely followed. Other centers include Viamão (77), Sapiranga (70), Manaus (61), and Rio de Janeiro (59). Pediatric TB remains challenging due to difficulties in sputum collection, making modern diagnostics critical; the effort supports early diagnosis and prevention in the municipal network.

articles.headline: Vigilância Sanitária encontra pragas em pizzaria na Paraíba após morte e surto de intoxicação
articles.headlineTranslated: Sanitary inspectors find pests at a pizzeria in Paraíba after a death and a poisoning outbreak.
articles.summary: Pombal, Paraíba, Brazil: Agevisa sanitary inspectors found pests and structural irregularities at a local pizzeria after a deadly outbreak of foodborne illness. One death: a 44-year-old woman, and 113 others sought emergency care with diarrhea and intense vomiting after consuming products from the establishment. Investigations cited inadequate food storage, exposed electrical installations, improper thermal conditions for preserving inputs, and absence of mandatory operating documentation. The outbreak mobilized Regional Hospital of Pombal and the local urgent care unit from the start of the week. The patient died after rapid clinical deterioration, transferred to ICU in critical condition before death. The Municipal Health Council and Civil Police monitor the case; the pizzeria issued a statement expressing solidarity and cooperating with Health Surveillance and Civil Police, supplying samples and documents. Authorities treat it as a priority given the high harm potential and number of victims.

articles.headline: O sinal inconfundível que diferencia chikungunya de outros vírus
articles.headlineTranslated: The unmistakable sign that distinguishes Chikungunya from other viruses.
articles.summary: Chikungunya is characterized by incapacitating joint pain and swelling, especially in knees, ankles, and wrists, causing mobility difficulties. The illness progresses in three phases: febrile (about 5–14 days), post-acute (days 15–90), and chronic (>90 days) when arthralgia may persist, with more than 50% of cases not fully resolving after the acute phase. Compared with dengue, which features high fever (39–40 C), sudden onset, headache, and retro-orbital pain but lacks intense, long-lasting joint involvement; and Zika, which typically has low or absent fever with an early itchy rash. Oropouche mimics dengue symptoms (headache, muscle pain) but usually does not cause chronic joint pain. Clinicians should suspect chikungunya with severe, swollen joints and movement difficulty in areas where the virus circulates. Accurate diagnosis is essential for proper management and monitoring of possible chronic disease.

articles.headlineTranslated: Warning About Sustained Transmission of Yellow Fever in South America - Prensa Latina News
articles.summary: Yellow fever warning: sustained transmission risk in South America. The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) alert notes that since late 2025 human cases have emerged in areas without recent transmission and outside known risk zones, including São Paulo in Brazil and Tolima in Colombia. Proximity to centers raises the risk of transmission via Aedes aegypti, with potential outbreaks. In 2025, 346 confirmed cases and 143 deaths were reported across Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Peru, and Venezuela. In seven weeks of 2026, 34 cases and 15 deaths were confirmed in Bolivia, Colombia, Peru, and Venezuela. The disease is viral, with no specific treatment; vaccination is the most effective prevention, and a single dose provides lifelong protection. Most 2025–2026 cases occurred in unvaccinated individuals. PAHO urges stronger surveillance, expanded vaccination campaigns for at‑risk populations, traveler vaccination information, reinforced health system capacity for early detection and clinical management, and vaccine stockpiling.

articles.headline: Mutirão contra a dengue em Curitiba: veja o que deve e o que não pode ser coletado
articles.headlineTranslated: Dengue Control Drive in Curitiba: See What Should Be Collected and What Cannot Be Collected.
articles.summary: Dengue control drive in Curitiba continues this week under the Curitiba sem Mosquito program. In Curitiba, Brazil, regional teams CIC and Matriz run mutirões to educate residents and remove debris to curb mosquito breeding, with municipal trucks handling disposal. On Wednesday, 18 March, the operation visited the Augusta Health Unit area (Rua Robert Redzimski, 921 – CIC). Teams will cover about 30 blocks, with collection scheduled for Thursday, 19 March. On Thursday, Curitiba Sem Mosquito also operates in Regional Matriz, targeting 24 blocks near Jardim Botânico (Rua Engenheiro Ostoja Roguski). Residents will receive guidance on 19 March, with collection set for 24 March. What is collected: nonfunctional furniture, appliances, bulky debris, recyclable materials (glass bottles, plastics, ferrous/metal containers), tires, and organic waste and vegetative matter if bagged. What is not collected: heavy civil construction waste, unbagged organics, toxic/hazardous items (lamps, medicines, batteries, paints) and vehicles.

articles.headline: Tragedia en una pizzería: una mujer murió y más de 100 personas terminaron intoxicadas
articles.headlineTranslated: Tragedy at a pizzeria: a woman died and more than 100 people were poisoned.
articles.summary: Food poisoning outbreak linked to La Favoritta pizzeria in Pombal, Paraíba, Brazil, sickened 118 patrons between March 15–17, 2026, who sought urgent care for nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, and malaise. One death occurred: Raíssa Maritein Bezerra e Silva, 44, an agronomist and public official, died March 17 after rapid clinical deterioration and ICU admission. Two others remain hospitalized in guarded condition, including an eight-year-old girl and a woman. Agevisa closed the pizzeria after an inspection found insects, improper food storage, hygiene failures, inadequate temperature control, oxidized equipment, and reuse of containers. Civil Police opened an investigation into the deaths and illnesses. The owner apologized and provided CCTV footage; his attorney argued no edible products or handling materials were found and bacteria could be unseen.

articles.headline: Formação nacional reúne lideranças e reforça enfrentamento da malária em áreas indígenas
articles.headlineTranslated: National training brings together leaders and reinforces the fight against malaria in indigenous areas.
articles.summary: Malaria elimination leadership course in Brasília, 17-19 March 2026, brings together managers, health professionals, and partner institutions to align strategies for malaria control in indigenous areas. Representing Amazonas's Fundação de Vigilância em Saúde (FVS-RCP) is Myrna Barata, head of Malaria and Hemoparasites at the Environmental Surveillance Directorate; the course is designed to strengthen surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment, enable early case identification, and implement more effective measures in priority territories. Amazonas authorities emphasize that malaria remains a significant challenge in indigenous regions, and leadership training and regional integration are key for reducing cases. Regions of particular focus within Amazonas include Alto Rio Negro, Vale do Javari, and Alto Solimões. The initiative supports integrated health surveillance aimed at reducing transmission and advancing elimination efforts in vulnerable areas. Event participants discuss public policies, integrated surveillance, diagnostics, treatment, entomology, and health education.

articles.headline: 6 anos do 1º caso de covid-19 em Maringá: histórias, perdas e lições que a pandemia deixou
articles.headlineTranslated: Six years since the first COVID-19 case in Maringá: stories, losses, and lessons the pandemic left behind.
articles.summary: On March 18, 2020, Maringá, Paraná, Brazil, confirmed its first COVID-19 case, prompting a public health emergency and a near-month lockdown. The initial patient was a 46-year-old woman who had arrived from Spain on March 11; symptoms appeared March 17 and she was hospitalized March 18, recovering at home due to a mild course despite rheumatoid arthritis. Her 84-year-old father, with comorbidities, died March 26, the first COVID-19 death in Maringá. Rosângela Machado, 54, was Paraná’s first COVID-19 fatality, registered March 25 and dying about five days later. By year-end, Maringá recorded 172,129 infections and over 1,800 deaths among residents. Vaccination began January 19, 2021, with Ana Paula de Oliveira Machado as the first recipient; health workers prioritized, then older groups. Since 2024, vaccines have been part of routine schedules for children 6 months–<5 years, with 2025 expansion to pregnant individuals and adults 60+.

articles.headline: Mpox aumenta no Brasil e reacende alerta para monitoramento e vigilância
articles.headlineTranslated: Mpox on the Rise in Brazil and Reignites the Alert for Monitoring and Surveillance.
articles.summary: Mpox cases rise in Brazil in early 2026, with 140 confirmed and 9 suspected nationwide as of 18 March 2026. São Paulo state accounts for 93 cases; notifications span Amazonas, Ceará, Minas Gerais, Pará, Paraná, Rio de Janeiro, Rio Grande do Norte, Rondônia, Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina, Sergipe, Tocantins, and the Federal District. Mpox is a viral infection causing fever, malaise, lymphadenopathy, and skin lesions that crust over. Transmission occurs mainly through direct contact with skin lesions, close physical contact, and sharing contaminated objects. Most recent cases have been mild to moderate; no deaths reported in 2026 so far. Rapid testing is decisive: molecular confirmation via real-time PCR detects viral DNA with high sensitivity and specificity and feeds surveillance systems, enabling faster isolation and targeted public health actions. Early detection accelerates response and containment.

articles.headline: Saúde de Volta Redonda promove ações pelo Dia Mundial de Combate à Tuberculose
articles.headlineTranslated: Volta Redonda Health Department promotes activities for World Tuberculosis Day.
articles.summary: Volta Redonda, Brazil — Ahead of World Tuberculosis Day on 24 March, the Municipal Health Department (SMS) and the Infectious Diseases Center (CDI) are conducting March educational actions to inform the public about TB signs, prevention, early diagnosis, and timely treatment. Early activities occurred at Specialized Care units Policlínicas da Mulher, da Cidadania e da Melhor Idade. Approximately 144 TB patients are under treatment in the municipal network. Since 2023, Volta Redonda has decentralized TB care into Primary Health Care via Unidades Básicas de Saúde, with free medications and SUS-based sputum diagnosis; complex cases are referred to the CDI. TB treatment lasts about six months and requires adherence to prevent relapse or resistance. On 24 March, Dia T will mobilize all health units for education, and the Emergency network will receive training to improve early case identification and management.

articles.headline: Gestão de riscos amplia eficiência do controle de Salmonella na suinocultura
articles.headlineTranslated: Risk Management Enhances the Effectiveness of Salmonella Control in Swine Production.
articles.summary: Salmonella control in the pork supply chain will be discussed at the symposium "Salmonella: the invisible challenge—Multispecies strategies for a safe future in food," held March 18–19, 2026 in Toledo, Paraná, Brazil. Representives from poultry, swine, and fish sectors will review prevention, sanitary control, and risk-management approaches spanning farm to table. Luís Gustavo Corbellini, CEO of Corb Science Solutions, argues that effective Salmonella control in swine production requires moving beyond traditional compliance to an integrated farm-to-table risk-management framework. He identifies critical points along the chain, including heterogeneity of carrier animals, environmental and feed factors that sustain the pathogen, and operational factors influencing carcass contamination at slaughter. The program emphasizes converting monitoring results—supplier analyses, raw materials, lots, environment and abattoir data—into interpretable risk signals to drive proactive, detective, and corrective controls with ongoing verification of effectiveness. Registration is via FACTA’s website.

articles.headline: El ECDC alerta de infección por una bacteria en pacientes que viajan a Cabo Verde
articles.headlineTranslated: The ECDC warns of a bacterial infection in patients traveling to Cape Verde.
articles.summary: Shigellosis and other gastrointestinal infections threaten travelers to Cabo Verde. Between 2022 and March 2026, 13 EU countries, the United Kingdom, and the United States reported 766 confirmed or probable Shigella infections in travelers returning from Cabo Verde. In the same period, over 300 additional confirmed or probable cases of other GI infections—salmonellosis, campylobacteriosis, giardiasis, cryptosporidiosis, yersiniosis, amebiasis, and STEC/EIEC—were documented. No cases have been reported in Spain to date. Transmission is likely food- or water-borne, with fecal-oral spread and potential secondary cases in households, nurseries, and healthcare facilities; Shigella’s low infectious dose facilitates spread. Most cases occurred among guests at the same hotel chain in Santa Maria, Sal Island. Travelers should practice hand hygiene, eat thoroughly cooked foods, avoid unwashed produce and ice, and drink bottled or boiled water. Seek medical care for diarrhea, fever, or abdominal cramps; clinicians should heighten surveillance and ensure diagnostics, reporting, and pre-travel advice.

articles.headline: Caso de bebê com sarampo em SP acende alerta para a vacinação no Brasil
articles.headlineTranslated: Case of a baby with measles in São Paulo raises concerns about vaccination in Brazil.
articles.summary: Measles case in a 6-month-old infant in São Paulo, contracted during a trip to Bolivia amid an ongoing outbreak, underscores the risk of imported infections for Brazil. Brazil remains measles-free by surveillance, but rising activity in the Americas—over 7,000 cases in early 2026 and 14,891 cases with 29 deaths in 2025—heightens transmission risk with international travel. The infant is too young for vaccination, illustrating herd immunity reliance on high population coverage. In 2025, about 92.5% of children received the first dose, but only 77.9% completed the schedule on time. SUS guidance: first dose at 12 months (triple viral), second at 15 months (tetraviral); people aged 5–29 without vaccination proof should immunize; 30–59 should have at least one dose. Symptoms include fever, red rash, cough, runny nose, and conjunctivitis; pneumonia and encephalitis are possible. Brazil is boosting surveillance, border controls, and vaccination campaigns at airports and ports to prevent imported cases from triggering outbreaks.

articles.headline: Tras detectar un caso en Buenos Aires, qué dijeron sobre la "viruela del mono" en San Juan
articles.headlineTranslated: After detecting a case in Buenos Aires, what did they say about monkeypox in San Juan?
articles.summary: Monkeypox (mpox) case confirmed in Buenos Aires, Argentina, as of March 18, 2026. A 31-year-old resident of Buenos Aires City with no recent travel was laboratory-confirmed by the Ministry of Health of the Nation and is recovering favorably after outpatient care. Mpox, known since 1970 with origins in Africa and under surveillance in Argentina for years, spreads primarily via direct contact with skin or mucosal lesions, though droplets and contact with contaminated objects can occur. Symptoms include fever, muscle pain, malaise, and lymphadenopathy; skin lesions start as red spots and progress to vesicles with a depressed center, potentially appearing on feet, genital region, or oral mucosa and are often painful. Isolation until crusts detach, PPE for healthcare workers, and 24-hour contact tracing with 21-day follow-up are advised. This case fits the broader international expansion, with recent reports in the United States, Canada, Brazil, Mexico, France, Portugal, and Spain.

articles.headline: Por que a gripe muda de nome? Entenda o que é influenza e suas variantes
articles.headlineTranslated: Why does the flu change its name? Understand what influenza is and its variants.
articles.summary: Influenza is caused by influenza viruses, mainly types A and B, with type A subdivided into H1N1, H3N2, and thousands of other variants that can circulate simultaneously. Naming variants helps surveillance and annual vaccine updates. In 2026, Brazil’s InfoGripe shows SRAG (severe acute respiratory syndrome) rising in both long- and short-term trends, with 16,882 SRAG cases nationwide and 6,064 (35.9%) lab-positive for a virus. Hospitalizations are driven by rhinovirus, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and influenza A. Vaccines include trivalent and quadrivalent (tetravalent); high-dose formulations target adults 60+. In SUS, vaccination runs April–August for everyone from 6 months old, with doses produced by Instituto Butantan and updated to dominant Southern Hemisphere viruses from the previous year. The article notes that “gripe” can refer to other respiratory infections, while influenza typically presents with higher fever and body aches than colds, COVID-19, or RSV.

Hospitalizations are driven by rhinovirus, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and influenza A. Vaccines include trivalent and quadrivalent (tetravalent); high-dose formulations target adults 60+. In SUS, vaccination runs April–August for everyone from 6 months old, with doses produced by Instituto Butantan and updated to dominant Southern Hemisphere viruses from the previous year. The article notes that “gripe” can refer to other respiratory infections, while influenza typically presents with higher fever and body aches than colds, COVID-19, or RSV.

Areas: São Conrado, Batistão, Coophavila II, Universitário, Alves Pereira, and Centenário. To maximize effectiveness, residents should keep doors and windows open during spraying. The intervention targets adult mosquitoes, including females, the primary transmitters, though non-target species may be affected. Weather conditions, including rain, wind, or mist, could delay or cancel activities. The operation is led by Sesau (Municipal Health Secretariat) and the Coordenadoria de Controle de Endemias Vetoriais (CCE V). This is part of ongoing dengue-control efforts in the capital; no case counts or outbreaks are reported in the article.

articles.headline: Mesmo com mortes sob suspeita, casos de dengue desaceleram na Capital em 2026
articles.headlineTranslated: Even with deaths under suspicion, dengue cases slow down in the capital in 2026.
articles.summary: Two dengue deaths in Mato Grosso do Sul are under investigation, but Campo Grande reports controlled dengue transmission in 2026. In the first nine epidemiological weeks, Campo Grande registered 2–54 dengue cases per week, far below 2025’s levels. Statewide, 1,470 suspected dengue cases have been reported this year, including 28 in Campo Grande; last year MS recorded 8,461 confirmed cases, 533 in the Capital, and 20 deaths. Nonetheless, suspected/probable dengue rose from 254 in late February to 463 in the first week of March. The CIEVS-CG – Sesau control diagram shows Campo Grande’s transmission remains below the endemic threshold in every week analyzed. Compared with 2025, 2026 shows markedly lower totals through week 9 (examples: W1 47 vs 104; W2 54 vs 137; W9 6 vs 211; with corresponding thresholds). Separately, chikungunya has caused four deaths in MS in 2026, including a 3-month-old in Dourados, highlighting ongoing arboviral risk; weekly monitoring continues to guide prevention and control.

articles.headline: Ação integrada entre as três esferas de governo intensifica vigilância de vírus respiratórios em RO
articles.headlineTranslated: Integrated action across the three levels of government intensifies surveillance of respiratory viruses in Rondônia.
articles.summary: Integrated action across federal, state, and municipal levels intensifies respiratory virus surveillance in Rondônia, Brazil. In Porto Velho from March 16–20, technical teams from state, municipal, national, and international bodies are collaborating to enhance surveillance, diagnostic capacity, and immunization, linking sentinel influenza-like illness (ILI) surveillance with universal severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) surveillance and strengthening laboratory services. Governor Marcos Rocha emphasized that investment in surveillance and prevention enables rapid, effective responses to respiratory diseases and strengthens the public health system. Gilvander Gregorio de Lima, director-general of Agevisa/RO, noted the exercise assesses health-unit performance, identifies best practices, and refines the Mosaic Strategy Action Plan to boost respiratory virus surveillance. Luma Kubota, epidemiological surveillance manager at Agevisa/RO, described the event as a knowledge exchange to address challenges in border areas and Indigenous populations, focusing on surveillance, vaccination, and diagnostics.

articles.headline: Entenda o que causou intoxicação alimentar em mais de 100 pessoas e a morte de mulher após jantar em pizzaria
articles.headlineTranslated: Find out what caused food poisoning in more than 100 people and the death of a woman after dining at a pizzeria.
articles.summary: Food poisoning outbreak in Pombal, Paraíba, Brazil, linked to a local pizzeria, sickened 118 people from Sunday to Tuesday and caused one death. Symptoms included nausea, vomiting, severe abdominal pain, and diarrhea. Health facilities reported 44 patients at the UPA de Pombal and 74 at the Regional Hospital of Pombal; most recovered with symptomatic treatment, but 44-year-old agronomist Raíssa Maritein Bezerra e Silva died after rapid clinical deterioration and ICU admission. Authorities closed the establishment and launched a police investigation. Agevisa inspectors found significant sanitary violations: no hygiene protocols, presence of insects, poor temperature control, rusted equipment, and reuse of food vessels. Samples from the victim and foods were sent to the Laboratório Central de Saúde Pública da Paraíba for analysis, with results expected in about one week to establish cause and source. Ongoing investigations include interviewing the owner and survivors.

articles.headline: Tuberculose ganha monitoramento mais estratégico com regionalização da saúde prisional - A Tribuna News - Notícias de Campo Grande-MS
articles.headlineTranslated: Tuberculosis gains more strategic monitoring with the regionalization of prison health care.
articles.summary: Brazil regionalizes tuberculosis (TB) monitoring in its prison health system, enabling indicators to be analyzed by team, municipality, and state to boost management and interventions. Approximately 70.4% of Primary Prison Health Care teams are rated 'regular' on the TB indicator, which requires four medical or nursing consultations in six months, sputum smear checks, chest X-ray, and HIV testing to ensure timely diagnosis, adequate treatment, and interruption of transmission within facilities. Indicators are part of the Primary Health Care quality component and were presented at the National Seminar on Prison Primary Health Care; regionalization allows analysis by Federation Unit, municipality, and team. The system is in a 2026 preparatory phase with six quality items; official result counting starts January 2027. Six evaluation axes guide monitoring. Current performance shows 49.3% of teams rated 'good' and 16.5% 'excellent' in access to prison primary care; STI screening and cervical cancer prevention largely remain 'regular.' Governance strengthened by 683 co-financed eAPP, under Portaria GM/MS No. 7,799 (Aug 20, 2025).

articles.headline: Prefeitura reforça cuidados contra a dengue e orienta população em Porto Velho
articles.headlineTranslated: City Hall reinforces dengue precautions and advises residents in Porto Velho.
articles.summary: Porto Velho, Rondônia, Brazil — The City Hall, via the Municipal Health Secretariat (Semusa), is intensifying Aedes aegypti control to curb dengue, Zika, and chikungunya. Field surveillance teams and community participation complement measures. The municipality uses the Rapid Indices Survey for Aedes aegypti (LIRAa) to identify high-risk areas and direct control efforts. After sampling, the second phase, Pós-LIRA, targets neighborhoods with the highest larval infestation with intensified interventions to reduce dengue cases. Emerson Torres, head of the Vector Control Division, emphasizes that field work is essential for monitoring the mosquito presence and guiding prevention. The survey covers various city regions and maps infestation levels, supporting efficient resource allocation and breeding-site elimination.

articles.headline: Bactéria resistente a medicamentos se espalha fora do ambiente hospitalar em SP, alerta novo estudo
articles.headlineTranslated: Drug-resistant bacteria are spreading outside the hospital environment in São Paulo, new study warns.
articles.summary: A 10-year study on Staphylococcus aureus in São Paulo shows MRSA spreading beyond hospitals. Analyzed from 51,000+ laboratory exams across 639 health units (hospitals, labs, primary care, emergency services) and published in Research Connections (Oxford University Press). Community MRSA infections average annual growth 3.61%, while hospital-associated MRSA cases in the state decline by 2.48% per year. Of all infections, 43% were MRSA, disproportionately affecting children and the elderly. Among non-hospital positive tests, 22% already showed antibiotic resistance. Geographically, main clusters were in central São Paulo and coastal municipalities. MRSA commonly causes skin infections but can invade bloodstream and heart, and may cause pneumonia with necrotic lung tissue. The authors call for smarter surveillance, lab data integration, stronger primary care, sentinel systems, and public policies to curb antibiotic misuse and proper disposal.

articles.headline: BH confirma caso de raiva após morcego ser encontrado morto
articles.headlineTranslated: Belo Horizonte confirms a rabies case after a bat was found dead.
articles.summary: On 2026-03-18, Belo Horizonte confirmed a rabies case after a dead bat in Diamante neighborhood, Barreiro region, tested positive by the city's zoonoses team. In response, authorities initiated a ring vaccination, immunizing dogs and cats within 300 meters of the finding to curb transmission. Health officials intensified guidance to seal gaps in homes and avoid contact with bats, alive or dead. Although rabies case numbers have fallen in recent years, this record underscores ongoing vigilance. Any contact with suspected animals—including bites, scratches, or handling—requires immediate medical evaluation, with vaccination or rabies immunoglobulin as appropriate. For domestic dogs and cats, owners should observe the animal for 10 days; if symptoms appear or the animal dies, contact zoonoses promptly. Rabies vaccines for dogs and cats remain available year-round at municipal centers and units.

articles.summary: Tuberculosis active case-finding campaign underway in Garça, São Paulo state, Brazil, as part of March Verde. Health teams will conduct screenings in plazas, companies, and institutions through March 31, prioritizing respiratory symptomatic individuals (cough for three weeks or more) and will provide guidance on the importance of rapid diagnosis to break transmission. If teams are not present, residents are advised to visit the nearest Family Health Unit (USF). TB is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Koch’s bacillus) and is primarily pulmonary but can affect other organs; transmission occurs via respiratory aerosols from untreated active cases. Symptoms include prolonged cough, late-day fever, night sweats, and weight loss. Brazil experiences about 84,000 new cases and 6,000 deaths annually. The schedule for March 18–20, 24, and 26 lists venues and times in Garça (e.g., Praça Matriz de São Pedro, NAM, CAPS AD), highlighting active outreach.”}{

articles.headline: Brusque confirma quatro casos de dengue e reforça alerta
articles.headlineTranslated: Brusque confirms four dengue cases and reinforces the alert.
articles.summary: Brusque, in the Vale do Itajaí region of Santa Catarina, Brazil, confirmed four dengue cases, triggering a heightened public health alert. Health authorities urge rapid elimination of Aedes aegypti breeding sites to curb transmission of dengue, and to reduce risks of Zika and chikungunya. Residents are advised to remove standing water from containers, ensure water-storage tanks are tightly sealed, and maintain heightened precautions in outdoor areas. Although case numbers remain limited, vector surveillance is being intensified to prevent new infections and contain spread. The response relies on strong community participation to identify and eliminate mosquito habitats, reinforce home protection measures, and sustain prevention efforts until transmission is controlled.

articles.headline: Fumacê volta aos bairros: combate à dengue depende de cada morador
articles.headlineTranslated: Fogging returns to the neighborhoods: dengue control depends on each resident.
articles.summary: Campo Grande, Brazil intensifies dengue, Zika, and chikungunya control with heavy fogging (fumacê UBV) from 16:00 to 22:00 in six neighborhoods—São Conrado, Batistão, Coophavila II, Universitário, Alves Pereira, and Centenário. The effort targets adult female Aedes aegypti, yet does not eliminate breeding sites such as standing water, clogged gutters, plant pots, and forgotten containers. Effective reduction requires residents to open doors and windows so the insecticide reaches resting mosquitoes; otherwise, hidden populations persist. Weather factors like rain, wind, or fog can pause spraying, reducing impact. Fogging is described as an emergency measure during outbreaks, while ongoing prevention relies on domestic actions and surveillance within homes and yards. The article underscores that while fumigation passes through neighborhoods, the persistent battle against dengue, Zika, and chikungunya occurs inside homes.

articles.headline: Surto de sarampo nas Américas deixa Brasil em alerta máximo para a doença
articles.headlineTranslated: Measles outbreak in the Americas puts Brazil on maximum alert for the disease.
articles.summary: Measles outbreak in the Americas triggers maximum alert in Brazil. The first 2026 measles case in Brazil was confirmed last week in São Paulo: a 6-month-old infant infected during a trip to Bolivia, which is amid a measles outbreak. In response, the Ministry of Health intensified vaccination campaigns in border areas, and Anvisa tightened inspections at airports and ports to prevent further importation and spread. The case represents an imported case linked to Bolivia. Brazil's health authorities urge keeping vaccination up to date and maintaining high coverage to avert further cases. The development underscores cross-border transmission risks of measles in the Americas and the critical role of vaccination and enhanced border/public health measures.

articles.headline: Bahia autoriza entrada forçada em imóveis para combate à dengue e outras doenças
articles.headlineTranslated: Bahia authorizes forced entry into properties to combat dengue and other diseases.
articles.summary: Bahia authorizes forced entry into public and private properties to combat dengue, chikungunya, Zika, and other vector-borne diseases and zoonoses amid imminent threats to public health as of March 18, 2026. The measure, published in the State Official Journal, allows access in cases of abandonment, absence, or refusal when entry is essential to curb disease spread, and actions must comply with legality, proportionality, and reasonableness, with authorization from the state or municipal Health Surveillance authority. Prior notification via edital on the health department’s site for five days is required. Execution may be carried out by Endemic Disease Control Agents (ACE) and health surveillance staff, with police or municipal guard support if needed. In occupied residential properties, entry is limited to exterior areas; in abandoned buildings, interior access is permitted to eliminate breeding sites (e.g., water containers). Actions are documented in a forcible-entry report and a detailed circumstance report.

articles.headline: Bactéria resistente a medicamentos se espalha fora do ambiente hospitalar em SP, alerta novo estudo
articles.headlineTranslated: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria spread outside the hospital setting in São Paulo, new study warns.
articles.summary: Staphylococcus aureus, including methicillin-resistant strains (MRSA), is spreading beyond hospitals in São Paulo state. A decade-long study analyzing over 51,000 laboratory tests across 639 health units found community MRSA infections rising an average of 3.61% per year, while hospital-associated MRSA cases declined by 2.48% annually. Of infections identified outside hospitals, 43% were MRSA, disproportionately affecting vulnerable groups such as children and the elderly. Among non-hospital positives, 22% already showed antibiotic resistance. Most infection clusters were located in central São Paulo city and coastal municipalities. While MRSA commonly causes skin infections, it can also enter the bloodstream, causing severe sepsis, endocarditis, and necrotizing pneumonia. The study, published in Research Connections (Oxford University Press), underscores the epidemiological risk of community-origin MRSA in urban settings.

articles.headline: Vírus respiratórios avançam no período chuvoso e acendem alerta para crianças | RDNEWS - Portal de notícias de MT
articles.headlineTranslated: Respiratory viruses advance during the rainy season and trigger a warning for children.
articles.summary: During the rainy season, respiratory viruses surge in Mato Grosso, Brazil, with Cuiabá under rising alert for Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SRAG). Infections include influenza A and B, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV/VSR), and rhinovirus; hospitalizations are increasingly linked to rhinovirus, RSV causing bronchiolitis in children under two, and influenza A across ages. The Fiocruz InfoGripe report (March 2026) places Mato Grosso among high-risk SRAG states; Cuiabá is among capitals with alert and upward trend. In 2025, Brazil recorded 43,946 SRAG cases attributable to RSV, with 82.5% in children under two; globally RSV accounts for about 3.6 million hospitalizations and 100,000 deaths annually in under-5s. Bronchiolitis symptoms include fever, cough, runny nose, wheeze, tachypnea, and possible cyanosis or apnea. Prevention centers on vaccination, hydration, ventilation, and symptom monitoring. Unimed Cuiabá offers RSV prophylaxis nirsevimabe and quadrivalent influenza vaccine, requiring ID and vaccine card.

articles.headline: Adapar inicia operação que reforça prevenção à influenza aviária no Litoral do Paraná
articles.headlineTranslated: ADAPAR launches an operation to bolster avian influenza prevention along Paraná's coast.
articles.summary: From 17 to 27 March 2026, Paraná’s Agência de Defesa Agropecuária (Adapar) launched a preventive operation against Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) along the state’s coast (Litoral). The effort involves 16 Adapar staff and veterinarians from the Santos Basin Beach Monitoring Project (PMP-BS), covering seven municipalities: Pontal do Paraná, Paranaguá, Guaratuba, Matinhos, Morretes, Antonina and Guaraqueçaba. In partnership with MAPA and PMP-BS, the activity is risk-based and preventive; Paraná recorded 13 wild-bird HPAI foci in 2023, with no new suspected cases to date. Activities include inspections of poultry properties, guidance to prevent introduction of HPAI and Newcastle disease, and sanitary education for backyard flocks. First-day actions included necropsies and simulations. Officials emphasize One Health and the importance of maintaining Paraná’s status as Brazil’s top animal-protein producer, responsible for over one-third of national chicken meat.

articles.headline: Aumento de casos de dengue e chikungunya acende alerta em Amambai
articles.headlineTranslated: Rise in Dengue and Chikungunya Cases Triggers Alert in Amambai
articles.summary: As of March 18, 2026, Amambai’s Municipal Health Secretariat, via Epidemiological Surveillance, reports a significant rise in dengue and chikungunya notifications and confirmed cases, reflecting the Mato Grosso do Sul regional trend of increased Aedes aegypti–transmitted arboviruses. In Amambai, chikungunya cases are rising and may lead to severe complications; neighboring Dourados has reported severe cases and deaths. Dengue symptoms include high fever, headache, retro-orbital pain, body and joint pains, and a red rash; chikungunya features fever, severe joint pain and swelling, fatigue, and rash. Authorities have intensified measures: home visits by endemic agents, case investigation and outbreak control, actions in schools and health units, elimination of breeding sites, and community education with ongoing monitoring. About 80% of breeding sites are inside residences, so residents should remove standing water, keep water tanks closed, clean gutters and drains, avoid trash buildup, and place sand in plant saucers. Community participation is essential.

articles.headline: Woman, 44, dies and 117 fall ill after eating at pizzeria | Need To Know
articles.headlineTranslated: Woman, 44, dies and 117 falls ill after eating at pizzeria | Need To Know
articles.summary: Food poisoning outbreak linked to a pizzeria in Pombal, Paraíba, Brazil, after dining on Sunday 15 Mar. A 44-year-old woman, Rayssa Maritein Bezerra e Silva, died in hospital on 17 Mar after initially experiencing diarrhoea, vomiting and abdominal pain; she deteriorated and required ICU care. A further 117 people sought medical attention in Pombal with similar symptoms (nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, malaise) after eating at the same pizzeria. The establishment was shut down; an inspection found insects, improperly stored food and other irregularities. Police will conduct investigations with laboratory tests on ingredients from the pizzeria and on Rayssa's body. Two people remain in hospital: an eight-year-old child and a woman. Rayssa, an agronomist, worked for the local council's environment department; her death has prompted calls for justice.

articles.headline: OMS alerta sobre nova variante da mpox e falha do antiviral
articles.headlineTranslated: WHO warns about a new mpox variant and antiviral failure.
articles.summary: New mpox (monkeypox) recombinant strain identified; the World Health Organization says the variant merges genetic material from two mpox lineages, raising concerns about undetected circulation and implications for surveillance and diagnostics. Separately, a February 25, 2026 study in The New England Journal of Medicine finds that the antiviral most commonly used to treat mpox may not confer meaningful benefit in a subset of patients, prompting questions about current treatment strategies. As of 18 March 2026, experts warn that recombination could affect exposed populations and complicate elimination efforts, underscoring the need for enhanced genomic tracking and cautious interpretation of antiviral efficacy. The report does not provide country-specific case counts or outbreak details, but signals an urgent call for vigilance and ongoing mpox research and management.

articles.headline: BH confirma primeiro caso de raiva em 2026 e reforça vacinação de animais " BH 24 Horas
articles.headlineTranslated: Belo Horizonte confirms first case of rabies in 2026 and reinforces animal vaccination "BH 24 Horas"
articles.summary: Belo Horizonte reports the first rabies case of 2026 after a dead bat in the Diamante neighborhood, Barreiro region, tested positive. Municipal Zoonoses collected the bat and laboratory confirmation established rabies. The Municipal Health Secretariat launched a 300-meter vaccination blockade for dogs and cats around the discovery site and issued guidance to residents on preventing bats entering homes. This is the year's first case; in 2024, 28 bats tested rabid, and in 2025, 21 did. Health authorities advise anyone exposed to potential vectors—bats, dogs, or cats—to seek evaluation at a health center for possible vaccine or serum. If a owned dog or cat bites someone, the animal should be observed for 10 days; if it becomes ill, disappears, or dies, Zoonoses must be notified. Rabies vaccination is available year-round at five Sterilization Centers and at the Zoonoses Control Center; addresses and hours are listed on the city site.

articles.headline: Brasil entra em alerta máximo por surtos de sarampo na América
articles.headlineTranslated: Brazil goes on high alert over measles outbreaks in the Americas.
articles.summary: Brazil remains on high alert for measles amid rising outbreaks across the Americas. Although holding a measles-free certificate since November 2024, Brazil faces import risk: in 2025, 14,891 measles cases were reported in 14 American countries with 29 deaths; by March 5, 2026, an additional 7,145 infections were confirmed. The first measles case of 2026 in Brazil was a six-month-old in São Paulo who contracted the virus during travel to Bolivia, which is experiencing an outbreak. Authorities stress there is no sustained domestic transmission yet. The strategy to preserve status includes active surveillance and expanded vaccination. SUS provides two doses (12 months and 15 months); first-dose uptake reached 92.5% in 2024, with 77.9% completing on time last year. People up to 59 without two doses should immunize. Anvisa issued airport/port guidance; border regions are prioritized. Global travel, including World Cup USA, Mexico, Canada, may heighten import risk; Gatti cited challenges.
