articles.headline: Com surto de chikungunya, aldeias fecham escolas na Reserva Indígena de Dourados
articles.headlineTranslated: Amid a chikungunya outbreak, villages close schools in the Dourados Indigenous Reserve.
articles.summary: Chikungunya outbreak in the Dourados Indigenous Reserve, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, has caused four deaths and widespread illness, fueling debate over school closures. Indigenous leaders say four RID schools were suspended as of March 18, while the municipality denies an official closure and will seek a joint decision with the Ministry of Health on declaring a sanitary emergency. The Força Nacional do SUS arrives to assess epidemiology and assist in emergency decisions; from March 19, teams will intensify door-to-door mosquito control targeting Aedes aegypti to curb arboviruses such as dengue and Zika. At Guateka Marçal de Souza Indigenous School, ~20 staff and ~10% of students have chikungunya symptoms; Tengatiu Magangatu reports many admin staff and ~30% of students symptomatic; other schools report similar morbidity. The fourth chikungunya death in Dourados was confirmed March 17: a 60-year-old woman with comorbidity, a 3-month-old infant, and two elderly residents (69 and 73).

articles.headline: Saúde está em alerta máximo por aumento do sarampo nas Américas
articles.headlineTranslated: Health on high alert due to measles surge in the Americas.
articles.summary: Measles surge prompts Brazil to maximum alert as Americas face ongoing outbreaks. In 2025, 14,891 measles cases were reported across 14 American countries with 29 deaths; by March 5, 2026, 7,145 infections were confirmed in the region. Brazil’s first 2026 case was a 6‑month‑old infant in São Paulo who contracted the disease during travel to Bolivia, which is experiencing an outbreak. Despite 38 cases in Brazil in 2025, the country remains officially measles‑free with no sustained transmission, though vaccination is emphasized to preserve status. Immunization follows two doses: first at 12 months (part of the triple viral) and second at 15 months (tetraviral); 2025 coverage was 92.5% for the first dose and 77.9% for completing the schedule on time. Implemented measures include rapid contact tracing, vaccination of contacts (dose zero for 6–12 months), active case finding, and three‑month post‑case monitoring. Travel risk is noted ahead of World Cup travel to North America (USA, Mexico, Canada); Anvisa campaigns target airports and border areas such as coastal regions, Amazon, Pantanal, and Foz do Iguaçu.

articles.headline: Alerta de sarampo cresce nas Américas e preocupa o Brasil - Boca do Povo News
articles.headlineTranslated: Measles alert grows across the Americas and raises concerns for Brazil
articles.summary: Measles outbreaks intensify across the Americas in 2026, with 7,145 infections reported in just over two months—roughly half of 2025's 14,891 cases, which included 29 deaths across 14 countries. Brazil remains measles-free with no sustained transmission since 2024, but reports its first case of the year in a six-month-old infant in São Paulo who contracted the virus during travel to Bolivia, amid a Bolivian outbreak. The Ministry of Health is boosting surveillance, implementing ring vaccination and immunization campaigns, especially along border areas. Vaccination remains the principal defense, with two doses scheduled for children. Authorities warn that increased international travel and major events may spread the virus, stressing the population to stay up to date with vaccination to prevent new outbreaks in Brazil and the region.

articles.headlineTranslated: Woman dies and more than 100 people go to hospital after eating at a pizzeria
articles.summary: An outbreak of food poisoning linked to a pizzeria in Pombal, Sertão da Paraíba, Brazil, has left one woman dead and 113 people seeking medical care between Sunday 15 and Tuesday 17 March 2026. The 44-year-old victim was admitted to Hospital Regional de Pombal with diarrhea, vomiting, and abdominal pain; she rapidly deteriorated and died after transfer to ICU. In parallel, 40 people were treated at the Emergency Care Unit (UPA) by Tuesday morning, and 74 others were admitted to the regional hospital (36 on Sunday, 38 on Monday), totaling 114 related cases. The pizzeria was closed by the municipal Sanitation Surveillance authority, with food and inputs seized for laboratory analysis. State Health Surveillance teams are assisting investigations; the establishment’s defense says inspections are ongoing. No confirmed pathogen or infection source is stated in the article.

articles.headline: SUS e prefeitura avaliam emergência sanitária em Dourados por chikungunya
articles.headlineTranslated: SUS and the city hall evaluate a public health emergency in Dourados due to chikungunya.
articles.summary: Chikungunya outbreak in Dourados, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, has caused four deaths among residents of the city’s Indigenous Reserve (Aldeia Jaguapiru and Aldeia Bororó). The deceased include a 60-year-old woman with comorbidities, a three-month-old infant, and elderly individuals aged 69 and 73. As of March 17, the state reported 2,639 probable chikungunya cases, up from 2,446 on March 7, with an incidence of 90.2 per 100,000; Mato Grosso do Sul leads national incidence (Brazil overall 7.8). Campo Grande has no suspected cases. Authorities are evaluating a Public Health Emergency decree for Dourados to enable intensified actions, including potential temporary school closures in the Indigenous reserve. From March 19, the National SUS Force will reinforce vector-control mutirões with door-to-door visits to eliminate Aedes aegypti breeding sites; ovitrampas are being installed and health education is underway by Indigenous agents. The reserve spans ~3,500 hectares and hosts over 15,000 residents.

articles.headline: Equipes de combate à dengue poderão entrar em imóveis públicos e privados na Bahia; entenda medida
articles.headlineTranslated: Dengue-control teams may enter public and private properties in Bahia; understand the measure.
articles.summary: On 18 March 2026, the Government of Bahia authorized SESAB vector-control teams to enter public and private properties in situations of imminent risk to public health to combat arboviruses such as dengue, Zika, and chikungunya. Portaria No. 240, published in the Diário Oficial do Estado, permits access to abandoned properties, properties without a responsible owner, or sites where access is unjustifiably refused, provided a proven health risk exists. A formal incident report, prior notice by edital, and authorization by the competent sanitary authority are required. For occupied residential properties, access is limited to exterior areas in cases of absence or access refusal; for abandoned properties, interior areas may be accessed. Actions will be conducted by vector-control agents and health-surveillance teams at municipal and state levels, with police or municipal guard support if needed. Bahia, Brazil.

articles.headline: Focos do mosquito da dengue aumentam 20% em Rio Grande em uma semana | Zona Sul
articles.headlineTranslated: Dengue mosquito hotspots increase 20% in Rio Grande in one week | South Zone
articles.summary: Dengue vigilance in Rio Grande, Brazil, shows Aedes aegypti hotspots rising 20.3% to 154 since the start of 2026, with 26 new records in the last week. The Industrial District (36) and Centro (35) harbor the most foci, followed by Vila da Quinta (18) and Cidade Nova (14). Surveillance chief Michele Menezes cited limited access to properties, resistance to trap checks, and many closed houses as factors fostering mosquito proliferation. No dengue cases are confirmed in Rio Grande yet; among 28 suspected, 26 have been ruled out and 2 remain under analysis. In Rio Grande do Sul state, confirmed dengue cases total 257 this week, signaling greater viral circulation. Vaccination with Qdenga (Takeda) has been available since February at all Basic Health Units except the Centro de Vigilância em Saúde, 8:30–11:30 and 13:30–16:30. The vaccine protects against all four serotypes and is indicated for both prior and never-infected individuals.

articles.headlineTranslated: Maximum alert: measles advances in the Americas.
articles.summary: Measles triggers maximum alert in Brazil as the Americas experience rapid spread. In 2025, the region recorded 14,891 measles cases and 29 deaths; by March 2026, total infections reached 7,145. Brazil cites international importation risk and has intensified active surveillance and vaccination campaigns to prevent internal transmission and reintroduction. A recent case involved a baby infected during international travel, highlighting import risk; Brazil remains measles-free domestically with no sustained transmission. Vaccination remains the main defense, using the measles-mumps-rubella (triple viral) vaccine with two mandatory doses at 12 months and 15 months; coverage remains a concern, prompting campaigns and vaccination for adults without documentation. Health teams act quickly: notify cases, implement vaccination blocks around contacts, and conduct active case finding with three-month regional monitoring; a 'dose zero' is given to at-risk infants. Travel and large events raise transmission risk; vigilance at airports and tourist areas is essential.

articles.headlineTranslated: Cachoeiro confirms Mpox and raises red alert.
articles.summary: Mpox has been confirmed in Cachoeiro de Itapemirim, Espírito Santo, Brazil, bringing the state's 2026 tally to three confirmed cases. The Cachoeiro patient lives in the municipality and presents fever, skin lesions, and body pains; early diagnosis is stressed to prevent complications and to guide isolation. Espírito Santo’s three 2026 cases are all men aged 20–49, with the first in Colatina, followed by a case in Serra, and now Cachoeiro. The state has about 50 notifications, most ruled out, but two cases remain under investigation, keeping surveillance active. Mpox is a viral zoonosis with human transmission mainly through contact with lesions or fluids, contaminated surfaces, and respiratory droplets. There is no specific treatment; clinicians manage symptoms. Authorities urge prompt medical care at first signs and adherence to isolation to reduce spread, per the Sesa/Mpox portal.

articles.summary: Measles case in a 6-month-old in São Paulo, Brazil, imported from Bolivia after a January trip, underscores the urgent need for high vaccination coverage. Bolivia has faced a measles outbreak since last year. The infant is ineligible for vaccination (MMR at 12 months; tetra-viral at 15 months, including varicella). Brazil achieved 92.5% first-dose coverage in 2023, but only 77.9% completed on schedule; Brazil remained PAHO-certified measles-free in 2024, losing certification in 2019 due to imported outbreaks. In the Americas, 14,891 cases were reported in 2023 across 14 countries with 29 deaths; by March 5, 2024, 7,145 infections were confirmed, led by Mexico, the United States, and Guatemala, mostly in non-vaccinated children under 1 year. Measles symptoms include fever, rash, cough, coryza, and conjunctivitis; complications include pneumonia and encephalitis. Vaccination provides lifelong protection; two doses for ages 5–29, one dose for 30–59; pregnancy and immunocompromised individuals are contraindicated.

articles.headline: Estado amplia vagas de castração de gatos para combater a esporotricose
articles.headlineTranslated: State Expands Cat Neutering Slots to Combat Sporotrichosis.
articles.summary: Paraná State expands exclusive cat sterilization slots through CastraPet Paraná to help control sporotrichosis in felines and humans. Beginning in March 2026, the program increases available surgeries by about 15% per municipality; Marmeleiro (Southwest) will add 20 operations for the drive on April 25. Since the fifth cycle began in November 2025, more than 6,000 cats have been sterilized at no cost, with this phase running through July 2026. Scheduling occurs at municipal points, where guardians receive preoperative guidance; after surgery, postoperative care, medications, and microchip implantation are provided. Officials say neutering reduces cat fights and territorial disputes that facilitate fungal transmission, supporting responsible ownership and lower infection risk. Sporotrichosis is a zoonosis causing skin ulcers in humans and animals; transmission occurs via scratches, bites, or contact with infected cats or contaminated environments.

Since the fifth cycle began in November 2025, more than 6,000 cats have been sterilized at no cost, with this phase running through July 2026. Scheduling occurs at municipal points, where guardians receive preoperative guidance; after surgery, postoperative care, medications, and microchip implantation are provided. Officials say neutering reduces cat fights and territorial disputes that facilitate fungal transmission, supporting responsible ownership and lower infection risk. Sporotrichosis is a zoonosis causing skin ulcers in humans and animals; transmission occurs via scratches, bites, or contact with infected cats or contaminated environments.

articles.headlineTranslated: Brazil on alert as measles spreads across the Americas
articles.summary: Measles alert in Brazil as the Americas see rapid spread in 2026. In just over two months, 7,145 measles cases were recorded in the region, nearly half of the 14,891 total in 2025. Brazil’s first 2026 case was a 6‑month‑old girl in São Paulo who contracted the virus during a trip to Bolivia, where an outbreak is ongoing; the infant’s age prevented vaccination. Brazil remains certified as measles-free with no sustained domestic transmission, but imported cases raise risk if coverage drops. SUS provides two doses at 12 and 15 months; in 2025, 92.5% received the first dose, 77.9% completed on time. Measures include ring vaccination, active case finding, border-area campaigns, and heightened surveillance at airports/ports. Outbreaks are centered in the United States, Mexico, and Guatemala; most cases occur among unvaccinated individuals, especially children under 1 year. Symptoms: fever, red rash, cough, runny nose, eye irritation; complications include pneumonia and encephalitis.

articles.summary: Measles case confirmed in São Paulo, Brazil, in a 6-month-old infant who traveled to Bolivia in January, renewing focus on vaccination coverage. The child is too young for Brazil's SUS schedule (first dose of MMR at 12 months; tetra viral at 15). Experts emphasize herd immunity: high vaccination reduces transmission and can sterilize infection. Last year in Brazil, 92.5% of infants received the first dose, but only 77.9% completed on time. The Americas registered 14,891 cases in 14 countries with 29 deaths last year; by March 5 this year, 7,145 cases, with Mexico, the United States, and Guatemala notably affected. Brazil remains measles-free with PAHO certification since 2024, though prior losses occurred in 2019 amid imported outbreaks. Typical symptoms include fever and red maculopapular rash, cough, coryza, and conjunctivitis; pneumonia and encephalitis are key complications, plus temporary immune suppression for 3–6 months.

articles.headline: Vigilância acha pragas em pizzaria na PA; mulher morreu e outras 113 pessoas passaram mal
articles.headlineTranslated: Public health surveillance finds pests at a pizzeria in Pará; a woman died and 113 others fell ill.
articles.summary: As of 18 March 2026, a suspected food-poisoning outbreak in Pombal, Paraíba, Brazil, linked to the La Favoritta pizza restaurant caused one death and 113 illnesses after meals there. Hospital records show 74 visits between 15–16 March for symptoms including acute gastroenteritis (stomach/intestinal inflammation) and vomiting, with 36 patients on 15 March (33 gastroenteritis, 3 vomiting) and 38 on 16 March (33 gastroenteritis, 5 vomiting, 1 suspected food poisoning). The deceased, Rayssa Maritein Bezerra (44), died 17 March at the Regional Hospital of Pombal after rapid deterioration; she had symptoms starting 15 March. The municipality closed the pizzeria after inspections found pests and multiple nonconformities (documentation gaps, improperly stored foods, exposed electricals, inadequate cooling). Civil Police investigate; Agevisa will assess samples. Toxicology exams are planned for the victim and patients to help define the cause and infection source (ingestion of pizzas from the establishment).

articles.headline: Prevenção e contingência para a Influenza Aviária em debate no RS
articles.headlineTranslated: Prevention and Contingency for Avian Influenza Under Discussion in Rio Grande do Sul
articles.summary: HPAI H5N1 has been confirmed in wild birds in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, with active containment and surveillance under way after a February-end focus at the Taim Ecological Reserve. A March 17 forum in Montenegro gathered public authorities and the aviculture sector to discuss Brazil’s and the world’s avian influenza landscape and domestic actions. Brazil maintains a strong sanitary status, exporting more than 50,000 tons of animal protein daily, and Rio Grande do Sul has mobilized since 2023, following an initial 2025 outbreak in a commercial farm; current emphasis is biosafety and intersectoral coordination under a One Health framework among Agriculture, Health, Environment, and private stakeholders. The disease’s complexity involves multiple species and wildlife interfaces; Brazil lacks a clear southern-hemisphere seasonality, though outbreaks have occurred April–August. Key biosafety points include farm location, access control, vehicle/equipment handling, wildlife intrusion, water quality, and mortality disposal. The forum attracted 212 in-person attendees and over 1,100 online viewers from various states.

articles.headline: Caso confirmado de sarampo acende alerta sobre cobertura vacinal
articles.headlineTranslated: Confirmed measles case raises alarm about vaccination coverage.
articles.summary: Measles resurgence in the Americas raises alarm over vaccination coverage. Brazil had achieved elimination certification in 2016 but lost it in 2019 after outbreaks triggered by imported cases. Last year, the region recorded 14,891 measles cases across 14 countries with 29 deaths; as of March 5, 2026, 7,145 cases have been confirmed this year, nearly half of last year's total in just two months. The burden is greatest in Mexico, the United States, and Guatemala. Most cases occur in unvaccinated individuals, especially children under 1 year. Measles is not a benign childhood illness: for each 1,000 cases the expected deaths are higher than typical; last year the Americas saw about 15,000 cases and nearly 30 deaths. Common complications include pneumonia and neurological disease such as encephalitis. The infection can cause temporary immune suppression for 3-6 months, increasing vulnerability to other infections.

articles.headline: Saúde está em alerta máximo por aumento do sarampo nas Américas
articles.headlineTranslated: Health on high alert as measles surges in the Americas.
articles.summary: Measles surges in the Americas trigger Brazil’s Health Ministry to maximum alert, with vaccination as the main defense and border-area campaigns underway. The SUS schedule mandates two measles doses: first at 12 months (as part of the triple viral vaccine) and second at 15 months (tetraviral). In 2025, Brazil logged 3,818 suspected infections; by January 26, 2026, there were 27 suspected cases nationwide. Upon confirmation, municipalities promptly notify the MoH, implement a vaccination blockade, identify all contacts, and vaccinate them; followed by active case finding—door-to-door and sweeps of laboratories and health units. With World Cup events in the United States, Mexico, and Canada potentially spreading travel-related risk, ANVISA is issuing vaccination messages at airports and ports. Domestic challenges include tourist hubs and a long land border with twin cities, underscoring the need to sustain high vaccination coverage.

articles.headline: Influenza Aviária: resposta rápida no RS evidencia força do sistema sanitário brasileiro no anuário de Avicultura Industrial | Agrimidia
articles.headlineTranslated: Avian Influenza: Rapid response in Rio Grande do Sul demonstrates the strength of Brazil's public health system in the Industrial Poultry Almanac | Agrimidia
articles.summary: Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) was laboratory-confirmed in commercial poultry in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, in May 2025. The response was rapid and coordinated, with depopulation of the affected farm completed within 12 hours, followed by cleaning and disinfection. Approximately 90 professionals were mobilized to install sanitary barriers and strengthen surveillance, aided by security forces and local authorities. Since HPAI arrived in South America in 2022, cases have been reported in Chile, Colombia, and Peru, prompting intensified monitoring in RS, especially near migratory bird corridors. Between 2023 and 2024, two wild-bird foci were identified in the Taím and Rio Pardo regions under the national contingency plan. The swift, structured response, sustained by trained teams, traceability tools, and cross-sector collaboration, preserved production and Brazil’s sanitary credibility in national and international markets, and provided strategic lessons for future outbreaks.

articles.headline: BH confirma primeiro caso de raiva em 2026 e reforça imunização
articles.headlineTranslated: BH confirms the first rabies case in 2026 and reinforces immunization.
articles.summary: Rabies confirmed in Belo Horizonte, Brazil, the first case of 2026. A bat found dead in the Diamante neighborhood, Barreiro region, tested positive for rabies, with laboratory confirmation by the municipal Zoonoses service. In response, the city launched a 300-meter vaccination block for dogs and cats around the site and issued guidance to residents on preventing home exposure to such animals. Historically, 2024 saw 28 rabid bats and 2025 saw 21. Public health authorities urge anyone with potential human exposure to rabid animals to seek medical evaluation promptly and initiate post-exposure prophylaxis if indicated. For domestic dogs or cats involved in an incident, observe the animal at home for 10 days; if it falls ill, disappears, or dies, contact Zoonoses or a health center. Rabies vaccination for dogs and cats is offered year-round at five Dog/Cat Sterilization Centers and the Zoonoses Control Center; addresses are on the city portal.

articles.headlineTranslated: Espírito Santo has three confirmed Mpox cases - ES Today
articles.summary: Three confirmed mpox cases in Espírito Santo, Brazil, as of March 18, 2026, per the state Health Secretariat bulletin. The third case involves a male resident of Cachoeiro de Itapemirim; ages affected span from 20–29 to 40–49. The first case in 2026 was reported in Colatina in January, with a second case in the Serra metropolitan region. Total notifications reach 50, with 42 discarded. Besides the three confirmed cases, two remain suspected and three are no longer monitored due to loss of contact with health authorities, hindering follow-up. Mpox (monkeypox) is transmitted person-to-person through close contact; no primates are involved. The World Health Organization renamed the disease mpox in 2022 to reduce stigma. Symptoms include fever, headache, body aches, fatigue, lymphadenopathy, and eruptive skin lesions on the face, genitals, perianal region, palms, soles, or mucous membranes; no specific antiviral treatment; care is supportive.

articles.summary: Food poisoning outbreak in Pombal, Sertão of Paraíba, Brazil, after pizza at La Favoritta. One death confirmed: Rayssa Maritein Bezerra e Silva, 44. Among 118 people seeking medical care after consuming pizza, symptoms included nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, and malaise. Medical teams at the local urgent care unit and the Regional Hospital of Pombal promptly treated patients; the deceased died around 8:59 a.m. on Tuesday, March 17, 2026, with signs compatible with a severe infectious condition. The pizza shop was interdicted by the Sanitary Surveillance authorities. Civil Police opened an inquiry to determine responsibility. The owner, Marcos Antonio Gomes Neto, 24, apologized, stating he was cooperating and sought to identify the cause, claiming no intent to harm. An attorney for the owner noted that inspections found no obviously spoiled products; possible unseen bacteria may be involved. No specific pathogen or laboratory confirmation reported.

articles.headline: Vírus respiratórios: ação reforça vigilância em RO - News Rondônia
articles.headlineTranslated: Respiratory viruses: action reinforces surveillance in Rondônia - News Rondônia
articles.summary: As of March 18, 2026, Rondônia intensifies respiratory virus surveillance via an integrated action in Porto Velho, coordinated by the State Government. The initiative brings together state, municipal, and national and international representatives to strengthen monitoring, diagnosis, and immunization, enhancing the public health response. The program analyzes indicators, service flows, vaccination coverage, and laboratory capacity, promoting integration of sentinel influenza-like illness (SG) surveillance with universal severe acute respiratory syndrome (SRAG) surveillance, aligning immunization and laboratory strategies. Agevisa notes cross-agency exchange to identify regional challenges, especially in border areas and Indigenous communities. The agenda includes technical meetings, field visits to sentinel units, hospitals, and to Policlínica Ana Adelaide, Cemetron, and Hospital Infantil Cosme e Damião, plus the Central Public Health Laboratory, with participation from the Ministry of Health and PAHO. Expected outcomes: recommendations to enhance surveillance efficiency and protect the population against respiratory diseases under the Mosaic Strategy plan.

articles.headline: Caso confirmado de sarampo acende alerta sobre cobertura vacinal
articles.headlineTranslated: A confirmed measles case raises concerns about immunization coverage.
articles.summary: First measles case of the year in Brazil involves a São Paulo infant too young for routine vaccination, who contracted measles after traveling to Bolivia in January, where an outbreak is ongoing. The case underscores the importance of high vaccination coverage to prevent imported cases from triggering local transmission, as measles is highly contagious. Brazil's first-dose coverage reached 92.5% last year, but only 77.9% completed the full schedule on time. The case follows last year's 38 confirmed infections in Brazil, mostly imported; the country remains PAHO measles-free since 2024, after losing the status in 2019 due to outbreaks. In the Americas, last year saw 14,891 cases and 29 deaths; by March 5 this year, 7,145 cases were reported, with most infections in unvaccinated individuals, especially under 1 year. Symptoms include fever, red rash, cough, and conjunctivitis; pneumonia and encephalitis are common complications, with transient immunosuppression post-infection.

articles.headline: Brasil em alerta máximo devido ao aumento de casos de sarampo nas Américas - Destak Jornal
articles.headlineTranslated: Brazil on high alert due to the rise in measles cases in the Americas - Destak Jornal
articles.summary: Measles outbreaks in the Americas push Brazil to maximum alert. In 2025 the region reported 14,891 cases and 29 deaths; by March 5, 2026, 7,145 confirmed infections. Brazil’s first 2026 case is a 6‑month‑old infant in São Paulo who contracted measles during a trip to Bolivia, which is experiencing a local outbreak. Brazil remains measles‑free since 2024 with no sustained domestic transmission, but international spread and tourism risk prompt intensified actions. Vaccination is central: border campaigns and routine immunization with two doses—first at 12 months (measles-containing vaccine as part of MMR) and second at 15 months (tetraviral). In 2024, 92.5% of infants received the first dose; 77.9% completed on time. All individuals up to 59 without two doses should immunize. Case management includes rapid notification, vaccination of contacts, active case finding, house‑to‑house vaccination, laboratory/health‑unit sweeps, and three months of monitoring; a dose zero may be given to 6–11‑month contacts. Anvisa is issuing travel vaccination messages at airports and ports, reflecting Brazil’s tourism corridors and extensive borders.

articles.headline: Fórum debate gripe aviária e reforça medidas de prevenção no RS
articles.headlineTranslated: Forum debates avian influenza and reinforces preventive measures in Rio Grande do Sul.
articles.summary: On 17 March 2026, public agencies and poultry sector representatives met in Montenegro, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, to discuss Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) H5N1, following confirmation of a focus in wild birds at the Taim Ecological Reserve in late February. The Rio Grande do Sul government said it has prepared since 2023, noting that the 2025 commercial-farm outbreak did not surprise officials. The forum aims to solidify RS as a biosafety and sanitary-control reference for poultry production, emphasizing producer-sanitary-public integration. Asgav’s president highlighted prior cooperation; Fundesa stressed Brazil’s sanitary status amid high poultry exports. Experts described the disease’s complexity and hemispheric differences in virus behavior. Daniela Pacheco Lacerda of the Ministry urged integrated action; biosafety measures on farms include access control, proper handling, and continuous monitoring. The event drew in-person and online participants from across the country.

articles.headline: Paciente com suspeita de Mpox é transferida de Brasiléia
articles.headlineTranslated: Patient with suspected Mpox is transferred from Brasiléia.
articles.summary: 56-year-old Ana Sousa da Silva was transferred on Tuesday (17) from Hospital Regional de Brasiléia to Pronto-Socorro de Rio Branco after presenting suspected Mpox symptoms. She had been admitted at Brasiléia on the 15th, where initial care was provided. Due to the suspicion of Mpox, she was sent to the state capital for a more detailed evaluation. Upon admission to Rio Branco’s emergency department, clinicians requested specific tests to investigate the possible infection. Her health status is stable, and she remains under medical observation while awaiting lab results to confirm or rule out Mpox. If confirmed, this could be the second mpox case documented in Acre's border region.

articles.headline: Prefeitura de Esperantina intensifica combate à dengue através da Secretaria Municipal de Saúde
articles.headlineTranslated: Esperantina City Hall Steps Up the Fight Against Dengue Fever Through the Municipal Health Department.
articles.summary: On 18 March 2026, Esperantina's Municipal Health Department led a dengue prevention campaign along Avenida Petrônio Portela, aiming to curb Aedes aegypti breeding and raise awareness about dengue, as well as its related diseases transmitted by the same mosquito. Health teams provided guidance, distributed informational materials, and reinforced practical daily measures to prevent standing water and mosquito proliferation. Key city officials, Secretary of Health Dérick Kawan and Mayor Ivanária Sampaio, underscored the administration's commitment to public health and disease prevention. The campaign emphasizes community participation as essential to reducing dengue risk in Esperantina, encouraging residents to keep yards clean and free of mosquito breeding sites. This effort is part of ongoing municipal actions to protect public health from vector-borne diseases in the city.

articles.headline: Global survey reveals pet owners lack awareness of parasite risks and seek clearer prevention advice
articles.summary: Heartworm remains a major canine health risk in the US, with >1.2 million dogs heartworm-positive (AVMA, 2024). Europe reports spread to new countries; in Latin America, Africa and Asia, prevalence remains high. External parasites such as ticks are widespread; Italy reports >47% of dogs infested, and Southeast Asia up to 67% of owned dogs with at least one tick. Tick-borne diseases include Lyme borreliosis (joint pain and potential kidney damage), babesiosis (destruction of red blood cells), and ehrlichiosis (fever and bleeding tendencies). Parasites can infect people, underscoring zoonotic risk. A global survey of 6,500 pet owners across the UK, US, France, Germany, Turkey, China, Japan, Mexico and Brazil finds 43% of pets with parasite infections, 75% seeking clearer prevention guidance, and 27% only slightly or not familiar with parasite risks. Veterinarians are the most trusted source (70%). On World Parasite Awareness Day (March 20), Boehringer Ingelheim launches "Small acts of love. Big moments of life" to promote simple, preventive care.

articles.headline: Bactéria resistente se espalha fora de hospitais e desafia protocolos médicos
articles.headlineTranslated: Resistant bacteria spread outside hospitals and challenge medical protocols.
articles.summary: MRSA (Staphylococcus aureus resistant to methicillin) is spreading from hospitals into communities in the São Paulo macro-region, Brazil. An analysis of 51,532 positive laboratory samples from 2011–2021 shows a shift: hospital-associated MRSA cases fell by 2.48% per year, while community-origin MRSA infections rose by 3.61% annually, and MRSA was linked to about 43% of infections examined. Roughly 22% of community samples already displayed antibiotic resistance. The highest concentration of cases was in central São Paulo city and in coastal municipalities, with factors such as population density, climate, and travel patterns possibly shaping transmission. In the Brazilian SUS, oral antibiotics with activity against MRSA are limited, potentially raising hospitalization risk and costs. Preventive measures include hand hygiene, wound care, environmental cleaning, and rational antibiotic use. Symptoms range from minor skin infections to severe pneumonia.

articles.headline: Crianças de 1 a 4 anos e idosos são os mais hospitalizados por influenza no CE; veja sintomas
articles.headlineTranslated: Children aged 1 to 4 years and the elderly are the most hospitalized for influenza in Ceará; see symptoms.
articles.summary: Influenza-associated Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SRAG) cases in Ceará, Brazil reached 236 in health facilities through epidemiological week 8 (Feb 28, 2026). Hospitalizations were highest among children 1–4 years (26.9%) and adults 70+ (22.7%), with 54.2% female; no deaths were recorded in this interval. The data show a seasonal rise in respiratory infections in early 2026 and a higher influenza burden than in 2025. Most influenza-like illness is mild; a small portion—primarily children and the elderly—progress to SRAG requiring specialized care. SRAG denotes severe evolution of a respiratory infection, with dyspnea, distress, oxygen saturation ≤ 94%, persistent fever, cough, and possible hypotension. Sesa began preparations in late 2025, including weekly bulletins, pediatric/geriatric clinical training, and guidance on oseltamivir. Last year’s vaccination coverage: children 59%, pregnant women 60%, elderly 53%. The 2026 flu vaccination campaign starts this month, with COVID-19 and pneumococcal vaccine updates and other preventive measures.

articles.headlineTranslated: Brazil enters "maximum alert" with a surge in measles cases across the Americas - News Rondônia
articles.summary: Measles outbreak triggers Brazil's 'maximum alert' as the Americas report 7,145 measles cases from Jan 1 to Mar 5, 2026, nearly half of 2025's total (14,891). Brazil records a confirmed measles case in a 6‑month‑old infant in São Paulo after travel to Bolivia, prompting emergency protocols. Despite remaining measles‑free since 2024, Brazil emphasizes preventing sustained transmission amid rising regional cases and a predicted influx of tourists ahead of the North American World Cup. Health authorities implement blocking vaccination: identify/notify contacts, active case finding, and Dose Zero—an extra vaccine dose for 6 months to 1 year olds in high‑risk areas—while preserving the 12 and 15‑month schedule. Coverage gaps persist: 2025 first‑dose uptake 92.5%, second dose 77.9%. All individuals up to 59 without vaccination proof should seek care; focus on borders and major tourism hubs like Pantanal, Amazon, and coastal areas.

Contraindications: pregnancy and immunocompromised status.

articles.summary: Measles case confirmed in a 6‑month‑old infant in São Paulo, Brazil; confirmation occurred last week. The infant had traveled to Bolivia in January, where an outbreak has persisted since last year, underscoring importation risk and the need for high vaccination coverage to protect young babies. Brazil remains measles‑free per PAHO/WHO, though last year recorded 42 locally acquired or imported cases; 2023 saw 38 imported infections. Routine vaccination remains the main prevention: first dose of the triple viral vaccine at 12 months, followed by a tetra‑viral dose at 15 months (adds varicella). In 2024, 92.5% received the first dose and 77.9% completed the schedule on time. Guidance: ages 5–29 should have two doses; ages 30–59 one dose; pregnant and immunocompromised should not be vaccinated. Imported cases can spark outbreaks if vaccination coverage declines.

articles.headline: Il fungo "mangia-pelle" che può passare dai gatti all'uomo: cos'è lo Sporothrix e perché preoccupa
articles.headlineTranslated: The "skin-eating" fungus that can pass from cats to humans: what is Sporothrix and why is it concerning.
articles.summary: Sporothrix brasiliensis, a dimorphic fungus causing sporotrichosis, raises public health concern as it passes from cats to humans. In Uruguay, confirmed cases appear in Maldonado and Rocha, triggering epidemiological surveillance. Unlike S. schenckii (soil-based), S. brasiliensis spreads mainly via cats; human infection occurs through scratches, bites, or contact with infected lesions. In cats, wounds, crusts and hair loss on the face, nose and limbs harbor high fungal loads. Over the past decade, WHO notes more than 11,000 human cases in affected areas, with Brazil the origin in the 1990s and spread to Argentina, Chile and Paraguay, and to Europe, including the United Kingdom since 2022. Europe remains rare; Italy regards it as uncommon, Bari reporting the most severe recent case not acquired from a cat. Stray cats may be reservoirs; control relies on early identification and antifungal treatment lasting weeks to months.

articles.headline: Bactéria resistente se espalha fora de hospitais - 18/03/2026 - Equilíbrio e Saúde - Folha
articles.headlineTranslated: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria spread outside hospitals.
articles.summary: MRSA (Staphylococcus aureus resistant to methicillin) is spreading from hospitals into the community in the São Paulo state macroregion, Brazil. A collaboration between Afip and Escola Paulista de Medicina da Unifesp analyzed 51,532 S. aureus–positive samples from 2011–2021, published in Research Connections (Oxford University Press). Hospital-associated MRSA shows a downward trend of 2.48% per year, while community-associated infections rise 3.61% annually. Overall, resistant S. aureus was linked to 43% of infections analyzed; community cases disproportionately affect children and the elderly. About 22% of community-associated samples already showed resistance to common antibiotics (penicillins and cephalosporins), signaling higher risk of empirical treatment failure. Maps identify the central region of São Paulo city and coastal municipalities as foci, with population density and skin infections highlighted as possible factors. Researchers urge territory-specific investigations and note a potential shift toward MRSA-directed empiric therapy in severe cases.

articles.headline: Detectan en el país la cepa más agresiva de la viruela del mono
articles.headlineTranslated: The country detects the most aggressive strain of monkeypox.
articles.summary: Argentina confirms its first Mpox clade Ib case, the most aggressive and contagious mpox variant, marking a shift from the prior clade II detections. The patient is a 31-year-old man from Buenos Aires City with no recent travel history, diagnosed March 10 after symptom onset February 24; he was treated as an outpatient and is recovering. No new linked cases identified yet; epidemiological investigation continues. By 2026, five mpox cases had been detected in Argentina, all belonging to clade II. The emergence of clade Ib signals a broader, global expansion: in the Americas, 14 cases have been reported across the United States, Canada, Brazil, Mexico, and Argentina, with community transmission reported in Europe (France, Portugal, Spain). Health authorities urge enhanced detection of symptoms (skin lesions, lymphadenopathy, fatigue, sore throat) and strengthened contact tracing to curb spread.

articles.headline: Mulher com suspeita de Mpox é transferida de Brasiléia para Rio Branco - O Alto Acre
articles.headlineTranslated: Woman with suspected Mpox is transferred from Brasiléia to Rio Branco - O Alto Acre.
articles.summary: A 56-year-old woman identified as A.S. da S. was transferred on the afternoon of 17 March 2026 from the Regional Hospital of Brasiléia to the Emergency Department in Rio Branco after presenting suspected Mpox symptoms. She had been hospitalized since 15 March in Brasiléia where initial care was provided. Due to suspicion, she was moved to the Acre capital for more detailed assessment. At Rio Branco, specific tests to investigate possible Mpox infection were ordered. Her condition remains stable, and she is under medical monitoring while awaiting laboratory results to confirm or rule out Mpox. If confirmed, this could be the second Mpox case recorded in Acre’s border region.

articles.headline: Veja perguntas e respostas sobre intoxicação alimentar de mais de 100 pessoas que comeram em pizzaria na PB; uma morreu
articles.headlineTranslated: See questions and answers about food poisoning affecting more than 100 people who ate at a pizzeria in Paraíba; one died.
articles.summary: Foodborne illness outbreak in Pombal, Sertão da Paraíba, Brazil, linked to a local pizzaria has sickened at least 117–118 people and caused one death. About 44 patients were treated at the Pombal Unidade de Pronto Atendimento on Sunday, 15 March, with nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, and malaise; 74 more were admitted to the Hospital Regional de Pombal (36 on 15 March, 38 on 16 March). An 8-year-old child remained hospitalized; a 44-year-old woman, Rayssa Maritein Bezerra e Silva, died on 17 March. The pizzaria was interdicted on 16 March; Agevisa PB found pests, insects, missing documentation, improper food storage, poor temperature control, and lack of hygiene/SOP protocols. Civil Police and health authorities will perform lab analyses of samples from the premises and the deceased; results expected in about one week. No imported/exported cases reported.

articles.headline: Ya hay ocho casos de chikungunya confirmados en Tucumán
articles.headlineTranslated: There are already eight confirmed cases of chikungunya in Tucumán.
articles.summary: Eight confirmed chikungunya cases in Tucumán, Argentina, as of 18 March 2026, all transmitted by Aedes aegypti. Three patients are in Yerba Buena; the remaining cases are concentrated in the southern part of the provincial capital. No dengue cases reported. Symptoms include fever, body aches, and severe joint pain. Health authorities have activated focal-control protocols: patient management, contact tracing, and home surveys within a 100–200 meter radius, plus fumigation and vector-control efforts to eliminate breeding sites. Officials urge early medical consultation for fever, body pains, or fatigue and reinforce prevention, especially for travel to areas with viral circulation such as Bolivia, Brazil, and Salta. Preventive measures recommended include applying repellent, using bed nets, deploying insecticide devices, and removing standing water in households.

articles.headline: Mulher morre e mais de 100 pessoas são hospitalizadas após comerem em pizzaria na Paraíba - Hugo Gloss
articles.headlineTranslated: Woman dies and more than 100 people are hospitalized after eating at a pizzeria in Paraíba - Hugo Gloss
articles.summary: Paraíba, Brazil, as of 18 March 2026, reports a likely foodborne gastroenteritis outbreak linked to a single pizzeria, with one death and 118 initial healthcare presentations. The deceased, Rayssa Maritein Bezerra e Silva, 44, progressed from diarrhea, vomiting and abdominal pain to ICU admission after initial discharge from Hospital Regional de Pombal. A total of 40 patients were treated at the Emergency Care Unit (UPA) and 74 at the Regional Hospital on Monday, with 4 more later seeking care at the UPA, totaling 118. Most patients recovered; an eight-year-old remained hospitalized. All had eaten pizza at the same establishment on Sunday night (March 15). Sanitation authorities interdicted the pizzeria; foods and inputs were collected for laboratory analysis. Agevisa coordinates the investigation; authorities urge anyone with symptoms to seek medical care.

articles.headline: Força Nacional do SUS chega em MS para conter epidemia de chikungunya
articles.headlineTranslated: National Force of the SUS arrives in Mato Grosso do Sul to contain a chikungunya epidemic.
articles.summary: Chikungunya outbreak in Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil: The National Force of the SUS arrives in Dourados on 18 March 2026 to join a task force tackling the epidemic in the Jaguapiru and Bororó Indigenous Reserves. Four deaths confirmed (three in Jaguapiru, one in Bororó, including a 3‑month‑old infant). More than 400 cases notified, with over 200 confirmed. Health teams perform triage, collect specimens, dispense medications and monitor patients; severe cases are referred to regional hospitals. The operation, coordinated with SESAI and Hospital Universitário da UFGD (administered by EBSERH), begins in the villages on 19 March 2026 and will continue as needed. Parallel mutirões target Aedes aegypti breeding sites, especially in water tanks and waste. The Jaguapiru-Bororó Reserve houses about 21,000 Indigenous people and has four basic health units, highlighting containment challenges.

articles.headline: Prefeitura inicia mutirão contra o mosquito Aedes aegypti no Petrolar
articles.headlineTranslated: City Hall launches a mosquito-control drive against the Aedes aegypti mosquito in Petrolar.
articles.summary: In Alagoinhas, Bahia, Brazil, the City Hall launched a major integrated drive in the Petrolar neighborhood to combat Aedes aegypti amid rising notifications of dengue, Zika, and chikungunya. On Tuesday, March 17, coordinated by the Arboviruses Combat Situation Room, the initiative unites multiple municipal secretaries to eliminate breeding sites, perform urban cleaning, and engage the community. Activities include home visits by endemic agents, resident guidance, school outreach, debris removal, street sweeping, and backpack spraying, with work continuing over several days. Residents stress the urgency, citing high case numbers and vulnerable children, while testimonials highlight ongoing health impacts from Zika. Endemias manager João Luiz Teixeira emphasized domiciliary visits, enforcement, reporting, and the importance of seeking care at the nearest health unit for symptoms. Official notifications help pinpoint mosquito activity and trigger targeted blocking operations, underscoring the critical role of community participation.

articles.headline: Chuvas aumentam número de mosquitos e SMS alerta para risco de arboviroses
articles.headlineTranslated: Rain increases the number of mosquitoes and SMS alerts for the risk of arboviral diseases.
articles.summary: 2026-03-18 — Natal, Brazil faces heightened Aedes aegypti activity with the rainy season, prompting the Municipal Health Secretariat (SMS) to warn of arboviral transmission risk. Proliferation is strongest in Rocas, East Natal, amid standing water, clogged drains, and mosquitos near streets; residents report widespread muriçoca/mosquito presence. The SMS links increased rainfall and heat to accelerated breeding and cites improper waste disposal and water-holding containers as key factors. The latest SMS epidemiological bulletin records 448 probable arboviral cases in Natal: 400 dengue (140 confirmed), 42 chikungunya (10 confirmed), 6 probable Zika (1 confirmed). Preventive measures include eliminating standing water, securing water tanks, cleaning gutters, proper waste disposal, larviciding deposits, and using screens and repellents. Vector-control actions involve house visits, source elimination, larvicide treatment, and community education. Wolbachia release is ongoing in 33 neighborhoods to reduce transmission; UBV fumigation cycles target high-incidence areas and are state-led. Report risks via WhatsApp 3232-8235 or Natal Digital.

articles.headline: Evento destaca estratégias contra salmonelose em suínos
articles.headlineTranslated: Event Highlights Strategies to Combat Salmonellosis in Swine.
articles.summary: Salmonellosis in swine remains a major concern for food safety in Brazil. In Indaiatuba, São Paulo, Boehringer Ingelheim hosted the Salmonella Experts event on March 17, 2026 to discuss strategies to prevent and control infection in pigs. The disease, mainly caused by Salmonella Typhimurium and Salmonella Choleraesuis, can cause diarrhea, septicemia, reduced performance, and poses a food-safety risk. Key control measures include strict biossegurity (quarantine of new arrivals, restricted visitors, farm-dedicated clothing and footwear, vehicle controls) and sourcing piglets from Salmonella-free or monitored farms; rigorous cleaning between batches and proper disinfection. Sanitation programs include periodic lab monitoring, prudent antimicrobial use under veterinary guidance, and vaccination. Luciana Hernig highlighted Enterisol Salmonella T/C, a live attenuated oral vaccine against Typhimurium and Choleraesuis, reducing clinical signs, fecal excretion, and tissue colonization, improving growth, and enabling single-dose administration from about 2 weeks of age. The vaccine supports biosafety and meat safety by lowering carcass contamination.

articles.headlineTranslated: Woman dies after eating a suspected pizza, and an outbreak sends more than 100 people to the hospital.
articles.summary: One woman, Rayssa Maritein Bezerra e Silva, 44, died in Pombal, Paraíba, Brazil, after symptoms consistent with foodborne intoxication amid a cluster that sent more than 100 people to medical care. The patient had eaten pizza with her partner on Sunday, 15 March, developed diarrhea, vomiting and abdominal pain, was initially treated and released, then deteriorated and was admitted to ICU with signs of severe infection; she died on 17 March. At least 114 people sought care with nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, and malaise across the local urgent care unit and regional hospital. The restaurant linked to the outbreak was inspected and closed; food samples were collected for laboratory analysis. Among patients, one eight-year-old remains hospitalized; others have been discharged. Authorities urge medical attention for anyone with related symptoms; investigation is ongoing.

articles.headline: Intoxicação alimentar atinge 118 pessoas na PB e causa uma morte
articles.headlineTranslated: Food poisoning affects 118 people in Paraíba and causes one death.
articles.summary: Food poisoning outbreak in Sertão da Paraíba, Brazil, linked to a Pombal pizzeria sickened 118 people from 15 to 17 March 2026, with one death. The 44-year-old agronomist and public servant Raíssa Maritein Bezerra e Silva died after initial hospital care and subsequent ICU admission, presenting with a grave infectious-like syndrome. Affected patients experienced vomiting, nausea, diarrhea, abdominal pain, and malaise. The restaurant was closed on 16 March by Agevisa for grave sanitary violations, including lack of required documentation, presence of pests and insects, improper food storage, irregular thermal conditions, and rusted equipment, with reuse of used food containers observed. The Civil Police opened an inquiry. The owner, 24-year-old Marcos Antônio, expressed regret and said he is cooperating with authorities; his attorney stated there was no intent to harm customers.

articles.headline: Viruela de mono: "Hay varias formas de contagio, pero la mayoría son debido al sexo sin cuidado" - Primera Edición
articles.headlineTranslated: Monkeypox: "There are several modes of transmission, but most are due to unsafe sex" - First Edition.
articles.summary: First clade Ib mpox case detected in Argentina: a 31-year-old man from the City of Buenos Aires, with no travel history, treated outpatient and progressing favorably. In 2026 Argentina had five mpox cases, all clade II (four in Buenos Aires, one in Río Negro). Globally in 2026, mpox expanded in the Americas to 14 cases (USA 9, Canada 2, Brazil 2, Mexico 1, Argentina 1) with community transmission in France, Portugal, and Spain. Expert Hugo Pizzi characterized the Buenos Aires case as a minor genetic variation, not alarming, part of a broader cluster of about 70 cases in the country. He noted mpox originated in Africa (Zaire/DRC) in the 1970s, with transmission mainly via sexual contact, plus saliva, close contact, and contaminated bed linens. He emphasized prevention and sexual health awareness amid rising sexually transmitted infections.

articles.headline: Argentina detecta el primer caso del clado Ib de viruela símica, más contagioso y grave
articles.headlineTranslated: Argentina detects the first case of clade Ib of monkeypox, more contagious and severe.
articles.summary: Argentina reports its first mpox case caused by clade Ib, a more contagious, severe lineage than prior clade II infections. By 2026-03-17, five more cases were recorded (four in Buenos Aires City, one in Río Negro). Across the Americas, 14 Clade Ib cases have been reported, including the United States, Canada, Brazil, Mexico, and Argentina. MPXV has clades I (Ia, Ib) and II (IIa, IIb); the 2022–2023 outbreak was linked to IIb. Argentina approved the Mpox Strategic Plan 2025–2026 in February 2025 to bolster prevention and response. Transmission is mainly via direct contact with lesions or mucosa during close or sexual contact; isolation until crusts fall; 24-hour tracing with 21-day follow-up. Symptoms include fever, headache, myalgias, lymphadenopathy; incubation 5–21 days; typical course 14–21 days; higher risk in immunosuppressed.

articles.headline: Entenda o que é meningite meningocócica bacteriana, doença em surto na Inglaterra
articles.headlineTranslated: Understand what bacterial meningococcal meningitis is, an outbreak of the disease in England.
articles.summary: As of 17 March 2026, England reports a meningococcal meningitis outbreak with 15 confirmed cases and two deaths. Four infections are meningococcal group B, including the fatalities: an 18-year-old student at Queen Elizabeth’s Grammar School in Faversham and a 21-year-old student at the University of Kent. Meningococcal meningitis infects the brain’s protective membranes; symptoms include fever, headache, vomiting, and neck stiffness, with a ~2-day incubation and transmission via respiratory droplets from coughing, talking, or kissing—facilitating spread in enclosed settings. The illness can progress rapidly to septic shock and multi-organ failure if not treated promptly with intravenous antibiotics (often third-generation cephalosporins such as ceftriaxone). Close-contact prophylaxis is used to curb transmission. UK case fatality is ~10%; Brazil historically ~20%. Vaccines exist for meningococcal B but are not routine in Brazil’s SUS; meningococcal C and ACWY vaccines are included in the Brazilian immunization program.

articles.headlineTranslated: New, more contagious strain of monkeypox spreading across the Americas; there are cases in Mexico.
articles.summary: New, more contagious monkeypox Clade Ib is spreading across the Americas; Argentina reports its first Mpox Clade Ib case in a 31-year-old Buenos Aires resident with no recent international travel; the patient is ambulatory and improving. Clade Ib, first identified in the Democratic Republic of Congo in 2023, is more transmissible than Clade II, which accounts for five Argentine cases. In 2026, Clade Ib cases have reached 14 in the Americas: 9 in the United States, 2 in Canada, 2 in Brazil, 1 in Mexico, 1 in Argentina. Transmission is via close contact or sexual contact; incubation 6–13 days; symptoms include painful skin/mucosal lesions (genital/anal), fever, fatigue, myalgias, headache, and lymphadenopathy. Isolation until crusts fall and skin heals; healthcare workers should use PPE, and contact tracing should begin within 24 hours with a 21-day monitoring period. A vaccinia-based vaccine exists; vaccination is prioritized for endemic zones and high-risk groups.

articles.headline: Surto de chikungunya suspende aulas em 4 escolas de aldeias em Dourados
articles.headlineTranslated: Chikungunya outbreak suspends classes in four indigenous village schools in Dourados.
articles.summary: Chikungunya outbreak in Dourados, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, has suspended classes in four schools located in the indigenous Bororó and Jaguapiru villages. In under three weeks, 407 indigenous cases have been notified, with 202 confirmed, 181 under investigation, and 24 discarded. The first victim was a 69-year-old woman who died on the 26th; a death of a 60-year-old woman was confirmed on the 12th. A 73-year-old man and a 3-month-old baby are also reported among the affected. Urban area reports 912 notifications this year: 379 confirmed, 383 awaiting results, 150 discarded; no deaths outside indigenous reserves. The four schools—Francisco Meireles, Ramão Martins, Tengatiu Magangatu, Guateka Marçal de Souza—are inoperative due to at least 20 staff with chikungunya. Response includes inspecting 4,319 properties, treating 2,173 sites, and locating 1,004 mosquito foci (90% in water tanks, trash, and tires); emphasis on eliminating standing water.

articles.headline: Mpox: especialistas explicam sintomas, tratamento e riscos - Folha Vitória
articles.headlineTranslated: Mpox: specialists explain symptoms, treatment and risks - Folha Vitória.
articles.summary: Mpox (monkeypox) is analyzed in a Brazilian report, noting that the World Health Organization renamed the infection to mpox to reduce stigma toward primates. The virus is carried mainly by small rodents (squirrels), with monkeys and humans as incidental hosts. Transmission occurs via direct contact with skin lesions, bodily fluids, respiratory droplets, or contaminated items such as clothing and bedding. The incubation period ranges from 6 to 13 days, potentially up to 21 days. Main symptoms are described by specialists but not enumerated in the excerpt. Treatment is symptomatic, with analgesics, antipyretics, and antivirals used in more severe cases. Ocular symptoms may require lubricating drops, antivirals or antibiotics, plus cold or moist compresses and saline eyelid hygiene. Preventive measures include avoiding direct contact with infected individuals and their lesions, not sharing contaminated items, and maintaining hand hygiene; masks are advised in outbreak settings. Published 17 March 2026 by Folha Vitória.

articles.headline: Mulher morre e mais de 100 pessoas vão parar no hospital após comerem pizza em restaurante
articles.headlineTranslated: Woman dies and more than 100 people are hospitalized after eating pizza at a restaurant
articles.summary: A deadly foodborne outbreak linked to a pizza restaurant in Pombal, Paraíba, Brazil, left one woman dead and prompted medical care for about 114 others between Sunday night and Tuesday. Rayssa Maritein Bezerra e Silva, 44, died Tuesday at 8:59 a.m. after rapid clinical deterioration and ICU admission with signs of a severe infectious syndrome. The La Favoritta restaurant remains closed as investigators collect samples; the State Health Surveillance Agency (Agevisa) conducted an inspection and seized materials for laboratory analysis. In total, 40 people sought care at the municipal urgent care (UPA) and 74 were admitted to the Regional Hospital of Pombal (36 on Sunday, 38 on Monday) with gastroenteric symptoms including diarrhea, vomiting, abdominal pain, nausea, and malaise. The infection source is linked to pizza consumed at the restaurant; investigations ongoing; owner cooperating.

articles.headlineTranslated: Inspector Cabral warns of the spread of chikungunya and advocates greater recognition for health workers and vector control agents.
articles.summary: Dourados, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, faces rising dengue and chikungunya, with 386 suspected and 206 confirmed chikungunya cases and three deaths in the Indigenous Reserve over the past two weeks (a 3-month-old infant, a 73-year-old without comorbidities, and a 69-year-old woman from Jaguapiru). About 70% of cases are concentrated in the Indigenous Reserve, prompting authorities to treat the outbreak as an epidemic and intensify vector-control efforts. Transmission is via Aedes aegypti; prevention focuses on removing standing water in homes—plants, containers, bottles, tires, clogged gutters, and uncovered water tanks. Five pregnant women are in the second trimester and two in the third trimester. Vector Control Agents and Community Health Workers are acknowledged for essential frontline work, and officials urge citywide community participation to eliminate mosquito breeding sites.

articles.headline: Bronquiolite: VSR causou 272 mortes de crianças em 2025. Temporada de casos começa agora
articles.headlineTranslated: Bronchiolitis: RSV caused 272 child deaths in 2025. RSV season begins now.
articles.summary: RSV drives bronchiolitis, an inflammatory lung condition that disproportionately affects the youngest. It is highly contagious and a major cause of severe respiratory infections in babies and small children, with bronchiolitis as its key presentation. In 2025, RSV caused 272 pediatric deaths. The infection is characterized by a high hospitalization rate and there is no specific antiviral treatment. Each autumn and winter, RSV burdens health systems, raising hospital admissions and demand for pediatric care. The article notes that the RSV season has begun as of 17 March 2026, signaling ongoing transmission and ongoing risk for infants and young children. This seasonal burden repeats annually.

articles.headline: Altas temperaturas favorecem mosquito da dengue; veja como prevenir
articles.headlineTranslated: High temperatures favor the dengue-carrying mosquito; see how to prevent.
articles.summary: Rising temperatures in São Paulo state heighten proliferation of Aedes aegypti and dengue transmission. As of 17 March 2026, the São Paulo State Health Secretariat reports 15,744 confirmed dengue cases and six deaths, with 315 chikungunya cases and two deaths. Dengue symptoms may begin abruptly and last 5–7 days. In response, prevention centers on eliminating standing water around homes. Key guidance includes sealing trash in plastic bags, keeping lids closed; clearing leaves and debris from gutters; filling plant pot saucer holes with sand; weekly washing and refilling plant-water vessels; turning containers that collect water on their side; keeping water tanks sealed; and disposing of items that collect water, especially after rain. The government also launched Dengue 100 Dúvidas to answer common questions on dengue, zika, and chikungunya. Daily case data remain accessible on the health department’s portal.

articles.headline: Botucatu inicia campanha de busca ativa para reforçar combate à tuberculose | Jornal Acontece Botucatu
articles.headlineTranslated: Botucatu launches an active case-finding campaign to reinforce the fight against tuberculosis | Jornal Acontece Botucatu.
articles.summary: Botucatu launches an active case-finding campaign for tuberculosis (TB) throughout March, across all municipal health units, to detect symptomatic respiratory cases early and expand treatment to curb transmission. The effort coincides with World TB Day on March 24 and uses the Ministry of Health’s Sintomático Respiratório as a confidential reporting tool central to TB control. Health teams will collect sputum for diagnostic testing; residents with respiratory symptoms are advised to seek care at the nearest service. TB is an infectious bacterium primarily affecting the lungs but can involve other organs such as bones, kidneys, and brain, and spreads via the air through speaking, coughing, or sneezing. Municipal data indicate stable TB case numbers; the campaign emphasizes vigilance as seasonal changes raise transmission risk in enclosed spaces.

articles.headlineTranslated: Divinópolis launches a new dengue control drive in 13 neighborhoods - Portal MPA
articles.summary: Divinópolis launches its sixth dengue-control cleanup blitz on Saturday, March 21, 2026, across 13 neighborhoods, organized by the Municipal Health Secretariat (Semusa). From 8:00 to 12:00, Environmental Health Surveillance teams will target Aedes aegypti breeding sites by removing water-holding items—tires, bottles, cans, plastics, tarps, tanks, drums—left on sidewalks in two city regions: North: Serra Verde; Conjunto Habitacional Oswaldo Machado Gontijo; Alto das Oliveiras; Nova Fortaleza I; Vila Anchieta. West: Vila Belo Horizonte; Vila Santo Antônio; Ipiranga; L.P. Pereira; Jardim Brasília; Walchir Resende; Prolongamento Walchir Resende; Orion. Residents are urged to place discarded items on the curb to facilitate pickup. Previous mutirões collected substantial waste: in the Southeast region two trucks of furniture, a recyclable truck, two pickups of various materials, and 28 tires; in the Southwest, three trucks of furniture, a recyclables truck, one pickup, and 35 tires. Eliminating standing water and proper waste disposal remain key.

articles.headline: Há seis anos, Acre confirmava primeiros casos de Covid-19; relembre
articles.headlineTranslated: Six years ago, Acre confirmed its first COVID-19 cases; look back.
articles.summary: Six years after Acre confirmed its first COVID-19 cases on March 17, 2020, the state logged 4,710 confirmed cases and 37 deaths in January–August 2025. By end of 2025 (epidemiological week 49), Acre reports exceed 175,000 cases and 2,105 deaths overall. In 2025, 4,873 cases and 24 deaths were recorded, with 15,393 vaccine doses administered. Historically, 2020 saw 41,620 cases and 795 deaths; 2021 had 46,764 cases and 1,056 deaths; 2022 had 70,315 cases and 189 deaths; 2023 had 8,015 cases and 27 deaths; 2024 had 3,553 cases and 14 deaths. The first cases included a 30-year-old man, a 50-year-old woman from São Paulo, and a 37-year-old lawyer in Fortaleza; the latter required 12 days in ICU. The first death occurred April 6, 2020 (Antônia Holanda, 79). The June 2020 peak recorded 217 deaths; April 2020 had 19. Government emergency was declared the same day as the first cases, implementing curfews, restrictions, and later school closures. Vaccination began January 2021 with CoronaVac (about 40,760 first/second doses), prioritizing health workers, elderly, and Indigenous communities; vaccination contributed to reduced severe disease and deaths, though transmission persists.

articles.headline: Surto de chikungunya suspende aulas em escolas das aldeias em Dourados
articles.headlineTranslated: Chikungunya outbreak suspends classes at the villages' schools in Dourados
articles.summary: Chikungunya outbreak in Jaguapiru and Bororó villages within the Dourados Indigenous Reserve, Mato Grosso do Sul, triggers suspension of classes at four schools: Escola Municipal Francisco Meireles, Escola Municipal Indígena Ramão Martins, Escola Estadual Indígena Guateka Marçal de Souza, and Escola Municipal Indígena Tengatuan Magangatu, effective March 18, 2026. The measure follows widespread staff absences that impede school operations; at Guateka Marçal de Souza, more than 20 employees are on medical leave. Mato Grosso do Sul records its 4th chikungunya death in 2026, all within the Dourados reserve, with Jaguapiru and Bororó described as having an epicemic spread. A major transmission driver cited is irregular regular water supply, causing households to store water in containers that favor Aedes mosquito breeding. Health teams are mobilized (SESAI, Hospital Universitário) with SUS support from the Força Nacional do SUS. Health transport within the reserve has halted after a contract breach with a contractor, compromising basic care and services such as dialysis; no clear resolution yet.

articles.headline: Sobe para quatro o número de mortos por chikungunya em área indígena
articles.headlineTranslated: Death toll from chikungunya in an indigenous area rises to four.
articles.summary: Chikungunya fatalities rise to four in Dourados Indigenous Reserve. The latest Health Surveillance bulletin (March 16, 2026) reports 407 cases notified in the Dourados Indigenous Reserve, with 202 confirmed, 181 under investigation, 24 discarded, and four deaths—two in Jaguapiru (69-year-old woman on Feb 26; 60-year-old woman on Mar 12), one in Jaguapiru (73-year-old man on Mar 9), and one 3-month-old infant in Bororó (Mar 10). In the urban area, 912 notifications in 2026 (379 confirmed, 383 awaiting results, 150 discarded), with no deaths outside the reserve. A city mutirão in Jaguapiru and Bororó, with state support and Itaporã, has inspected 4,319 properties, treated 2,173 sites, identified 1,004 mosquito breeding sites (90% in water tanks, trash, tires), sprayed 43 properties, and mobilized 86 endemic agents and 29 indigenous health workers. Aedes aegypti transmission; symptoms include high fever, severe joint pain, and fatigue; severe cases may lead to encephalitis, meningitis, or paralysis; recovery can be slow.

articles.headline: Divinópolis confirma primeira morte por dengue em 2026 - Portal MPA
articles.headlineTranslated: Divinópolis confirms first dengue-related death in 2026 - Portal MPA.
articles.summary: Divinópolis, Brazil, confirms the first dengue-related death in 2026, with a second possible dengue-related death under investigation, per the Municipal Health Secretariat update on 17 March 2026. The city reports 530 dengue notifications, of which 142 are laboratory-confirmed. Hospitalizations total 59. Of the confirmed dengue cases, 136 are dengue fever with six warning signs; 208 cases remain under investigation and 180 have been ruled out. No cases of severe dengue have been recorded to date. The neighborhoods with the most notifications are São José (41), Centro (30), Catalão (28) and São Roque (23), followed by Tietê, Planalto and Afonso Pena. There have been six chikungunya notifications, but no confirmed chikungunya cases; three hospitalizations remain under investigation for suspected chikungunya. No Zika virus records in 2026. Preventive measures emphasize eliminating standing water and controlling Aedes aegypti breeding sites.

articles.headline: 'Alegre e acolhedora': quem é a mulher que morreu após comer em pizzaria investigada por surto de intoxicação alimentar na Paraíba
articles.headlineTranslated: 'Cheerful and welcoming': who is the woman who died after eating at a pizzeria investigated for a food poisoning outbreak in Paraíba.
articles.summary: Outbreak of food poisoning linked to a pizzeria in Pombal, Paraíba, Brazil, with one death and about 114 people ill. Rayssa Maritein Bezerra e Silva, 44, a public servant, died after eating at the establishment; she developed diarrhea, vomiting and abdominal pain, was hospitalized, and died on March 17 following rapid clinical decline and ICU transfer. In total, 114 people sought care: 40 at the UPA and 74 at the Hospital Regional de Pombal, most treated and discharged, with two still hospitalized (an 8-year-old child and an adult woman). The pizzeria has been interdicted by the Vigilância Sanitária de Pombal; an inspection by Agevisa-PB found irregularities, including insects and poorly stored foods. The Civil Police opened an inquiry; forensic and health authorities will analyze samples from the restaurant and the victim, with no timeline for results. The outbreak appears linked to a single establishment in northern Paraíba.

articles.headline: Mulher morre e outras 113 pessoas são hospitalizadas após comerem pizza
articles.headlineTranslated: Woman dies and 113 more people are hospitalized after eating pizza.
articles.summary: One death and 113 hospitalizations linked to pizza served at La Favoritta in Sertão do Paraíba, Paraíba, Brazil. Rayssa Maritein Bezerra e Silva, 44, died after diarrhea, vomiting and abdominal pain; death confirmed at 08:59 local on Tuesday by Hospital Senador Rui Carneiro in Pombal, where she had been in intensive care. Affected individuals include 40 treated at Pombal's Urgent Care and 74 at the Regional Hospital of Pombal, most having eaten the same pizza Sunday night. One eight-year-old remains hospitalized, leaving 114 patients in care. Agevisa, the state surveillance agency, has inspected La Favoritta, which is closed; the owner is cooperating as investigators look for a contaminated-food source and determine if the outbreak is linked to the weekend event.

articles.headline: Espírito Santo registra terceiro caso de mpox e dois seguem em investigação
articles.headlineTranslated: Espírito Santo records third mpox case, and two remain under investigation.
articles.summary: As of 17 March 2026, Espírito Santo (ES), Brazil, reports its third mpox case this year. The patient is a man from Cachoeiro de Itapemirim; ES has 50 notifications, with 42 discarded and 2 under investigation. All confirmed ES mpox patients presented sudden fever and skin eruptions. Nationally, Brazil has 149 mpox cases: 140 laboratory-confirmed and 9 under analysis. Mpox is a zoonotic viral disease transmitted through contact with infected people, contaminated materials, or infected wildlife. Common symptoms include skin lesions, swollen lymph nodes, fever, headache, body aches, chills, and weakness. Individuals with similar symptoms should seek healthcare services promptly.

articles.headline: Servidora pública morre e outras 113 pessoas são internadas após comerem pizza na PB
articles.headlineTranslated: Female public servant dies and another 113 people are hospitalized after eating pizza in Paraíba.
articles.summary: In Pombal, Paraíba, Brazil, a 44-year-old municipal employee, Raissa Maritein Bezerra e Silva, died on 17 March 2026 after suspected food poisoning from a local pizzaria. She had been hospitalized on 16 March with diarrhea, abdominal pain, and vomiting, deteriorating to grave condition and death in the ICU. Her partner also experienced malaise. By 17 March, 114 people had sought care for similar symptoms: 74 admitted to the Regional Hospital of Pombal and 40 treated at a Unit of Emergency Care (UPA); one eight‑year‑old remains hospitalized, others discharged. The pizzaria was closed by the municipal Sanitation Surveillance; samples were collected for laboratory analysis, and Agevisa conducted an inspection. The municipality declared mourning and suspended non-essential services. The investigation aims to identify the infectious agent and contamination source.

articles.headline: Saúde de Mundo Novo intensifica combate à Dengue com vacinação de agentes da linha de frente
articles.headlineTranslated: Mundo Novo Health Department intensifies the fight against Dengue with vaccination of frontline workers.
articles.summary: On 2026-03-17, Mundo Novo’s Municipal Health Secretariat launched a dengue vaccination drive using the Instituto Butantan vaccine, prioritizing frontline workers: community health agents (ACS) and endemic disease control agents (ACE) who visit homes and eliminate breeding sites. Eligible personnel are aged 15 through 59 years, 11 months, and 29 days. Vaccinations are provided Monday–Friday at UBS Central and UBS Fleck, from 7:00 to 11:00 and 13:00 to 17:00. The aim is to protect field staff who maintain health system functionality and sustain epidemiological surveillance against Aedes aegypti–borne dengue. A closing note states participation is voluntary, with readers invited to comment with their name and city to engage.

articles.headline: Ministério da Saúde adota estudo sobre previsão de surtos de dengue com participação do MCTI
articles.headlineTranslated: Ministry of Health adopts a study on dengue outbreak forecasting with the participation of the MCTI.
articles.summary: As of 17 March 2026, Brazil adopts a dengue forecasting model integrating mathematical predictions, machine learning, and climate data to anticipate dengue incidence and Aedes aegypti dynamics. Developed with Laboratório Nacional de Computação Científica (LNCC) and the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MCTI), the ensemble model is now part of the Ministry of Health's official epidemic-response strategy and was published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS) as part of the IMDC24 Dengue Forecasting Sprint in Brazil. The approach combines multiple predictive systems to improve reliability under outbreak conditions. It draws on climate inputs and vector surveillance within the Mosqlimate-Infodengue consortium, including FGV, Fiocruz, UERJ, IMPA, and partner institutions from Saudi Arabia, Spain, and the United States. By forecasting peaks, it helps optimize resource distribution and guide preventive actions before dengue surges.

articles.headline: Prefeitura amplia campanha "Todos Contra a Dengue" e reforça alerta de prevenção em Cuiabá
articles.headlineTranslated: City Hall expands the "Everyone Against Dengue" campaign and reinforces the dengue prevention alert in Cuiabá.
articles.summary: Dengue prevention efforts in Cuiabá, Brazil, intensified as the city expands the 'Todos Contra a Dengue' campaign in 2026. The Municipal Health Secretariat and Health Surveillance report 197,192 vector-control inspections across districts in early 2026, identifying and eliminating Aedes aegypti breeding sites. Despite reduced dengue case numbers, one death has been confirmed this year. Vaccination against dengue is available in the public network for children and adolescents aged 10–14, with a two-dose schedule. A new larvicide strategy uses BTI Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis in fixed water deposits (e.g., water tanks, cisterns) to suppress larvae; the product leaves a sandy powder residue, does not alter water taste or odor, and is considered safe when properly applied. Public guidance urges removing standing water, sealing tanks, cleaning gutters, and proper waste disposal; seek care for fever, body pain, headache, or malaise. ACEs should be allowed during home visits.
