articles.headline: Confirman el primer caso autóctono de la "viruela del mono"
articles.headlineTranslated: First Locally Transmitted Case of Monkeypox Confirmed.
articles.summary: On 17 March 2026, Argentina reports its first autochthonous mpox case, a 31-year-old resident of Buenos Aires, due to clade Ib. Confirmation by sequencing and real-time PCR. Symptoms began 24 February: fever, exanthema, headache, myalgias, lumbar pain, lymphadenopathy, and anorectal pain; the patient recovered as outpatient. Epidemiology links exposure to several casual sexual partners and travel contacts; this is the first clade Ib case without travel, though six mpox cases in 2026 (five in Buenos Aires, one in Río Negro) relate to earlier variant. Fourteen mpox cases in the Americas (USA, Canada, Brazil, Mexico). Clade Ib is linked to more severe disease. Transmission occurs mainly by direct contact with lesions or mucosa during close or sexual contact; also via contaminated objects and respiratory secretions. Lesions are deep, delimited, with umbilication, progressing from macules to crusts. articles.headline: Sorocaba registra queda nos casos de dengue no início de 2026 | TVS+
articles.headlineTranslated: Sorocaba records a drop in dengue cases in early 2026 | TVS+
articles.summary: Dengue in Sorocaba, Brazil shows a sharp early-2026 decline after a deadly 2025. The city reports thousands of dengue cases and 31 deaths in 2025; in Jan–Feb 2025 there were 14,136 cases and 31 deaths, while Jan–Feb 2026 records 18 cases and zero deaths. The reduction results from a partnership between the municipal government and residents, illustrated by Maria de Lourdes Brito who keeps yards free of standing water—no plant saucers, perforated PET bottles, and frequent changes of dog water. Despite improvement, vector control continues via the Zoonoses department and community actions. Four quarterly larval index surveys identify areas with higher Aedes aegypti breeding to target interventions. The report emphasizes ongoing prevention and sustained community engagement as essential to maintaining control of dengue in Sorocaba.

articles.headline: Com aumento de casos de HIV em Gramado, Secretaria da Saúde amplia combate e descentraliza atendimento de prevenção | abc+
articles.headlineTranslated: With an increase in HIV cases in Gramado, the Department of Health broadens the fight and decentralizes prevention services | abc+.
articles.summary: On 2026-03-17, Gramado’s Health Department expanded HIV prevention by decentralizing PrEP to all basic health units (UBS) and Family Health Strategy teams (ESF), after rising local HIV cases. Previously PrEP was available only at the Specialized Care Service (SAE) in Hortênsias, Canela. The move aims to reduce geographic barriers and extend protection to those at highest risk. Reported HIV cases rose from 20 in 2023 to 46 in 2024 and 40 in 2025. PrEP uses daily antiretrovirals—tenofovir disoproxil fumarate and emtricitabine—reducing HIV infection risk; the WHO deems it safe and effective. Condoms remain essential for other STIs. Eligibility: Gramado residents aged 15+, weight ≥35 kg; pregnant/lactating individuals may use under medical supervision. Risk factors include inconsistent condom use, history of STIs, seeking PEP, multiple partners, sex for money/drugs, or needle sharing. Access via nearest UBS with SUS card; prescription filled at the Central Pharmacy.

articles.headline: Fungo transmitido por gatos preocupa autoridades e reforça vigilância sanitária internacional
articles.headlineTranslated: Fungus transmitted by cats concerns authorities and reinforces international public health surveillance.
articles.summary: Brazilian-origin fungus Sporothrix brasiliensis, capable of feline-to-human transmission, has been detected outside its usual focus, prompting heightened surveillance in Uruguay. The dimorphic fungus grows as filamentous structures in the environment and as yeast in humans, aiding survival and spread. Sporotrichosis can be transmitted via scratches, bites, or contact with lesions from cats, with street cats linked to more severe disease. Cats often present facial, nasal, and paw lesions and may act as reservoirs. In humans, initial red cutaneous papules can ulcerate and spread along lymphatics; rare but severe complications include pulmonary infections, arthritis, and meningitis, especially in immunocompromised individuals. Diagnosis relies on lesion analysis or culture; treatment with itraconazole or terbinafine typically lasts several weeks. No official alerts yet in Uruguay; authorities urge vigilance and prompt medical or veterinary consultation for suspected cases.

articles.headline: El Ministerio de Salud detectó la variante más agresiva de la viruela del mono en Argentina
articles.headlineTranslated: The Ministry of Health detected the most aggressive variant of monkeypox in Argentina.
articles.summary: Argentina confirms its first mpox (monkeypox) case in clade Ib, a 31-year-old man in Buenos Aires with no recent travel. Diagnosis on March 10 by RT-PCR and vesicular-content DNA sequencing; patient ambulatory and improving; no secondary cases detected to date. Clade Ib—subvariant of clade I—exhibits increased human-to-human transmission and greater clinical severity than the 2022 clade IIb strains. Argentina had five clade II cases in 2026 (four in CABA, one in Río Negro). Across the Americas in 2026, 14 clade Ib cases: United States 9, Canada 2, Brazil 2, Mexico 1, Argentina 1; Europe reports transmission in France, Portugal, Spain. The patient reported multiple new sexual partners, highlighting exposure via sexual networks; incubation 5–21 days (typically 6–13); disease usually self-limited in 14–21 days with supportive care. Prodrome includes fever, headache, myalgia, lymphadenopathy, fatigue, sore throat, followed by vesicular lesions; isolation and PPE recommended, with home hygiene guidance.

articles.headline: MS chega à 4ª morte de indígenas da mesma reserva por chikungunya em 2026
articles.headlineTranslated: Ministry of Health reports the 4th death of indigenous people in the same reserve due to chikungunya in 2026.
articles.summary: Chikungunya deaths rise in Mato Grosso do Sul, with four fatalities in 2026 all in the Dourados Indigenous Reserve (Jaguapiru and Bororó). The latest victim is a 60-year-old woman with comorbidities, who died March 12; earlier deaths include a 69-year-old woman (Feb 26), a 73-year-old man (Mar 9), and a 3-month-old infant (Mar 10). All deaths occurred within the reserve, Brazil’s largest urban indigenous territory (about 3,500 ha, >15,000 residents). The reserve reports 407 suspected cases: 202 confirmed, 181 under investigation, 24 discarded. In the urban area, 912 notifications with 379 confirmed; no deaths outside the reserve. MS leads Brazil in 2026 with 90.2 probable cases/100k; nationwide 16,558 probable cases and 10 deaths; MS accounts for ~40% of national chikungunya deaths. A mutirão in Jaguapiru and Bororó mobilizes 4,319 properties inspected and 1,004 mosquito breeding sites identified (90% in water tanks, trash, tires). Transmission by Aedes aegypti; symptoms include high fever and severe joint pain; risk of neurological complications. Emphasize eliminating standing water; ongoing control despite irregular rains.

articles.headline: Campanha contra tuberculose é iniciada em Manaus
articles.headlineTranslated: Campaign against tuberculosis is initiated in Manaus.
articles.summary: Manaus, Amazonas, launched the 2026 Mobilization Campaign against Tuberculosis on 17 March at USF Adalgiza Barbosa de Lima in the West Zone, ahead of World Tuberculosis Day on 24 March. The initiative seeks to reinforce prevention, expand early diagnosis, and ensure treatment within the municipal health network. According to Semsa, Manaus has recorded 471 tuberculosis cases so far this year. In March, diagnostic drive includes sputum testing for people with a cough of two weeks or more, broader testing for latent tuberculosis infection, and active case finding among contacts of TB patients. The campaign also emphasizes education on symptoms—persistent cough, fever, and weight loss—and works to counter stigma, underscoring that tuberculosis is curable and treatment is free through Brazil's Unified Health System (SUS).

articles.summary: Três Lagoas, Brazil — The Municipal Health Secretariat will host another meeting of the Municipal Committee for Mobilization and Combat against Aedes aegypti on Thursday, March 19, starting at 8:00 a.m. The open event, held at the Sindicato dos Servidores Públicos Municipais (SSPM), seeks to advance actions to reduce suspected dengue cases reported in the municipality. The committee is tasked with monitoring and shaping strategies for prevention and control of arboviruses, and with planning ongoing dengue-control activities while developing rapid-response plans for dengue, Zika virus, and Chikungunya outbreaks. The gathering, conducted by the Municipal Committee for Mobilization and Combat against Aedes aegypti, emphasizes community involvement and rapid public-health decision-making in the fight against Aedes aegypti–borne diseases. Location: Rua Manoel Pedro de Campos, 1050, Nossa Senhora Aparecida neighborhood.

articles.headline: Viruela del mono en Argentina: se confirmó el primer caso de una variante más peligrosa
articles.headlineTranslated: Monkeypox in Argentina: The first case of a more dangerous variant has been confirmed.
articles.summary: Monkeypox clade Ib, a more transmissible and potentially more severe variant, is confirmed in Argentina—the first case. A 31-year-old man from Buenos Aires City (CABA) has no recent international travel, suggesting local circulation; he is stable on outpatient treatment. Previously in 2026, Argentina reported five mpox cases (four in CABA, one in Río Negro) all belonging to clade II. Across the Americas this year, clade Ib accounts for 14 cases: United States 9, Canada 2, Brazil 2, Mexico 1, and Argentina 1; Europe reports community transmission in France, Portugal, and Spain. The Health Ministry urges reinforced surveillance and prompt evaluation for umbilicated lesions or proctitis, plus lymphadenopathy, fatigue, and sore throat, with travel/contact history reviewed. If confirmed, strict isolation is required until crusts detach and new skin forms, and health workers should use PPE due to higher contagion risk.

articles.headline: Sesau orienta população sobre prevenção da leptospirose durante período chuvoso
articles.headlineTranslated: Sesau advises the public on leptospirosis prevention during the rainy season.
articles.summary: Leptospirosis remains a public health concern in Alagoas ahead of the rainy season. The acute febrile infection is caused by Leptospira bacteria, primarily carried by rodents, and transmitted via direct contact with or contamination by rodent urine in floodwater, sewage, or contaminated objects. Prevention emphasizes avoiding exposure to rainwater, floodwater, and water from rivers/streams; if exposure is unavoidable, wear gloves and waterproof boots; use treated drinking water and thoroughly wash foods with potable water, using sodium hypochlorite where available. After contact with mud or floodwater, shower and monitor for symptoms, and seek medical care if needed. Core symptoms include muscle pain (calves), fever, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, headache, conjunctival hemorrhage, photophobia, eye pain; rash and enlargement of liver, spleen, or lymph nodes may occur. Incubation ranges 1–30 days (commonly 7–14). In 2025, Alagoas recorded 30 cases and 8 deaths.

articles.headlineTranslated: Mpox Clade Ib variant detected in Argentina, more contagious and severe.
articles.summary: Mpox Clade Ib detected in Argentina—the first case of this more contagious and potentially severe mpox variant—in Buenos Aires (CABA) with no recent travel. The 31-year-old man is under ambulatory follow-up and improving. Previously, Argentina had five mpox Clade II cases in 2026 (four in CABA, one in Río Negro), a milder lineage; the Clade Ib case suggests possible local circulation and raises vigilance. Internationally, 14 Clade Ib cases have been reported in the Americas this year: nine in the United States, two in Canada, two in Brazil, one in Mexico; Europe reports community transmission in France, Portugal, and Spain. Authorities urge intensified surveillance and clinical suspicion, noting symptoms such as umbilicated skin lesions, lymphadenopathy, proctitis, sore throat, and fatigue. Measures include isolation until complete healing of lesions, mandatory PPE for health workers, and contact tracing within 24 hours with a 21-day follow-up.

articles.headline: Prefeito assina decreto que autoriza distribuição gratuita de medicamento contra a esporotricose - Jornal O Sul
articles.headlineTranslated: Mayor signs decree authorizing free distribution of a medication for sporotrichosis - O Sul Newspaper
articles.summary: Santa Cruz do Sul, Brazil, enacted Municipal Law 10.284/26 and Decree 12.731 to create the Municipal Program for Enfrentamento e Controle da Esporotricose Animal e Humana. The program enables free distribution of itraconazole, provides veterinary care and diagnostic testing for animals with sporotrichosis, and requires microchipping, case tracking, and integrated surveillance. It emphasizes One Health, with Sebema and Sesa coordinating efforts. Eligibility prioritizes stray, community, or low-income owned animals (per capita income up to half a minimum wage or up to three minimum wages). Owners must present a veterinary report, CadÚnico socio-economic data, and sign a treatment commitment; noncompliance could lead to animal removal. Euthanasia is allowed only in poor prognosis and irreversible suffering, not as population control. Distribution began March 9, 2026. Cats are highlighted as primary victims; a rescued cat, Sol, recovered after treatment.

articles.headlineTranslated: Espírito Santo reports third mpox case, and two remain under investigation - Folha Vitória.
articles.summary: As of 17 March 2026, Espírito Santo, Brazil, reports its third mpox (monkeypox) case, with two additional cases under investigation. The state logged 50 notifications: 42 ruled out and two suspected. Nationally, Brazil counts 149 mpox cases, with 140 laboratory-confirmed and nine still under analysis. All confirmed patients exhibited sudden fever and a generalized skin eruption. Mpox is a viral zoonosis; human transmission can occur through close contact with infected persons, contaminated materials, or infected wild animals. The report highlights ongoing surveillance in Espírito Santo and the national caseload, underscoring symptomatology (fever, rash) and laboratory confirmation as key factors for case status.

Transmission occurs mainly through direct contact with infected individuals or contaminated materials, with close physical proximity facilitating spread. Symptoms typically appear progressively and manifestations vary in intensity; the article emphasizes preventive habits to reduce risk. No imported/exported case details are provided. Continued monitoring, high-quality information, and active prevention are highlighted to contain transmission in Ceará.

articles.headline: Saneamento precário em Santo Amaro preocupa moradores e aumenta risco de doenças
articles.headlineTranslated: Poor sanitation in Santo Amaro worries residents and increases the risk of disease.
articles.summary: Poor sanitation in Santo Amaro, Brazil, centers on open sewage and debris on Rua do Viveiro and Rua Fausto Rabelo, where residents report that wastewater flows openly, obstructing movement and increasing accident risk. Pedestrians must walk on wooden planks, and children use the hazardous path to reach homes. Health concerns accompany the filth, with frequent contact with dirty water and waste raising the risk of infections, especially among the elderly and young children. A mother of a newborn describes the baby becoming ill with an eye problem attributed to the unsanitary conditions; another resident, known as Jorge, reportedly developed a skin disease linked to the environment. Community efforts—meetings and petitions—have sought public action, but residents say authorities have offered only promises and have yet to implement concrete measures. The article highlights perceived health risks and governance gaps amid a failing sanitation situation.

articles.headlineTranslated: Amid Chikungunya cases, Zé Teixeira denounces gasoline shortages in the villages of Dourados.
articles.summary: Chikungunya outbreaks in the Indigenous Reserve of Dourados, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, have caused three deaths in two weeks, with a 3‑month‑old baby who developed symptoms on Mar 6 and died Mar 10, along with a 73‑year‑old man and a 69‑year‑old woman; dengue cases are also reported in the same communities. A epidemiological bulletin released Mar 13 by the state health department confirms the fatalities and ongoing transmission. State Deputy Zé Teixeira (PSDB) denounced gasoline shortages that hinder transport for Indigenous people and criticized the Indigenous affairs secretariat’s management. He stated he funded fuel for transport and financed chikungunya tests and medications, and secured road maintenance within the reserves. Dourados lies roughly 233 km from Campo Grande.

articles.headline: Maringá inicia nova estratégia de vacinação contra a dengue para trabalhadores da saúde
articles.headlineTranslated: Maringá launches new dengue vaccination strategy for healthcare workers.
articles.summary: Maringá, Paraná, Brazil launches a new dengue vaccination phase targeting primary health care workers in the SUS. Starting Wednesday, March 18, 2026, the city will vaccinate Basic Health Unit vaccinators, Community Health Agents (ACS), and Endemic Control Agents (ACE), following Technical Note 11/2026 from the Ministry of Health. The municipality received 917 doses of a live-attenuated dengue vaccine produced by Instituto Butantan, with phased distribution defined with state health authorities and the Ministry. Training for UBS teams occurred on March 12, 2026. Doses will be allocated proportionally among UBSs, with potential expansion to other health workers as new lots arrive. The vaccine is live-attenuated and cannot be administered to pregnant or breastfeeding women, people living with HIV, or those with immunodeficiency. Health Secretary Antônio Carlos Nardi emphasized this supply follows national/state plans, and that dengue prevention—eliminating mosquito breeding sites and public participation—remains essential alongside immunization.

articles.headline: MS confirma 4ª morte por chikungunya em 2026, diz Ministério da Saúde
articles.headlineTranslated: Ministry of Health confirms 4th chikungunya-related death in 2026.
articles.summary: Chikungunya deaths in Mato Grosso do Sul rise to four by 17 March 2026, all in Dourados, where Indigenous communities are affected by an Aedes aegypti–driven outbreak. The fourth fatality is a 60-year-old woman with comorbidities, who died on 12 March; a three-month-old baby died about a week earlier; the other victims are a 69-year-old and a 73-year-old. All four residents live in the same Dourados Indigenous Reserve—the largest urban reserve in Brazil (≈3,500 hectares; >15,000 residents); the infant resided in Aldeia Bororó, the others in Aldeia Jaguapiru. Campo Grande has no suspected cases; Aquidauana is investigating another suspected chikungunya death in an Indigenous woman. From 7–17 March 2026, probable cases in MS rose 7.9% (2,446→2,639); MS leads Brazil with 90.2 probable cases per 100k (national 7.8). Brazil totals 16,558 probable cases and 10 deaths; MS accounts for about 40% of deaths. A federal task force in Dourados treated 1,156 houses and found 589 breeding sites (26% of visits), using ovitraps and health education.

articles.headline: Advierten sobre la circulación de Chikungunya en la región y su riesgo ante la llegada de Semana Santa
articles.headlineTranslated: Experts warn about the circulation of Chikungunya in the region and the risk it poses ahead of Holy Week.
articles.summary: Chikungunya circulation is a regional threat, with a large Bolivia epidemic and cases reported in Argentine provinces Jujuy, Salta, Tucumán, Formosa, and Chaco; dengue remains at low levels in Misiones, but Aedes aegypti-transmitted Chikungunya poses ongoing risk ahead of Holy Week. Misiones' vector surveillance chief Fabricio Tejerina notes no locally transmitted Chikungunya cases yet; however, cross-border movement during holidays increases importation risk. Chikungunya causes disabling joint pain; about 15–20% may develop chronic arthritis or arthralgia, lasting months to years. Paraguay experienced a severe outbreak last year with mortality around 2–3% and several pediatric deaths; prior dengue infection does not confer protection against Chikungunya. Prevention emphasizes eliminating mosquito breeding sites and personal protection (repellents, nets, insecticides). Vaccines exist for dengue; Chikungunya vaccines are in late-stage trials in Brazil; Argentina’s INMET closure is cited as a setback for science in Misiones.

articles.headline: Campo Grande registra três novas mortes por SRAG
articles.headlineTranslated: Campo Grande reports three more deaths from SARS.
articles.summary: Campo Grande, Brazil, reports three additional deaths from Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SRAG) amid the peak respiratory-virus season. Since 2026 began, the city has 310 notifications and 25 deaths. In the latest week, notified cases rose 12.7% (275→310); confirmed cases edged up (125→138); cases under investigation jumped from 31 to 50 (~61%). Deaths reached 25 (from 22); influenza and rhinovirus each caused two deaths; one death was due to Covid-19; one to other respiratory viruses; 18 deaths had no specified cause. Among confirmed infections, rhinovirus led with 73 cases; influenza and RSV each had 16; Covid-19 13; metapneumovirus 11; nine cases were other respiratory viruses. Health services saw reduced attendance (1,150→977) and urgent/emergency visits (3,531→3,281). An epidemiological alert urged health-system measures; vaccination coverage stands at 59.68%, with 381,016 doses administered (135,757 to target groups, 227,478 to the general population).

articles.headline: No Rio Grande do Sul, Ministério da Saúde amplia uso de mosquitos estéreis para controle do Aedes aegypti em território indígena
articles.headlineTranslated: In Rio Grande do Sul, the Ministry of Health expands the use of sterile mosquitoes to control Aedes aegypti in indigenous territory.
articles.summary: A Brazil-wide expansion of the sterile insect technique (SIT) using irradiation is under way in the indigenous Guarita territory, Tenente Portela, Rio Grande do Sul, with the Km10 and Linha Esperança villages. The Ministry of Health funds the approach to control Aedes aegypti, the dengue, Zika, and chikungunya vector, in areas where chemical products are restricted. The release of sterile male mosquitoes, when they mate with wild females, prevents offspring and reduces vector populations. This marks the second territory in Brazil and the world to deploy SIT by irradiation. The Guarita project builds on a year of ovitramp surveillance, health education, and community mobilization; prior deployment occurred in Cimbres, Pesqueira, Pernambuco. The initiative began March 9–11 with community engagement and the first releases; future releases will be weekly, with entomological monitoring and mechanical control of breeding sites.

articles.headline: Americana reduz em 99% os casos de dengue este ano - Novo Momento
articles.headlineTranslated: Americana reduces dengue cases by 99% this year - Novo Momento
articles.summary: Dengue in Americana, Brazil, dropped by 99% year-over-year. For the first two months of 2026, confirmed dengue cases plummeted to 32 from 2,715 in 2025, with no dengue-related deaths reported so far this year; prior Jan–Feb 2025 saw 32 deaths. Despite the sharp decline, the city maintains intensified Aedes aegypti control. The Municipal Dengue Control Program conducts daily breeding-site removals during house-to-house visits, clearing containers such as cans, bottles, tires, tarps, and drums, while residents receive prevention guidance. Additional measures include educational campaigns, larval-density assessments, targeted inspections, and a reactivated AI-assisted geospatial surveillance system to monitor cases in real time. The interdepartmental arbovirus task force meets regularly, and public messaging runs under the slogan 'Dengue will not have a place in 2026.'

articles.headline: Viruela del mono en Argentina: confirman el primer caso de la variante Clade Ib, la más agresiva y contagiosa - Somos Jujuy
articles.headlineTranslated: Monkeypox in Argentina: First Case of the Clade Ib Variant, the Most Aggressive and Contagious - Somos Jujuy
articles.summary: As of 17 March 2026, Argentina confirms its first Monkeypox case caused by the Clade Ib variant, in a 31-year-old man residing in Buenos Aires City (CABA). Diagnosis was validated by PCR and genomic sequencing in official labs. The patient exhibited fever, myalgia, lymphadenopathy, fatigue, sore throat, and vesicular skin lesions. The case follows five earlier mpox infections in 2026 caused by earlier strains; Clade Ib is described by the WHO as more severe and more transmissible. The Ministry of Health activated heightened surveillance, including isolation until crusts fall and skin heals, and contact-tracing to determine travel-related exposure or contact with travelers. Health professionals were alerted to look for individuals with multiple lesions or lesions in genital, anal, or facial areas. Transmission is mainly via direct contact with lesions, bodily fluids, or prolonged close contact (including sexual). Regional context includes Brazil and Mexico reporting this variant in 2026, reinforcing preventive measures and early medical consultation.

articles.headline: Governo do Acre confirma caso de Mpox na região de fronteira com a Bolívia - O Alto Acre
articles.headlineTranslated: Acre government confirms mpox case in the border region with Bolivia - O Alto Acre
articles.summary: On 17 March 2026, Acre state authorities confirmed a mpox (monkeypox) case in the border region with Bolivia, in Alto Acre/Brasilienza area near Cobija. The patient was under observation at the regional hospital of Alto Acre in Brasiléia. Following initial speculation about the case and rumors it was being monitored abroad, health authorities initiated contact tracing and exposure monitoring. Mpox is a viral disease transmitted through direct contact with skin lesions, bodily fluids, or contaminated materials; common symptoms include skin eruptions, fever, lymphadenopathy, body aches, and weakness, typically lasting two to four weeks. After confirmation, Brazil’s national CIEVS and the Border CIEVS activated surveillance protocols; São Paulo and Cobija health teams were mobilized to aid in tracing contacts. Sesacre reported epidemiological surveillance, Lacen, and other agencies implementing Ministry of Health measures. Brazil continues mpox surveillance in 2026, with most cases in São Paulo and no deaths reported so far.

articles.headline: Força Nacional do SUS é mobilizada após mortes por chikungunya em aldeias de MS
articles.headlineTranslated: The SUS National Force mobilized after chikungunya deaths in villages in Mato Grosso do Sul.
articles.summary: Chikungunya outbreak in Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, prompts deployment of the National SUS Force to Dourados to reinforce control in Indigenous reserve villages Aguapiru and Bororó. Three deaths confirmed: a 69-year-old woman with hypertension and diabetes; a 73-year-old man without comorbidities whose symptoms began Feb 4 and died Feb 11; and a 3-month-old infant without comorbidities. Dourados has 386 suspected and 206 confirmed chikungunya cases. The Health Ministry has been monitoring the situation and has maintained a team in the villages since last week to devise an action plan with the city and state government. In early March, ~100 health and endemic agents visited over 2,200 residences, conducting mass cleanup campaigns, installing mosquito egg traps, and spraying chemicals to control the vector. The National SUS Force is due to arrive on Thursday, March 19, 2026, to bolster efforts.

articles.headline: Por que a gripe muda de nome? Entenda o que significam Gripe, Influenza, H1N1 e H3N2 - PORTAL !YOBA
articles.headlineTranslated: Why does the flu change its name? Understand what flu, influenza, H1N1, and H3N2 mean - PORTAL !YOBA.
articles.summary: Influenza is caused by influenza A and B viruses, which mutate constantly with multiple variants circulating; H1N1 and H3N2 are subtypes of Influenza A identified by surface proteins. In Brazil during early 2026, Fiocruz InfoGripe reports 14,370 severe respiratory infections notified; 35% tested positive for any respiratory virus, with about 20% of confirmed cases due to Influenza A and about 1.7% due to Influenza B. Vaccines are updated annually, typically as trivalent or quadrivalent formulations covering two influenza A lineages and one or two influenza B lineages, and high-dose versions (e.g., Efluelda) are available for adults over 60 to boost protection. Not all respiratory illnesses are flu; other viruses (e.g., coronaviruses, RSV) can cause similar symptoms, though influenza infections more often include high fever and body aches. Vaccination, hand hygiene, and monitoring persistent symptoms remain key preventive measures during the season.

articles.headline: MG soma mais de 8 mil casos de dengue e registra seis mortes em 2026
articles.headlineTranslated: Minas Gerais records more than 8,000 dengue cases and six deaths in 2026.
articles.summary: Minas Gerais, Brazil, reports 8,144 confirmed dengue cases and six deaths in 2026, per SES-MG update on March 16, 2026. There are 26,471 probable dengue cases (all notifications excluding discarded), with 14 additional dengue deaths under investigation. For chikungunya, 2,306 confirmed cases and one death are recorded; 4,048 probable chikungunya cases, with no deaths under investigation. Zika accounts for 19 probable and 3 confirmed cases, with no deaths reported or under investigation. The epidemiological bulletin notes ongoing monitoring of all cases. Health authorities underscore prevention through eliminating mosquito breeding sites to reduce transmission of dengue, chikungunya, and Zika. The report does not specify laboratory methods beyond 'confirmed' and 'probable' designations or any imported/exported-case details.

articles.headline: Viruela del Mono: detectan el primer caso de una variante más contagiosa y severa en Argentina
articles.headlineTranslated: Monkeypox: First Case of a More Contagious and More Severe Variant Detected in Argentina.
articles.summary: Argentina confirms its first mpox case from Mpox Clade Ib, reported in BEN 799. The patient is a 31-year-old man from Buenos Aires with no travel history and is recovering after outpatient care. Mpox spreads via direct contact with lesions or mucous membranes, close contact (including sexual contact), fomites, or respiratory droplets; incubation 5–21 days (usually 6–13). Clade I is historically more severe and lethal than Clade II, with higher risk in immunosuppressed individuals and uncontrolled HIV. In 2026, six cases have been confirmed in Argentina: five in Buenos Aires City and one in Río Negro with travel to Chile. 14 Clade Ib cases have been reported in the Americas: US 9, Canada 2, Brazil 2, Mexico 1, Argentina 1; France, Portugal, Spain report community transmission. Authorities urge heightened suspicion for umbilicated lesions or proctitis, isolation until crusts fall, PPE for health workers, and 21-day follow-up with 24-hour contact tracing.

articles.headline: Mulher morre e 113 são internados após comerem pizza
articles.headlineTranslated: Woman dies and 113 are admitted to hospital after eating pizza.
articles.summary: On March 17, 2026, a 44-year-old woman, Rayssa Maritein Bezerra e Silva, died in Pombal, Paraíba's Sertão region, Brazil, with suspected food poisoning after consuming pizza at a local establishment. She had been admitted to the Regional Hospital of Pombal since March 16, after presenting diarrhea, vomiting, and abdominal pain—symptoms consistent with foodborne illness. The hospital noted rapid clinical deterioration, with the patient transferred to the Intensive Care Unit in grave condition, with signs compatible with a severe infectious process. Overall, 114 people sought medical care in the city following pizza consumption; 113 were admitted to hospital, and one fatality has been recorded. No laboratory-confirmed pathogen is reported in the available summary. Investigations into the infection source or any imported/exported cases were not detailed.

articles.headline: Prefeitura de BH identifica morcego contaminado com raiva e faz vacinação de cães e gatos na Região do Barreiro
articles.headlineTranslated: Belo Horizonte City Hall identifies a bat infected with rabies and vaccinates dogs and cats in the Barreiro Region.
articles.summary: Rabies confirmed in Belo Horizonte, Brazil: a bat found dead in the Diamante neighborhood, Barreiro region, tested positive after municipal zoonoses lab analysis. Bats are major vectors of human rabies in Brazil and the Americas. In 2024, Belo Horizonte recorded 28 positive bats; 2025, 21; 2026 currently has one confirmed case. After confirmation, the Barreiro regional zoonoses unit launched a 300-meter vaccination blockade for dogs and cats near the discovery site, alongside pet vaccinations. Residents were advised to seal gaps and avoid direct contact with bats. If exposed to a potentially rabid animal, seek immediate medical evaluation at a health center, with vaccination or rabies immunoglobulin as needed. Domestic dogs/cats involved in bites should be observed for 10 days; if illness, disappearance, or death occurs, contact zoonoses or the health center. Rabies vaccines for dogs and cats are offered year-round at five Centros de Esterilização de Cães e Gatos and the Centro de Controle de Zoonoses (CCZ); hours/addresses on the city site.

People aged 12 and up who have not yet been vaccinated or who last received a dose more than one year ago should visit a health post, bringing CPF or SUS card and the vaccination booklet. The municipality awaits new doses of the COVID-19 Baby vaccine for children six months to under five years to resume service and currently lacks the influenza vaccine, pending delivery for the next national campaign. Maintaining up-to-date vaccination is urged for individual and community protection.

articles.headline: Fumacê percorre três bairros nesta terça para conter avanço da dengue na Capital
articles.headlineTranslated: Fogging goes through three neighborhoods this Tuesday to curb the spread of dengue in the capital.
articles.summary: ULV fogging in Campo Grande targets three neighborhoods—Noroeste, Nova Lima, and Coronel Antonino—on Tuesday, 17 March 2026, from 4:00 pm to 10:00 pm. Teams from the Vectorborne Endemic Control Coordination (CCEV) under the Municipal Health Secretariat (Sesau) will spray an insecticide as a fine mist to reduce adult Aedes aegypti, the vector for dengue, Zika, and chikungunya. The fogging relies on open doors and windows to allow entry and reach into residences. Weather conditions such as rain, strong winds, or fog may delay or cancel the operation. Importantly, ULV fogging only affects adults and does not kill eggs or larvae; therefore eliminating standing water in yards, gutters, pots, and other containers remains the principal prevention measure.

articles.headline: HDT realiza conferência internacional sobre histoplasmose com participação de especialista dos Estados Unidos - Brazil Urgente
articles.headlineTranslated: HDT holds international conference on histoplasmosis with the participation of a specialist from the United States - Brazil Urgente.
articles.summary: Histoplasmosis International Conference—Diagnostic Gaps, Global Disease Burden, and the Role of Endemic Centers—will be held at Hospital Estadual de Doenças Tropicais Dr. Anuar Auad (HDT) in Goiânia, Goiás, Brazil, on March 19 at 9:30 AM. Hosted by HDT/Instituto Sócrates Guanaes (ISG), the meeting features US infectious disease specialist Nathan Bahr (University of Minnesota) and Alessandro Pasqualotto (UFCSPA), with Renata Soares as moderator. Directed at infectologists, hospital leadership, and SES-GO officials, it will discuss diagnostic challenges, the global burden of histoplasmosis, and the strategic role of endemic centers, presenting epidemiological data and plans for international multicenter research. Highlights include the HISTO-FACT study, Induction study results, and a new seven-year international protocol. Histoplasmosis is caused by Histoplasma capsulatum, linked to soil contaminated by bird or bat excreta, and is a major HIV/AIDS-related mycosis in Latin America; it remains underdiagnosed with barriers in testing access and care networks. HDT is a reference center for infectious diseases and medical mycology; ISG has managed it since 2012.

articles.headlineTranslated: Mass mobilization in Simplício Mendes intensifies the fight against dengue.
articles.summary: Last Friday, March 13, the municipality of Simplício Mendes, through the Epidemiological Surveillance Center, conducted a dengue-control mutirão across multiple city points to educate residents, inspect homes, and remove containers that can collect standing water—the primary breeding site for Aedes aegypti mosquitoes transmitting dengue. The operation reinforced everyday precautions: keep water tanks tightly closed, avoid litter, and eliminate any object that could serve as a breeding ground. The municipal cleaning team supported the effort by removing illegally discarded materials. Everaldo Melo, Dengue Surveillance Coordinator, said the mobilization is essential given that dengue cases have been notified in the municipality, and urged residents to collaborate because prevention begins at home. The Surveillance unit notes that actions will continue, but population involvement is indispensable to prevent the disease’s spread in the municipality.

Zika registers three confirmed cases and 19 probable cases, with no deaths confirmed or under investigation to date. The figures reflect surveillance data for the year to date; no imported/exported case details are provided. Ongoing monitoring continues to track arboviral threats in Minas Gerais.

articles.headline: Mpox: Saúde confirma 1º caso no Acre
articles.headlineTranslated: Mpox: Health confirms first case in Acre.
articles.summary: First mpox case confirmed in Acre, Brazil, in the municipality of Brasileia. The case is classified as imported, with exposure possibly during a trip to the state of São Paulo; symptoms began about one week after returning to the border region. Laboratory confirmation was obtained, and the patient is being monitored by Vigilância em Saúde. There is no evidence of local transmission in Acre at this time. The Secretariat activated national and border surveillance (CIEVS) and the CIEVS for Fronteira in Brasileia, with notification to health authorities in Cobija, Bolivia, and in São Paulo for contact tracing. The central laboratory (LACEN) and other institutions were mobilized, and all control, monitoring, and follow-up measures recommended by the Ministry of Health are being implemented. Active surveillance continues across Acre to ensure rapid response to any suspected mpox cases.

articles.headline: Seis anos após 1º caso, Acre soma mais de 174 mil confirmações e 2.118 mortes por Covid-19
articles.headlineTranslated: Six years after the first case, Acre has more than 174,000 confirmed cases and 2,118 deaths from COVID-19.
articles.summary: Six years after Acre, Brazil registered its first COVID-19 cases on March 17, 2020, with 174,977 confirmed infections and 2,118 deaths out of 444,878 notifications, per the Coronavírus Brasil panel. Initial cases: one from the private network and two at Rio Branco’s emergency department, days after the WHO declared the pandemic. March 20, 2020 saw closures of malls, bars, and travel restrictions; the first death occurred April 6, 2020 (79-year-old woman, UPA Second District). By July 2020, deaths reached 500. Vaccines arrived in January 2021 after Anvisa approved CoronaVac and Oxford/AstraZeneca; February 2021 triggered a red phase due to hospital risk. November 2021 introduced a vaccination passport for access to public spaces. In 2025 Acre reported 4,873 cases and 24 deaths; 2023–2025 saw most cases in ages 40–49, with 62.8% female. In Jan–Mar 2026, 15 new cases were recorded.

articles.headline: Confirman el primer caso de una persona infectada por una variante más contagiosa y severa de viruela del mono
articles.headlineTranslated: First Case of a Person Infected with a More Contagious and Severe Variant of Monkeypox Confirmed
articles.summary: As of 17 March 2026, Monkeypox in Argentina marks the first confirmed case of clade Ib, the more transmissible and severe variant, in a 31-year-old man resident of Buenos Aires. He contracted locally, with no travel history, while previous 2026 cases (five total) were clade II (four in the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires, one in Río Negro). The clade Ib arrival changes the local epidemiology, as national health bulletin notes higher transmission and potential for complications, prompting reinforced surveillance and response protocols. Internationally, clade Ib has been detected in the United States, Canada, Brazil, and Mexico, with community transmission in France, Spain, and Portugal. Argentina activated measures to curb spread: heightened clinical suspicion for compatible symptoms (skin lesions, lymphadenopathy, extreme fatigue), case isolation until lesions resolve, and 24-hour contact tracing with three weeks of follow-up. Early detection remains critical to limit outbreaks.

articles.headline: Temporada de gripe chega mais cedo ao Brasil e covid tem leve alta, alerta Fiocruz
articles.headlineTranslated: Flu season arrives earlier in Brazil and COVID-19 shows a slight uptick, Fiocruz warns.
articles.summary: Early influenza season arrives in Brazil, driving SRAG (Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome) hospitalizations linked to rhinovirus, RSV, and influenza A. Tocantins shows no uptick; influenza A is contributing to SRAG in Rio de Janeiro, Mato Grosso, Amapá, Pará and Rondônia, while the Northeast sees increases except in Alagoas and Sergipe. In São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, COVID-19 cases rise slightly but have not increased hospitalizations. For 2026, InfoGripe reports 16,882 SRAG cases with 6,064 laboratory-confirmed; rhinovirus (40.8%), influenza A (20.8%), COVID-19 (15.8%), and RSV (13.5%) are the most frequent etiologies. Vaccination efforts: free influenza vaccines for vulnerable groups, with about 6.9 million doses delivered by Instituto Butantan; flu vaccination expected to start by month’s end. An RSV vaccine is available on SUS for pregnant women from 28 weeks, protecting newborns. RSV remains linked to severe disease in under-2s across Acre, Amazonas, Pará, Rondônia, Mato Grosso, Goiás, Paraíba, Sergipe; RSV causes ~80% of bronchiolitis and ~60% of pneumonia in this age group, with ~20,000 infants under 1 year hospitalized annually and higher mortality in prematurity. Echoed guidance: reduce contact, mask when out, and practice hand hygiene.

articles.headlineTranslated: Perform laboratory diagnosis (molecular, serological, and confirmatory) for HIV, HTLV, HPV, and clinically important respiratory viruses.
articles.summary: Laboratory diagnostic services cover HIV-1/2, HTLV-1/2, Human Papillomavirus (HPV), SARS-CoV-2, Influenza, and other clinically important respiratory viruses, employing molecular, serological, and confirmatory methods tailored to the agent and testing purpose. Analyses use clinical specimens such as whole blood, serum or plasma, respiratory secretions, and cervical material, and apply RT-qPCR, real-time PCR, ELISA/EIA, immunoblot, and Western blot. These assays enable detection, differentiation, and confirmation of viral agents and can be used for initial diagnosis, confirmation of screening test results, infection monitoring, and, when applicable, viral load quantification and genotyping.

articles.headline: Fiebre Amarilla, viejo enemigo cercano
articles.headlineTranslated: Yellow fever, an old, close enemy.
articles.summary: Yellow fever re-emerged in Venezuela with 36 cases and 20 deaths (2025–early 2026); case fatality rate >55%, mainly adults 10–49. Barinas accounted for about one third of cases and seven deaths, with spread along a jungle–agricultural corridor to Apure, Portuguesa, Guárico, Lara, and Táchira, signaling transboundary risk. Colombia reported imported cases from Apure and Amazonas, indicating active transmission Venezuela had not officially reported. Across South America, January–April 2025 registered 301 cases and 124 deaths (CFR 41.1%); Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia and Peru together had 289 cases and 115 deaths. Apparent CFR >40% in several countries suggests substantial underreporting. Four drivers shape this re-emergence: deforestation and agricultural expansion bringing Haemagogus and Sabethes mosquitoes; climate change lengthening rainy seasons and boosting vectors; migration and porous borders enabling silent spread; institutional weakness and conflict hindering vaccination and surveillance. Calls for One Health and dynamic vaccination models; risk projections extend to Mexico and other regions.

articles.summary: Ubatuba, Brazil, reports 723 dengue cases in 2026 through the latest update, with 291 lab-confirmed or clinically-epidemiologically confirmed cases in residents and 25 imported; 32 dengue cases remain under investigation and 3 have been discarded. No dengue deaths have occurred. Chikungunya has 18 confirmed cases this year, among 167 suspected (83 discarded, 66 awaiting results). No Zika or yellow fever cases are confirmed in 2026. Oropouche fever has 3 suspected discarded cases and 4 under investigation. January: 348 dengue cases; February: 318; March: 57 so far. Leading dengue neighborhoods are Centro (23), Estufa II (20) and Ipiranguinha (20), followed by Sertão da Quina (11) and Perequê-Açu (10). The outbreak is widespread across the municipality. The nine confirmed cases involved patients hospitalized for more than seven days before the contingency plan to curb the outbreak was implemented; laboratory confirmation occurred before isolating patients and transferring others to the contingency ICU. Infected patients are isolated in a dedicated space with a dedicated team; other patients were moved to contingency ICU beds. Enhanced cleaning, hand hygiene, terminal cleanings, staff training, and routing of new ICU cases via the municipal central and SAMU to Hospital Ouro Verde or other units are in place, ongoing until stabilization.

articles.summary: Argentina reports its first case of the severe monkeypox clade Ib in an ongoing international expansion. As of 2026-03-17, 14 cases in the Americas are tallied: 9 in the United States, 2 in Canada, 2 in Brazil, 1 in Mexico, and 1 in Argentina; European countries Spain, France and Portugal confirm community transmission. Monkeypox is caused by an Orthopoxvirus and spreads mainly through direct contact with skin or mucosal lesions, and by close sexual contact, contaminated objects, respiratory droplets in prolonged proximity, and, in some regions, animal contact. Incubation ranges 5-21 days (commonly 6-13). Early symptoms include fever, headache, myalgias, lymphadenopathy, and fatigue, followed by skin lesions, often on the genital, anal, facial regions or limbs. Health authorities urge isolation of infected individuals until lesion healing, strengthened contact tracing, and strict PPE use in healthcare settings, with early case detection to contain spread.

articles.headline: Fórum Estadual de Influenza Aviária reúne setor avícola para discutir prevenção e biosseguridade no RS | Agrimidia
articles.headlineTranslated: State Avian Influenza Forum brings together the poultry sector to discuss prevention and biosecurity in Rio Grande do Sul | Agrimidia
articles.summary: March 17, 2026 — The second State Avian Influenza Forum will be held in Montenegro, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, gathering leaders, technicians, and poultry producers to discuss prevention and response for avian influenza. At Teatro Roberto Atayde Cardona, Vale do Caí, it starts at 1:30 PM and will be livestreamed on the YouTube channel of the State Secretariat of Agriculture, Livestock, Sustainable Production and Irrigation. Organized by the Department of Animal Health Surveillance and Sanitary Defense, in partnership with the Gaúcha Poultry Association and the Fund for Development and Sanitary Defense of Animals, it features talks and panels. Topics cover the global and national avian influenza scenario and recurring biosafety lapses in farms, with a public-private panel addressing the current situation, sanitary challenges, and contingency strategies. Emphasis on biosafety as the tool to prevent virus introduction and spread in commercial poultry amid global attention to avian influenza.

articles.summary: Mpox (monkeypox) in Espírito Santo, Brazil: as of March 17, 2026, the state confirms its third case in 2026. The latest patient is a man from Cachoeiro de Itapemirim in the southern region; the first case was Colatina and the second in Serra. A total of 50 suspected cases have been notified: 3 confirmed, 2 under analysis, and 42 discarded. Mpox is caused by MPXV, an Orthopoxvirus; though zoonotic, current transmission is primarily human-to-human, via direct contact with skin lesions, bodily fluids, prolonged close respiratory contact, or contaminated objects. Symptoms typically appear 3–16 days post-exposure (up to 21 days) and include skin eruptions, fever, lymphadenopathy, headache, myalgia, chills, and weakness; lesions progress from macules to vesicles to crusts and heal. Diagnosis is laboratory-based from lesion material; there is no widely available specific treatment. Vaccination targets high-risk groups, including immunosuppressed HIV patients, certain lab workers, and close contacts after evaluation.

Prevention: immediate isolation on lesions, urgent medical consultation, avoid contact with symptomatic individuals, and avoid sharing personal items.

Symptoms: high fever, severe myalgias, back pain, headache, extreme fatigue; lymphadenopathy; rash starting on the face and spreading to the body, including genital and anal regions. Prevention: immediate isolation on lesions, urgent medical consultation, avoid contact with symptomatic individuals, and avoid sharing personal items.

articles.headline: Detectaron el primer caso de viruela del mono de mayor severidad en Argentina
articles.headlineTranslated: First case of the most severe monkeypox detected in Argentina.
articles.summary: Argentina reports its first mpox case caused by clade Ib in 2026, adding to five prior clade II cases (four in Buenos Aires City, one in Río Negro). Health authorities warn clade Ib is more severe and contagious and urge strengthened surveillance. Through 2026, 14 clade Ib cases have been confirmed in the Americas (USA 9, Canada 2, Brazil 2, Mexico 1) with community transmission in Europe (France, Portugal, Spain). Clinicians should heighten mpox suspicion in patients with umbilicated lesions, proctitis, lymphadenopathy, fatigue, or sore throat, and assess travel or contact history. Infected patients should be isolated until crusts shed and new skin forms; PPE for health workers; contact tracing within 24 hours and a 21-day follow-up. The Buenos Aires case involves a 31-year-old man with symptom onset Feb 24; no travel in 21 days but multiple new sexual partners. PCR confirmed clade Ib on Mar 10 from vesicular content; no new suspected cases yet; epidemiological investigation ongoing. Transmission is via direct contact with lesions or mucosa, contaminated objects, or close respiratory droplets; incubation 5–21 days (usually 6–13).

Clade Ib is more transmissible and potentially more severe than previous lineages, and its international spread in 2026 includes the United States, Canada, Brazil, and Mexico, with community transmission in France, Portugal, and Spain. Argentina previously reported only clade II infections; five mpox cases so far in 2026, four in Buenos Aires and one in Río Negro. The Ib sublineage originated in Central Africa and spread globally, though there is no evidence of higher mortality outside endemic regions. Transmission occurs via direct contact with lesions or mucous membranes, sexual contact, contaminated objects, and possibly short-range respiratory exposure. Symptoms include fever, headache, myalgias, lymphadenopathy, fatigue, followed by skin lesions. Argentina’s Health Ministry urges strengthened surveillance, rapid case identification, contact tracing, isolation until lesions heal, and PPE for health workers.

articles.headline: Botucatu tem 41 espécies de morcegos catalogadas; caso de raiva acende alerta e reforça orientações | Jornal Acontece Botucatu
articles.headlineTranslated: Botucatu has 41 bat species cataloged; a rabies case raises an alert and reinforces guidelines | Jornal Acontece Botucatu
articles.summary: Rabies case confirmed in a bat found in a property in Vila São Lúcio, Botucatu. The specimen is the insectivorous Myotis nigricans, one of 41 bat species cataloged in the Botucatu area; Brazil has about 180 bat species, compared with roughly 45 in the United States. The positive rabies case highlights the risk that bats can harbor the virus, though bats provide ecological benefits such as insect control and pollination. Health authorities advise the public not to touch fallen or unusual bats; isolate the site, avoid contact with dogs and cats, and promptly contact Vigilância Ambiental em Saúde (VAS) at (14) 3811-1609 for safe rescue. Vaccination supplies are prioritized for animals with exposure; routine vaccination for dogs and cats will resume when the supply normalizes. VAS operations: weekdays 7:30–17:00; outside hours call 153 (Municipal Civil Guard).

articles.headline: Covid-19 ainda registra casos graves, mas permanece em queda no RS após seis anos da pandemia
articles.headlineTranslated: COVID-19 still records severe cases, but remains in decline in Rio Grande do Sul after six years of the pandemic.
articles.summary: Six years after COVID-19 arrived in Rio Grande do Sul, SRAG activity remains but with a downward trend. In 2026, RS recorded 1,263 SRAG hospitalizations, including 192 for COVID-19 and 55 for influenza; 709 had no identified agent. There were 93 SRAG deaths, including 29 linked to COVID-19. In Porto Alegre, 117 SRAG hospitalizations this year, 24 due to COVID-19; 13 SRAG deaths, 5 COVID-19. Health authorities say the pattern matches the seasonal cycle, with respiratory illnesses rising from April and peaking June–August. City bed occupancy reached 99% by Monday, with 4,384 inpatients across 4,420 beds. COVID-19 circulates endemically, mainly Omicron lineages, with higher transmission but lower severity in a highly vaccinated population. Flu vaccination begins March 28; COVID-19 vaccines remain for priority groups; boosters are advised due to waning immunity.

articles.headline: Estes 11 erros aumentam o risco de infecções alimentares, aponta estudo
articles.headlineTranslated: These 11 mistakes increase the risk of foodborne infections, according to a study.
articles.summary: As of 2026-03-17, 11 common kitchen practices increase the risk of foodborne infections, according to a University of São Paulo (USP) study published in Food and Humanity. In Brazil, about 5,000 people were surveyed online on food shopping, storage, and handling. Key findings show only 38% properly sanitize vegetables; 17% consume raw or undercooked eggs; and 11.2% delay refrigerating leftovers for more than two hours. These behaviors elevate the risk of foodborne diseases (DTAs), which the World Health Organization estimates affect about 600 million people globally each year. Common symptoms include vomiting, diarrhea, nausea, abdominal pain, and dehydration. The main bacterial culprits identified are Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, and Salmonella. The study highlights that routine domestic practices may significantly raise infection risk in Brazil, underscoring the need for proper washing, cooking, and timely storage.

articles.headline: Eu vi a morte ao meu lado", diz colunista social do Acre ao relembrar pandemia de Covid-19
articles.headlineTranslated: "I saw death by my side," says the Acre-based social columnist as they recall the COVID-19 pandemic.
articles.summary: COVID-19 struck Acre, Brazil, with the first recorded case on 17 March 2020. By September 2025, Acre had 174,977 cases and 2,118 deaths. Social columnist Vagno Di Paula recalls battling the disease after losing his sense of taste; he spent about 22 days hospitalized, including periods in intensive care, without vaccine availability at the time. With obesity and hypertension, he feared for his life as he experienced non-invasive ventilation and oxygen masking, enduring claustrophobia and anxiety; he recalls near intubation and describes staff as ‘angels’ who monitored his oxygen saturation. He attributes a spiritual moment during sedation to Jesus bringing him back, with discharge on 24 December 2020. Post-recovery he reports tachycardia, leg pain, anxiety, and claustrophobia, requiring physiotherapy; the ordeal altered his outlook, valuing life and loved ones.

articles.headline: Ceará confirma segundo caso do mpox em 2026, de acordo com a plataforma IntegraSUS - Contexto Notícias
articles.headlineTranslated: Ceará confirms second mpox case in 2026, according to the IntegraSUS platform - Contexto Notícias.
articles.summary: As of 17 March 2026, Ceará confirms its second mpox case in 2026, with eight additional suspected cases under investigation per IntegraSUS. The first case in 2026 was confirmed on 9 March in Fortaleza; the city for the second patient is not disclosed. Nationally, Brazil has 149 confirmed mpox cases and 539 suspected, with the Southeast region accounting for 122 confirmations. Mpox is caused by mpox virus (MPXV), a zoonotic Orthopoxvirus in the Poxviridae family. Transmission occurs via contact with infected people, contaminated objects, and infected wildlife. There is no specific antiviral; treatment is supportive and symptomatic. In Ceará last year, 69 notifications were recorded, including 13 confirmed and 56 discarded after investigation. Nationally, CNIESV data indicate 140 confirmed mpox cases in 2026 and 539 suspected notifications.

articles.headline: Há 6 anos, Acre confirmava 3 primeiros casos de Covid-19 e decretava situação de emergência
articles.headlineTranslated: Six years ago, Acre confirmed the first three cases of COVID-19 and declared a state of emergency.
articles.summary: COVID-19 in Acre, Brazil: On March 17, 2020, Sesacre declared a 30-day state of emergency after confirming the first three SARS-CoV-2 cases in Rio Branco (two at the Pronto-Socorro and one in a private network). By March 20, the state closed malls, bars, restaurants and halted intercity travel. The first death occurred on April 6 (a 79-year-old woman); by April 17 there were 135 infections and five deaths. Acre reached 500 deaths by July 2020. Vaccination began January 2021 after Anvisa approved CoronaVac and AstraZeneca; the first vaccinees were an 85-year-old resident and a 66-year-old nurse. Vaccination coverage expanded through 2021–22, with a vaccination passport in Nov 2021 and Expoacre in 2022 requiring it; by May 2022, 71.21% had first dose. In 2023, bivalent Pfizer doses started (over 67,000 doses). In 2026, 15 cases were recorded Jan 1–Mar 7 (SE 09); since 2020, total confirmed cases are listed as 176.24.

articles.headline: Quase 100 pessoas passam mal após comer em pizzaria na Paraíba
articles.headlineTranslated: Nearly 100 people fall ill after eating at a pizzeria in Paraíba.
articles.summary: An outbreak of food poisoning linked to a pizzeria in Pombal, Paraíba, Brazil sickened at least 84 people, with authorities indicating the figure is approaching 100. Since Sunday night, 15 March, 33 patients were treated at the local Emergency Care Unit (UPA) and 51 at the regional hospital. The municipality closed the establishment on Monday, 16 March, following a technical inspection and health notifications. Reported symptoms include severe abdominal pain, vomiting, nausea, and malaise. The illness is classified as food poisoning (intoxicação alimentar). The Brazilian Ministry of Health notes that food poisoning can be caused by bacteria and their toxins, viruses, intestinal parasites, or chemical substances. Investigations are underway to identify the source and guide appropriate public health actions.

articles.headline: Detectan en Argentina el primer caso de la viruela del mono más agresiva: cómo prevenirla
articles.headlineTranslated: First Case of the More Aggressive Monkeypox Detected in Argentina: How to Prevent It
articles.summary: Argentina reports its first Mpox case of clade Ib, a more contagious and potentially more severe variant, in a 31-year-old man from Buenos Aires. He had no recent international travel, presented with rash, fever, pain and lymphadenopathy, and recovered after ambulatory care. Clade Ib is spreading globally in 2026, with cases in the United States, Canada, Brazil and Mexico, and community transmission in France, Portugal and Spain; Argentina had five clade II infections earlier in 2026 (four in Buenos Aires City, one in Río Negro). Mpox is an Orthopoxvirus transmitted by direct contact with skin lesions or mucous membranes, close sexual contact, contaminated objects, and, with prolonged exposure, short-range respiratory spread. Symptoms include fever, headache, myalgia, lymphadenopathy, fatigue, followed by skin lesions; illness often resolves in 14–21 days. Authorities urge enhanced surveillance, rapid detection, contact tracing, and isolation until lesions crust; PCR/sequencing confirmed clade Ib; no secondary cases detected yet.

articles.headlineTranslated: They confirmed the first case of the most contagious variant of monkeypox in Argentina: what are its symptoms.
articles.summary: Clade Ib, a newly identified mpox (monkeypox) variant detected in late 2023 in the Democratic Republic of Congo, shows higher transmissibility and virulence than prior strains. Authorities warn it can spread rapidly through sexual and community contact. In 2026, Argentina reported five mpox cases, all linked to Clade II, amid a shifting landscape as Clade Ib expands regionally. Reports of Clade Ib infections have surfaced in the United States, Canada, Brazil, and Mexico, with Argentina also affected; community transmission has been documented in France, Portugal, and Spain. Transmission occurs mainly via direct contact with skin or mucosal lesions in close or sexual contact; contaminated objects and prolonged exposure to respiratory secretions can also spread the virus. Incubation is 5–21 days, and illness is typically self-limited over 2–3 weeks. Early symptoms include fever, headache, muscle pains, swollen lymph nodes, fatigue, and sore throat, followed by lesions on the genital, anal, face, or limbs.

articles.headline: Acre confirma primeiro caso de Mpox no interior e autoridades inicia rastreamento de contatos
articles.headlineTranslated: Acre confirms first Mpox case in the interior and authorities begin contact tracing.
articles.summary: Mpox (monkeypox) confirmed in Acre's interior, Brazil. Acre's Health Secretariat (Sesacre) reports the first interior case; the patient was treated at Hospital Geral de Brasiléia in Vale do Alto Acre. The patient is a medical student studying in Cobija, Bolivia (Pando Department), who had recently been in São Paulo, Brazil. The patient tested positive and is in isolation; authorities have begun identifying and monitoring contacts. Mpox transmission occurs through direct contact with infected individuals, skin lesions, respiratory secretions, or contaminated objects, via close or intimate contact. Common symptoms include fever, headache, muscle pains, fatigue, lymphadenopathy, and skin or mucosal eruptions. Sesacre urges anyone with suspected symptoms to seek medical care and to avoid physical contact or sharing personal items while the disease is suspected.

articles.headline: ¿Va a viajar? Bogotá centraliza vacunas de sarampión en el Aeropuerto y Terminales ante falta de dosis
articles.headlineTranslated: Are you traveling? Bogotá centralizes measles vaccines at the airport and terminals due to a shortage of doses.
articles.summary: Bogotá centralizes measles-rubella vaccination at El Dorado International Airport and at Salitre and Satélite del Sur transport terminals due to a dose shortage, prioritizing international travelers and ring vaccination. The Expanded Immunization Program currently has about 5,000 doses available, insufficient for over 200 vaccination points; demand surged from 7,995 doses in Q1 2025 to 22,064 by March 2026 (275% increase). The city reports three imported measles cases and maintains an epidemiological alert while awaiting vaccine replenishment from the Ministry of Health. A request for 50,000 additional doses was submitted on February 20, 2026 but remains unassigned. Travelers are advised to be vaccinated at least 15 days before departure. Families should verify children’s vaccination cards and ensure two doses of the measles-rubella (MMR) vaccine, with Bogotá confirming adequate MMR stock across more than 200 points until supplies normalize.

articles.headline: MG tem 6 mortes por dengue e mais de 8 mil casos confirmados; há uma morte por chikungunya e cerca de 2 mil casos da doença
articles.headlineTranslated: Minas Gerais has six dengue-related deaths and more than 8,000 confirmed cases; there is one chikungunya-related death and about 2,000 chikungunya cases.
articles.summary: Minas Gerais, Brazil, reports ongoing dengue, chikungunya, and Zika activity as of March 16–17, 2026. The state health secretariat (SES) urges intensified prevention and control of Aedes aegypti, the vector for all three diseases. Dengue: 8,144 laboratory-confirmed cases and six deaths in 2026, with 14 dengue deaths under investigation; probable dengue cases stand at 26,471. Chikungunya: 2,306 confirmed cases and one confirmed death, with one death under investigation; probable chikungunya cases total 4,048. Zika: 3 confirmed cases and 19 probable, with no deaths reported. A dengue vaccine from Butantan is highlighted, maintaining protection for five years and reducing severe cases. The report also notes ongoing epidemiological updates and current transmission patterns, underscoring the importance of vector-control measures and continued surveillance.

articles.headline: Chile refuerza vacunación contra la influenza ante circulación de una nueva variante
articles.headlineTranslated: Chile steps up influenza vaccination amid circulation of a new variant.
articles.summary: Chile intensifies influenza vaccination as an A(H3N2) variant circulates regionally. The campaign targets 85% coverage among high-risk groups, including health and education workers, older adults, people with chronic diseases, pregnant individuals, lactating women, and schoolchildren. For the second year, Chile’s Health Ministry advanced the vaccination program to reduce infections and complications before winter. Authorities confirm A(H3N2) circulation in Chile and neighboring Peru, Bolivia, Paraguay, and Brazil, a strain linked to higher transmissibility and more severe outcomes in the elderly. About 1,200 vaccination points operate nationwide. Preventive measures are reinforced: frequent handwashing, covering coughs or sneezes, staying home with symptoms, and seeking urgent care for severe cases.

articles.headline: 24 organizaciones alertan sobre el "inicio" de epidemia de fiebre amarilla y piden transparencia
articles.headlineTranslated: 24 organizations warn about the "start" of a yellow fever epidemic and call for transparency.
articles.summary: Twenty-four organizations, led by the National Academy of Medicine and the NGO Provea, warn of the start of a yellow fever epidemic in Venezuela and urge immediate government action. They criticize opacity, noting first cases were detected in June 2025 but eight months passed before acknowledgment. In a letter to the Health Ministry and Parliament, experts urge release of the 2024–2026 epidemiological bulletins to restore transparency and evidence-based decisions. Health Minister Nuramy Gutiérrez confirmed deaths from the disease last year, while official tallies show seven confirmed cases in 2026; Isabel Iturria had cited 36 infections since mid-2025. The government declared an epidemiological alert aiming for 95% vaccination coverage, reporting 49,000 recently immunized, adding to about three million vaccinated over the past decade, with donations from India, Russia and Brazil. Despite efforts, the Expanded Immunization Program has not met targets, underscoring the need to strengthen health systems to reach all Venezuelans.

articles.headline: Liderança de terreiro de Magé participa de Conferência sobre Hanseníase
articles.headlineTranslated: Leadership of Magé's terreiro participates in a conference on Hansen's disease.
articles.summary: Hansen's disease (leprosy) is highlighted in Magé, Brazil, as religious leadership from a terreiro, Pai Paulo de Ogun, participates in Brazil's National High-Level Conference on Hansen's Disease. The event links public health policy with human rights and traditional knowledge, emphasizing the strategic role of terreiro communities in health promotion, equity, and addressing long-standing inequalities affecting Black populations and vulnerable territories. By engaging alongside public managers, international bodies, scientific experts, and social movements, the participation broadens understanding of Hansen's disease beyond a purely biomedical frame, underscoring that the illness is deeply influenced by social, cultural, and territorial determinants that impact early diagnosis, access to treatment, and stigma reduction. The involvement of religious and community leaders in policy discussions reinforces social oversight and participatory approaches toward more inclusive, effective disease responses. Pai Paulo reaffirmed a commitment to a Brazil free of Hansen's disease, without stigma, guided by social justice and health equity.

articles.headline: Gripe aviária é tema de evento em Montenegro nesta terça-feira - Jornal O Sul
articles.headlineTranslated: Bird flu is the topic of an event in Montenegro this Tuesday - Jornal O Sul
articles.summary: Bird flu (Avian Influenza) headlines the second Rio Grande do Sul State Avian Influenza Forum in Montenegro, Vale do Caí, RS, at Teatro Roberto Atayde Cardona on Tuesday, March 17, 2026, from 13:30. Organized by Seapi’s Department of Vigilance and Sanitary Defense of Animals (DDA) with Asgav and Fundesa, the event aims to share prevention and response strategies after a recently identified focus in Gaucho properties. The program includes 14:00 a session on the Avian Influenza scenario in Brazil and worldwide (Daniela Pacheco Lacerda, MAPA), 14:30 biosafety basics (Paulo Raffi), and a 15:00 panel on the country’s Avian Influenza situation with Daniela Pacheco Lacerda, Fernanda Pinto Piccinini (MBRF), Fernando Groff (DDA), José Eduardo dos Santos (Asgav), João Paulo Zuffo (Seara Alimentos) and Paulo Raffi, followed by closing at 15:40. Live stream via Seapi YouTube; details at agricultura.rs.gov.br.
